THIS month’s extended international break has seen a number of the Premier League’s biggest stars depart to represent their countries.

But not all of those asked were able to answer their call-ups, with injuries and concerns over club form keeping a number of major stars at home.



So many will not be making the journey in fact that you can create a title-challenging XI of Prem players who had to turn down the chance to play for their national sides over the coming weeks.

Karl Darlow might not have made any headlines in goal for Manchester United this season, but he is a solid Premier League-level stopper kicking off the line-up.



He was handed a competitive Red Devils debut in the Carabao Cup last week – in which he conceded three against Brighton – and has now had to step back from the Wales squad due to an unspecified knock.

He plays behind a back three featuring Arsenal star Piero Hincapie marshalling the penalty area.



The Ecuadorian has been struggling with a groin strain of late, and though he has featured intermittently off the bench for the Gunners this season, new Ecuador boss Marcelo Gallardo confirmed he would be staying in North London to continue his recovery rather than joining up with his national side.

Hincapie is flanked on either side by Tino Livramento and Pedro Porro, with the latter unfortunate to pick up a hamstring injury in the opening 20 minutes of Spurs’ clash with Aston Villa in his final game before joining up with Spain.

Livramento made Thomas Tuchel‘s initial England squad despite playing less than 90 minutes of football for Newcastle so far this season, and it was not all that surprising to see him pull out to continue working on his recovery.

He joined a number of other stars leaving the England squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia – with a potential midfield duo of Kobbie Mainoo and Declan Rice also turning down the call.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The pair recused themselves as a result of unspecified injuries and concerns over playing load, with Mainoo now forced to wait until the next international break to try and prove himself under Tuchel.

Both Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford also had to withdraw, bringing the total tally of England stars to step away from Tuchel’s original squad to five.

Rashford has been managing a hip injury and limped off the field in his most recent United outing, while Palmer is making sure he does not aggravate a muscular injury.

Spurs star Kudus completes a world-class midfield, after he chose not to join up with his Ghana team-mates for Afcon qualifiers in order to focus on regaining full fitness at club level.

Sports.title: BBC Sport ‘to AXE top journalist jobs and bulletins’ in brutal cost-cutting drive
Sports.content:
Next

BBC has announced more staff redundancies as lunchtime and overnight sports bulletins are set to be cut, it is reported.

This comes as part of major money-saving measures recently brought in by the news corporation.

Staff have been informed that the sports bulletins, which run on BBC’s 24-hour News channel, will no longer be aired, according to The Times.



As a result, around seven sports journalists’ jobs – including four senior roles – will be axed.



Some staff were told of the decision this morning, after the number of employees who requested voluntary redundancy was reportedly too low, leading to compulsory cuts.

Alex Kay-Jelski, the BBC’s Director of Sport, is also due to address employees at the news corporation’s Salford headquarters in the early afternoon.

This comes as the BBC has lost a number of live coverage events over the past 10 years, including Formula 1, England’s Six Nations matches and the Open.



Sky Sports now holds the highest number of live sports broadcasting rights in the UK, with TNT Sports (formerly BT Sport) following closely behind.

Despite this, Kay-Jelski said back in February that the broadcaster would remain “relevant” even if it lacked many of the rights to live sports events.

At the time, he said: “You can still be relevant, you can still matter if you don’t show the sport. No-one out there can show it all.

“So, you just have to make sure you’re in the conversation of the things that matter.”



The Times added there had been talk of a possible strike ballot as a result of the redundancies.

In June, the BBC announced 550 roles would be axed across News, Nations and Content divisions by the start of next year.

It added that further savings across all divisions – including corporate divisions – will be laid out in the coming months, with around 700 roles expected to close.

A total of 2,000 jobs are expected to be lost across the company.

This comes as part of the broadcaster’s intention to make £500million of savings over the next three years, which includes a reduction in hours of programmes, radio stations and genres.



The BBC has been approached for comment.

REAL MADRID icon David Alaba is moving to Italy to sign for Udinese as a free agent.

Alaba, 34, left Real in July following five glittering years that saw him winning two LaLiga titles, the Copa Del Rey and two Champions League honours.

3 Credit: Getty Images – Getty

3 Credit: Getty Images – Getty



That was after another 11 stunning years with Bayern Munich where he won ten Bundesliga titles, six German Cups and another two Champions League trophies.

According to transfer insider Fabrizio Romano, Udinese have reached a verbal agreement with the versatile defender.



The Austria international has been described as a “dream signing” for the Serie A outfit.

However, “formal steps” are still needed to iron out the final details of that deal.

Alaba amassed a total of five goals and nine assists in 132 appearances with Real.

The centre-back, who can also play at full-back, suffered a raft of muscle injuries during his time in Madrid which limited his game time.

The Austrian also dealt with injuries during his time with Bayern, where he registered 33 goals and 55 assists in 431 appearances.

Udinese are currently 13th in the Serie A table after a poor start that saw them losing three of their first five matches, of which they only won one.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Alaba will be linking up with the likes of Nicolo Zaniolo, Christian Kabasele and Scotland international Lennon Miller.

This comes after a busy 2026 World Cup as he played in every game for Austria until their elimination in the last 32 from eventual champions Spain.

That took Alaba‘s total tally to 15 goals in 117 caps for his national team.

Sports.title: 500 days of hell: Luckless Dejan Kulusevski ace set for emotional Tottenham return as De Zerbi hails ‘new signing’
Sports.content:
Next

ANGE POSTECOGLOU infamously labelled Dejan Kulusevki’s injury “just a knock” when the Swede first suffered it back on May 11, 2025.

Yet today Kulusevski clocks up 500 DAYS on the sidelines since that fateful, freak crock just 19 minutes into a 2-0 home defeat to Crystal Palace.



The pain of missing out has been utter hell for the model pro, whose friends describe him as a football obsessive.

But the good news is there finally could be some light at the end of the tunnel for the luckless playmaker.



Kulusevski’s injury was so long ago Marc Guehi was still playing for Palace and it was in an innocuous challenge with the England defender that the Spurs star damaged his kneecap.

Then boss Postecoglou waved away fears it would be yet another major injury to one of his stars… but it developed into the worst of the lot.

Kulusevski underwent patella surgery in the same month and stories emerged in August that he would be out until the end of 2025 at least.

But a return in the New Year ended up being a wild overestimate as Kulusevski’s injury proved more complicated than initially hoped.

He had to go under the knife again in March to clear up any lingering issues that were preventing a full recovery.

Kulusevski, a devout Christian, really believed he would be back in time to play at Sweden’s second World Cup in 20 years this summer but it was not to be.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Yet his faith was rewarded when on August 31 he returned at long last to full-team training at Spurs following 477 days out injured.

Such a prolonged spell without action meant it was always going to be a number of weeks from that point before he played competitively again, though.

The physical toll of team training meant that after a few days he had to go back to individual work for a period.

Boss Roberto De Zerbi described it as a “small, small problem” and it is understood that it was nothing unexpected given his time in the treatment room.

Though it did kibosh any hopes Sweden boss Graham Potter had of having “world class” Kulusevski with his squad on international duty this month.



Now the interminable wait appears to be almost over.

There is genuine hope from the player that after the international break, he will soon be included in one of De Zerbi’s matchday squads.

It could even be as soon as on October 10 when Spurs go to Old Trafford, the venue for perhaps Kulusevski’s most impressive Tottenham display during the 3-0 win there in September 2024.



But if it is not at Manchester United, it is currently anticipated it will likely be one of three or four games following it, barring any setbacks.

Kulusevski’s return, whenever it finally takes place, should bring a smile to all football fans regardless of their loyalties.

He is known and respected not only for his talent and his work-rate, but is also a football nut who is obsessed with honing his craft.

It is why he is a regular reader of books that focus on mentality and self-improvement, while he is also a keen meditator.

Both of these passions have been indulged more than normal over the last 18 months to help Kulusevski in his recovery.



Like the other Spurs players not away with their countries during this international break, he has been given a week off by De Zerbi before a fortnight of training which commences the start of next week.

De Zerbi feels the 26-year-old can be a “new signing” when he returns – one that Spurs really could do with after their shocking start to the season.

The Italian knows he must manage Kulusevski carefully but is delighted at the winger’s progress for one of the feel-good stories of the season.

Speaking in August, De Zerbi said: “It’s great watching him during the season and also because he deserves it because he suffered too much for his career for his age, for his level of human. I’m not speaking of him as a player but as a human.”

Postecoglou once famously quipped, when talking about injuries as Spurs boss, that every time he saw “light at the end of the tunnel, it turned out to be an oncoming train”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kulusevski will know exactly what his old gaffer meant given his hellish ride and will have learned long ago in his recovery not to get ahead of himself.



Yet now, after almost a year and a half, Kulusevski looks genuinely on track for his long-awaited comeback.

Sports.title: 0.3%-owned Johan Manzambi can be difference-maker for Dream Team bosses after international break
Sports.content:
Next

DREAM TEAM managers were forced to wait for a proper look at Johan Manzambi (£3.8m).

And his first start for Aston Villa did not disappoint.

The 20-year-old was one of the World Cup’s most eye-catching performers before a knee injury ruled him out before the round of 32.



The Swizterland starlet scored three goals and provided two assists in North America, averaging a goal involvement every 40 minutes!



Unfortunately, the same injury meant Manzambi was unavailable for the Villains’ first four games of this season following his transfer from Freiburg.

Unai Emery eased him into action in Gameweek 4 with substitute cameos against Nottingham Forest and Coventry but it wasn’t until Gameweek 5’s trip to Tottenham that the attack-minded midfielder was deemed ready to start.

As the successor to Morgan Rogers (£5.7m), there is considerable pressure on Manzambi to make significant tangible contributions in the final third and he delivered in spades against Spurs.

Seconds before the half-time whistle, he opened the scoring with a simple close-range finish, a result of his ultra advanced position in the six-yard box.

Then midway through the second half, he assisted Nicolas Jackson (£3.4m) for the visitors’ second goal with a classic example of link-up play after a long ball forward.

Manzambi was replaced by George Hemmings (£2.6m) soon after but a goal and assist meant he banked 14 points in North London, the joint-highest tally achieved in the fixture alongside Emi Buendia (£3.3m).



In the fact, only Antoine Semenyo (£5.7m) earned more points among Dream Team midfielders than the Villa pair in Gameweek 5.

Dream Team bosses keen on Manzambi should be encouraged by his willingness to get close to Jackson, in the same manner he supported Breel Embolo at the World Cup.

He is rightfully categorised as a midfielder in Dream Team but essentially played as a second striker for long spells against Spurs.

Manzambi is capable of playing off either flank in Emery’s preferred 4-2-3-1 formation but looks increasingly effective as a No10 as he continues to develop.



His 14-point haul was well timed as it will be on gaffers’ minds throughout the international break.

When Dream Team resumes, Aston Villa will fulfil four consecutive double Gameweeks:

Sports.title: Man Utd news LIVE: JJ Gabriel latest as new deadline set after 'agreement reached'
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel has been the centre of attention at Manchester United

Plenty is going on at Manchester United during the first international break of the season, with the club facing a number of issues after a disappointing start to their Premier League campaign, including uncertainty surrounding the future of JJ Gabriel

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's Manchester United news live blog for Wednesday, September 23.

JJ Gabriel continues to dominate the conversation around Old Trafford after the highly-rated youngster informed Manchester United of his desire to leave the club. Widely regarded as one of the brightest talents in United's academy, Gabriel has long been tipped for a big future at the club, making his decision all the more surprising.

The teenager is understood to have enlisted agent Ali Barat as efforts to secure a move away from United intensify. Barat's involvement could prove significant, with reports suggesting his connections have helped open up potential opportunities at European giants Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

Despite requesting an exit, Gabriel remains registered with United for the remainder of the season and cannot be deregistered. Club officials are still hopeful the situation can be resolved and that the youngster can be persuaded to stay.

Gabriel turns 16 on October 6, when he becomes eligible to sign a scholarship agreement with United. However, he will have to wait until his 17th birthday before he can sign a professional contract.

Off the pitch, United are also due to publish their latest financial results today, offering a fresh insight into the club's economic position.

Sports.title: Man Utd revenue soars but debt rises as latest financial accounts released
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce record revenue figures but debt rises again in latest financial accounts

Manchester United have announced their fourth quarter and full year fiscal 2026 results with the Reds recording record revenues after Sir Jim Ratcliffe's cost-cutting measures

View 2 Images Manchester United have announced their latest financial results (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United recorded record revenues in their latest financial results. United say that the club continue to benefit from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's operating cost and headcount reductions, alongside the improved third-place Premier League finish during the 2025/26 season.

‌



Despite recording a full year operating profit of £22.6million, United once again posted an overall loss for the year of £43m, compared to £33m the year before.

‌



United's revenue, however, rose by 1.7 per cent compared to 2024/25, which the club believe shows they are on the right track given they had no European football and no training kit sponsor in place. In total, United posted record revenues of £677.6m, up from £666.5m in the previous full year.

‌



The club feel that more "financial discipline" is needed to stabilise the business after they recorded a loss.

Roy Keane points finger after JJ Gabriel quit bombshell with reminder about Man United starlet READ MORE :

Debt levels at United, meanwhile, are also still rising, though it is part down to the change in interest rates and the refinancing of some bonds in June of this year.

United believe "non-current borrowings" now stand at £577.6m, up from £471.9m last year. The Reds also have a revolving credit facility, which is similar to a credit card, and that stood at £100m at the end of June 2026.

‌



Meanwhile, United's matchday income dropped by £6.8m, which is no surprise given the Reds had 10 fewer games at Old Trafford last season, due to no European football and being knocked out of the FA Cup and Carabao Cup at the first hurdle.

Once more, United's wage bill fell, down to £302m, and United said that was "primarily due to changes in the make-up of the men’s first team squad, combined with savings associated with headcount reduction programs implemented over the previous two fiscal years."

View 2 Images Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada revelaed record revenues (Image: Getty)

‌



United Chief Executive Officer Omar Berrada said: "We are pleased to have secured record revenues and adjusted EBITDA which demonstrates the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football. This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years.

"It also proves Manchester United's enduring popularity and commercial strength. While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.

"With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men’s and women’s teams during the summer window and our men’s team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We have also strengthened commercially and have welcomed Betway as our new Training Kit partner and SumUp as our new Sleeve partner; two excellent organisations which we are delighted to be working with, alongside our kit supplier, adidas and front of shirt partner, Snapdragon.

"Our other main area of focus is our plan to develop a new 100,000-seater stadium. We have now completed the major milestone of securing the land which will form part of the proposed location of the new stadium."

Article continues below

United have made a disappointing start to the 2026/27 season. The Red Devils have won just one of their opening five Premier League matches, drawing two and losing two. United made a winning start to life back in the Champions League by thrashing Sabah 4-0 but they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney takes aim at Man Utd board for 'weak' decision and reveals manager hope
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney takes aim at Man Utd board for 'weak' decision and reveals manager hope

Wayne Rooney hopes Michael Carrick can turn Manchester United's fortunes around but says the squad is 'a bit weak' following the transfer window

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney speaks on Stick to United (Image: Stick to United)

Wayne Rooney believes recruitment figures have let down Michael Carrick and played a role in Manchester United's difficult start to the season. However, the iconic former Red Devils striker is confident that his former teammate can turn things around.

‌



They sit in the bottom half of the table at the first international break of the season after one win in their opening five Premier League matches. They are winless in their last four and Matheus Cunha's deflected effort spared increased scrutiny as United picked up a point at Fulham on Sunday.

‌



Pressure has begun to mount on the United head coach, despite only being handed the reins on a permanent basis in the summer. Rooney has expressed his desire to see Carrick spark an improvement after the break.

‌



He told talkSPORT: "He [Carrick] knows what's in for there and listen, you always want more as a manager, I'm sure he would have wanted more from the transfer window, but he's left with what he's left with.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"I think the Premier League has got better, there's better teams in there. But if you don't win at Man United, or at any club, at the minute it's very tough, so I hope he turns it around."

United strengthened their squad during the summer transfer window, channelling the bulk of their expenditure into midfield reinforcements. Andrey Santos joined for £48million, potentially rising to £50m, from Premier League rivals Chelsea, while Youri Tielemans came in after his £35m release clause was activated.

Despite this, many felt that other areas of the United squad were left short, particularly in attack and defence. Rooney believes the recruitment team failed to adequately support the manager.

‌



He said: "There's always going to be pressure, Michael knows that. If you're not winning football games at Man United, then that pressure is there if you don't win one game.

View 2 Images Cunha was one of the additions to the United squad in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"So, it hasn't been the ideal start to the season... there are certain things which I felt the club had to do before the window shut, in bringing players in... the squad is a bit weak.

"He's got to find a way to get more and the best out of these players to get up the table after this international break... I think the break has come at the right time.

"He's shown that he can get results out of this group of players. They have to get their head down and work and hopefully get some better results."

‌



Following the draw in West London, Carrick came out defiantly to rubbish reports of pressure mounting on his position in charge, after winning 12 of his 17 games last season. "I think that'll be a lot longer than one or two games of results," he said.

"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, I'm not thinking 'how long have I got?' It's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in.

"That's just not on the radar. It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results, and two or three games too many because I really hate losing. But that doesn't mean that the world caves in."

Sports.title: Ireland make feelings clear as Dara O'Shea asked about shaking hands with Israel players
Sports.content:
Ireland make feelings clear as Dara O'Shea asked about shaking hands with Israel players

Heimir Hallgrimsson and Dara O'Shea have been speaking in a press conference ahead of Republic of Ireland's Nations League trip to Kosovo on Thursday

View 3 Images Dara O'Shea was asked whether the Republic of Ireland players plan to shake hands with their Israeli opponents (Image: Tim Clayton/Corbis via Getty Images)

The Republic of Ireland players will discuss whether to shake hands with their Israeli counterparts on Friday, according to defender Dara O'Shea. Ireland are set to go up against Israel twice during the extended three-week international break, with the first meeting taking place in Hungary on Sunday.

‌



There has been pressure on Ireland to boycott matches against Israel due to the attack in Gaza. But, earlier this summer, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) voted to proceed with the games - which take place on September 27 and October 4 - amid concerns that a boycott could harm the nation.

‌



Despite that, Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson made his feelings clear about facing Israel during his squad announcement last week, saying: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel," when asked about keeping his players focused on the football, rather than on the political standpoint that these matches are facing.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Now, O'Shea has been asked whether Ireland, who travel to face Kosovo first on Thursday, are prepared to shake hands with Israeli players amid the increased outrage around the two fixtures.

‌



Speaking in a press conference on Wednesday, Ipswich and Ireland defender O'Shea said: "We spoke already at the start of the week that we are going to come together on Friday and discuss this as a group.

"Tomorrow we have a game to focus on. Once the game is over and Friday comes, we are all going to come together as one and discuss it."

Hallgrimsson's take on Israel caused a strong reaction from the Middle Eastern nation, with the Israeli FA hitting back on social media, claiming the Ireland manager is ignorant and a hypocrite.

‌



View 3 Images Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

"We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," the Israeli FA said in a statement. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Taoiseach Micheal Martin, who is Ireland's prime minister, then spoke on Tuesday at the United Nations, where he criticised the Israeli's attack on Hallgrimsson and branded it as "unacceptable".

‌



"They are unacceptable remarks and should be withdrawn," Martin said in New York. "We're very clear and I think [UN secretary-general] Antonio Guterres said it again this morning, he has never in his lifetime seen the level and scale of death and destruction as he witnessed in terms of the Israeli government's war on Gaza in the aftermath of the horrific Hamas attack preceding the war. Our manager is saying the exact same thing.

"Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

Hallgrimsson was asked about the support he has received from Martin in the press conference on Wednesday, to which he replied: "Obviously, we are grateful for the support we have.

‌



View 3 Images Heimir Hallgrimsson speaking in a press conference (Image: Brian Lawless/PA)

"What I said last week has taken the attention away from maybe what is most important, we are playing an important game against Kosovo. Maybe it was not clever for me to take the attention like this. We need to be focused on the game. But to answer the question, we are grateful for all the support we get. It's a tricky time."

The Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a military offensive in Gaza, and more than 73,000 people have since been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

‌



Israel has denied that it has committed genocide, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity. They feel their military operations in Gaza have been conducted in self-defence and in accordance with international law.

Despite this, more than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group to urge a boycott of the games against Israel. Ireland are set to face Israel in Hungary on Sunday before the reverse fixture takes place in Serbia seven days later.

The letter states that the FAI, UEFA and the Irish government should have intervened before this stage, but there is still time to "show the power of sport to unite". Sportspeople, including Olympian Ciara Mageean, former Republic of Ireland footballer Louise Quinn, and ex-Ireland rugby fly-half Tony Ward, have signed it.

Sports.title: 5 things in Julian Ward's in-tray as incoming Liverpool chief left with Virgil van Dijk dilemma
Sports.content:
Liverpool are set for yet another period of change with Julian Ward set to be appointed as the club’s new sporting director. The 45-year-old is set to step into the role as a replacement for Richard Hughes, who left earlier this month to join Al-Hilal.

Michael Edwards has also moved on, having left his role as the chief executive officer of football at the club’s FSG owners. Following a long search, Liverpool have now chosen to promote Ward from FSG’s technical director - and he is expected to be very busy indeed once he steps into the job.

With the Reds in the opening weeks of a new era with Andoni Iraola still finding his feet as the club's head coach, Ward will play an influential role in shaping with the future at Anfield looks like.

Take a look at the pressing matters in Ward's in-tray as he prepares to take the reins:

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Agree on strategy

Having already been at Liverpool and FSG, Ward already has a good idea of what the club’s approach is going to be in the transfer market. But what he needs to decide is whether he wants to keep it the same or alter it slightly.

The Reds have not been afraid to splash the cash over recent seasons, with the big-money acquisitions of Hugo Ekitike, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak.

‌



Of course, that kind of strategy is not sustainable when utilised every single season. So Ward and Liverpool’s recruitment team might have to look to more affordable players going forwards.

View 4 Images Julian Ward previously had a huge role under Jurgen Klopp (Image: Getty Images)

2. Sort out the Mac Allister situation

Argentine midfielder Alexis Mac Allister has made his complaints over a potential new contract known over recent days. He claimed that he was ‘very, very sad’ after being told that the Reds were not in a position to offer him a new deal.

And while he remains happy at the club, Liverpool might have to make a decision soon. Mac Allister has two years remaining on his current contract so the Reds might have to decide to sell if they cannot extend his stay.

‌



If they can, they need to get moving soon or they will risk Mac Allister entering his final year and he could well become another big-money star to leave the club for nothing.

View 4 Images Alexis Mac Allister is keen to sign a new deal at Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

3. Make decisions on other deals - including Van Dijk

Speaking of players set to leave for nothing, Liverpool could have a host of first-team stars departing in just eight months’ time. Alisson and Virgil van Dijk have both been pivotal for Liverpool over the past few years but see their respective deals expire at the end of the season.

They could be joined by Wataru Endo, Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas. It goes without saying that some decisions have to be made.

‌



Whether that be new deals or emotional farewells, those calls need to be made by Ward and possibly soon as it could dictate what Liverpool do either in January or the following summer window.

4. Start planning for the future

It goes without saying that Liverpool could be set to lose a huge chunk of experience should both Alisson and Van Dijk leave. And not just that, they would be losing their leadership and their dressing room influence.

Put simply, that needs addressing. Dominik Szoboszlai would emerge as the most likely candidate to claim the captain’s armband but other than him, Liverpool desperately need more experience.

Whether that be players with Premier League experience or indeed European, the Reds need to look into the market for stars that add to their leadership group. And that falls on Ward and his scouting team.

‌



View 4 Images Andoni Iraola is the man tasked with leading Liverpool into a new era (Image: AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

5. Bring young players to the forefront

While signings will of course be one of the main responsibilities that Ward will have to consider, another aspect of the squad that he needs to consider is the amount of young players in contention.

The Reds have the likes of Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha and more chomping at the bit for first-team football at Anfield. And should they not receive it, they could be tempted to look elsewhere - Ngumoha has already been linked with a move to Arsenal.

Ward needs to open up dialogue with the duo, and those following in their footsteps, to ensure their futures remain on Merseyside and there is a tangible path into the first team.

‌

Ray Houghton believes Republic of Ireland's players face an "impossible" position around the two Israel games, after Micheal Martin called Israeli FA remarks about Heimir Hallgrimsson "unacceptable"

View 3 Images Republic of Ireland are due to face Israel on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Former Republic of Ireland midfielder Ray Houghton has criticised the Irish government for failing to back the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) amid the outrage around the upcoming matches against Israel.

‌



Ireland are set to face Israel on Sunday, September 27 and Sunday, October 4 in two Nations League fixtures during the extended three-week international break.

‌



During his squad announcement for two matches against Israel, as well as a trip to Kosovo and a home game with Austria, Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson said: "We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel," when asked about keeping his players focused on the football, rather than on the political standpoint that these matches are facing.

‌



In response to Hallgrimsson's comments on Monday, the Israeli FA hit back in a social media statement, saying: "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

"Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Although Irish prime minister Micheal Martin spoke on Tuesday at the United Nations where he criticised the Israeli's attack on Hallgrimsson, Houghton believes it's too little too late. The 64-year-old ex-Liverpool and Fulham man has claimed that the Irish government should have intervened much sooner.

View 3 Images Ray Houghton (Image: INPHO/James Crombie)

Due to the mass criticism surrounding the two matches, Houghton feels the Ireland players have been placed into an "impossible" situation.

‌



"They are damned if they do and they are damned if they don't," he said, speaking on behalf of IrishBetting.ie. "It's one of those things where the players have got to get on with their job. They are playing away from home, there'll be no Irish fans and it's a game that no one really wants, is it?

"If you ask the players honestly, they would probably say they don't want to play either. But there is a commitment from the FAI to play it. I don't know what would happen if they didn't play it, how UEFA would sanction Ireland.

"I think it has been quite clear that the Irish public don't want the game. Not everyone, but the majority.

‌



"A lot of people say to the players, just don't play. But it's a really difficult one, a really difficult story to be a part of. I think the players have been put in a position that they don't want to be in."

Despite this, more than than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group to urge a boycott of the games against Israel. Ireland are set to face Israel in Hungary on Sunday before the reverse fixture takes place in Serbia seven days later.

The letter states that the FAI, UEFA and the Irish government should have intervened before this stage, but there is still time to "show the power of sport to unite". Sportspeople including Olympian Ciara Mageean, former Republic of Ireland footballer Louise Quinn, ex-Ireland rugby fly-half Tony Ward have signed it.

As well as that, Amnesty International condemned Israel's inclusion in the Nations League as "a betrayal of Palestinians, football's own rules and human rights."

Steve Cockburn, Amnesty International's Regional Director for Europe, said: "It's unconscionable that the Israel men's football team will participate in the UEFA Nations League this autumn despite clear evidence that Israel's football association continues to support illegal settlements.

"Instead of sending a clear message that there is a cost for Israel's unlawful occupation of the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) and its atrocity crimes against Palestinians, UEFA is giving Israel an international stage as it maintains its brutal occupation of the OPT, its system of apartheid over all Palestinians, and its ongoing genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko injury mocked as Michael Carrick accused of 'killing' Man Utd teammate
Sports.content:
Benjamin Sesko injury mocked as Michael Carrick accused of 'killing' Man Utd teammate

Michael Carrick is being accused of ‘killing’ a Manchester United player, with Benjamin Sesko also the subject of mocking now for having sustained a shin injury

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko is being questioned over the severity of his shin injury (Image: Visionhaus, Getty Images)

Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt have questioned the seriousness of a shin injury that continues to sideline Benjamin Sesko at Manchester United. The pair have also accused Michael Carrick of playing Matheus Cunha in a position that 'kills him' and makes him nowhere near as effective as he can be.

‌



Sesko, 23, missed the 1-1 draw with Fulham. The striker felt pain in his shin during the Carabao Cup third round defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford.

‌



Cunha started up front in the absence of the Slovenia international. He scored United's late equaliser to earn a point.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Butt said: "Playing Cunha as a nine kills him. He's nowhere near the player he is off the side."

‌



The only time Cunha and Sesko have started together so far this season was in the Champions League match against Sabah. United's number ten began on the left wing and scored his first goal this term.

"We haven't got a number nine other than Sesko, other than (Joshua) Zirkzee, but he's been going, staying, going, staying. And when he does come on, he doesn't look anywhere near a Manchester United number nine."

Butt continued: "The biggest problem is the number nine. How can Man United have one centre forward? Who is injured, with what, a shin injury?" Scholes added: "How do you injure your shin? Ain't that a broken leg? Can't you just put your shin pads on?"

‌



View 2 Images Nicky Butt has had his say on how Cunha is being used (Image: The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Latest news and analysis via the MEN’s Manchester United Facebook page

His co-host then concluded: "You either break your shin, or you play. Put your shin pads on or your padding on, I don't quite get it. Without knowing what it is, it is hard to discuss it."

‌



Sesko missed all of pre-season with the injury. It also ended his debut campaign three matches early.

Butt also delivered his verdict on the rest of United's squad, saying: "Midfield, we have good footballers, but can't dominate a game.

"The back four look an average back four. The right-back, is he going to get you into the top two, top three? No. Harry (Maguire) is past his best. (Lisandro) Martinez is a good footballer, but he's not a dominant centre back. We know with Luke (Shaw), he plays three or four games, gets an injury, then he's back in. The back four is a massive problem."

Article continues below

Shaw notably started every Premier League match last season for United, one of only five outfield players ever to do so for the club. The others to do so are Denis Irwin, Gary Pallister (twice), Maguire and Steve Bruce.

Sports.title: Former England boss lands shock new job aged 73 as he returns to work
Sports.content:
Former England boss lands shock new job aged 73 as he returns to work

The ex-England coach has landed a new job more than two decades after he steered the Three Lions' ship and anointed a legendary captain

View 3 Images Ex-England caretaker manager Peter Taylor has been hired as an assistant for Thailand (Image: Thailand FA)

Former England boss Peter Taylor has landed a new job with the Thailand national team. The 73-year-old only managed the Three Lions as caretaker for one game in 2000 - a 1-0 defeat to Italy.

‌



Not many ex-footballers can say they've played for and managed their country. Taylor can. The Essex-born boss enjoyed a storied playing career for the likes of Crystal Palace and Tottenham in the 1970s and '80s. He was first selected for England whilst not playing in either the first or second division at Palace, which was and still is unheard of.

‌



Taylor made four Three Lions appearances and scored two goals in 1976. After subsequent spells at Leyton Orient, Oldham Athletic, Maidstone and Exeter City, he began his coaching career as a player-manager at Dartford a decade later. In 1996, Glenn Hoddle asked him to manage England's Under-21s and he obliged.

‌



After three years in this role, Taylor returned to club management before being hired as caretaker for the England senior side following Kevin Keegan's sudden resignation.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Max Dowman handed England reality check as Arsenal star eyes long-standing record READ MORE :

Inside the rise of Ezri Konsa and why World Cup star can inspire England's next generation READ MORE :

In the one game he oversaw against Italy, he leaned on the youth of Gareth Barry, Jamie Carragher and Rio Ferdinand. He also handed David Beckham the armband for the first time before heading back to manage Leicester City.

‌



View 3 Images Taylor was the first coach to name Beckham as captain for England (Image: Getty)

Taylor has manned the dugout for various sides since, his latest club stint coming as manager of non-league outfit Canvey Island FC. But now, he's back in an international set-up.

Even before his senior role with England arrived, Taylor was a Premier League manager. After the caretaker stint, he was recruited by some big names, including Brighton, Hull City, Palace, England's Under-21s for a second three-year spell and Bahrain's national team.

‌



But since 2001, he's held 16 different managerial positions and Thailand has now appointed Taylor as an assistant to manager Anthony Hudson for the upcoming FIFA ASEAN Cup.

A statement from the Thailand FA revealed the reason behind bringing in the experienced Taylor. He'll join another English assistant, Kane Wintersgill, within the set-up.

Hudson said: "Regarding Peter Taylor, we wanted to bring in an additional support member to assist with training. Of course, he isn't coming in to replace anyone or take over anyone's role, but rather to support the entire staff and help make our work more efficient."

‌



View 3 Images Thailand will soon play in the ASEAN Cup (Image: Getty)

Taylor has previously worked as an assistant under Hudson. In 2016, he accepted an offer to join Hudson's staff on the New Zealand national team. He was based in England and monitored the All Whites stars who plied their trade in Europe, which included ex-West Ham defender Winston Reid and Chris Wood, then of Leeds United.

Speaking in 2016 of Taylor, Hudson said: "I have a huge amount of respect for Pete. Certainly, everyone I know in football who speaks about Pete holds him in the highest regard. He's a good man."

Article continues below

His latest role with Thailand is a reversal from 2011, when Hudson worked as an assistant to Taylor with Bahrain. He led the Bahraini team to their first regional competition in history, the GCC Games, but was sacked in 2012 after a crushing loss to the United Arab Emirates.

Taylor's first match with Thailand will be against Pakistan on September 26. Their ASEAN Cup campaign continues against Vietnam on September 29 and the Philippines on October 2. The final of the competition will take place on October 5.

Sports.title: Rising cruiserweight talent Roehrig signs with Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
Lucas Roehrig has signed a promotional deal with Zuffa Boxing and will fight on Sky Sports.

The cruiserweight talent, only 23 years old, has impressed in his rise through the cruiserweight ranks.

He will fight next on Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena on November 7, live on Sky Sports.

His trainer and mentor is former world champion George Groves. Roehrig has been flawless so far in his professional career.

The young Londoner has won nine fights, never been defeated and has taken five of those wins inside the distance.

Roehrig made his pro debut in 2024, halting former English champion Joel McIntyre in three rounds.

Last year he shut out American prospect Brian Jones over six rounds. From then on, he's continued to box and beat opponents with winning records.

His last two fights have been consecutive stoppage victories, over Adam Kolarik and Faton Tolaj, at York Hall.

Roehrig is now joining a promotional powerhouse that has a strong cruiserweight stable, including Jai Opetaia, Chris Billam-Smith, Ryan Rozicki and more.

Zuffa Boxing 11, headlined by Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton, takes place this Saturday live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: 'Scotland was always the one for me' - Binks' pride at first call-up
Sports.content:
"I've wanted to play for Scotland for years, and now the opportunity has come. I'm just really proud."

Defender Luis Binks has played at under-21 level for both Scotland and England, but insisted he did not hesitate when new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli said he wanted him in his first squad.

The Brondby captain is one of six players handed their first full call-ups for the Nations League games against Slovenia, North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Pocognoli has said he will not beg players to choose Scotland, something the 25-year-old agrees with.

"I think if he had to try and convince me, convince anyone, it's probably not the right thing for the player," Binks told Sky Sports News.

"I didn't need any convincing; I was available.

"I wanted to play for Scotland. I've wanted to play for Scotland for years and now the opportunity has come, I'm just really proud.

Image: Robbie Ure (L) and Luis Binks are two of the new faces in the Scotland squad

"It's where you feel your heart is and where you want to go. This was the route I wanted to take."

It is a new-look Scotland under Pocognoli with 12 players who were in Steve Clarke's final squad for the World Cup missing out, only Scott McTominay, Lawrence Shankland and Che Adams through injury.

And while it's a new environment for Binks, there are some familiar faces within the camp.

"It was a few years ago that I was with Aaron Hickey in Bologna and he got called up while we were there.

Image: Aaron Hickey has 22 caps for Scotland

"I could play for the 21s at the time and nothing ever coming up but it was always, Scotland was always the one for me that I wanted to go and play for.

"Going back years ago, under 16s when I went away with Scotland, the vibe was just so good.

"It felt like a proper team, it was just normal lads and you felt like you were playing with your mates so I knew there was always that feeling around it. I wanted to go and be a part of that again."

The Pocognoli era officially gets underway in Ljubljana on Saturday, with a game against Switzerland at Hampden Park three days later.

The squad then fly to North Macedonia on October 3 before returning to Glasgow to face Slovenia again on October 6.

Image: The Scotland players are training in La Manga ahead of their Nations League opener

Scotland were demoted from Nations League A after a play-off defeat by Greece last year and return to the second tier for this year's competition.

"Obviously we want to get to the A group of the Nations League but there are a lot of new faces, a lot of new management, new ways of playing," Binks added.

"I know what it's like because I've got a new manager at my club now and it's taking a bit of time so I imagine it's the same sort of process here.

"It's just about getting the players on board and buying into everything the manager wants to do.

"It's been early days, but I think everyone is fully on board and believes in what we can do as a country."

Sports.title: The other Sessegnon: Ryan's twin Steven rebuilding at AFC Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Steven and Ryan Sessegnon walked out at Craven Cottage side by side, each holding their daughters, last month.

The twins had made their way through Fulham's academy together and played in the first team together on a handful of occasions - but that night, they played against one another for the first time ever.

It was a special moment; a full-circle moment.

In any of the previous three seasons, a game like this would have been a perfect chance for a family reunion, as Steven had been living in Manchester for three years while playing for Wigan.

But now he's back home. And not just 'home' in terms of being back in south-west London. Properly back home.

He points ahead as he speaks to Sky Sports on a terrace at the Dons' training ground in New Malden. "We used to play academy games literally across this grass."

He points to the left. "I spent time at Coombe Boys School, which is five minutes up the road."

Fulham's Motspur Park training ground is six minutes' drive away. There, his nephew Kayden is part of the U18 squad.

"It's really wholesome to be back," says Sessegnon. "It helps massively being around family.

"I get to see my older brothers, my nieces, my nephews and I see my brother [Ryan] a few times a week.

"We play at two different levels, so there isn't too much to speak about as if we were in the same league, but we catch up on life, being dads, being providers, being men in our families and what the future looks like."

Sessegnon's return home has come at an important point in his career.

In his first season at Wigan in 2023/24, he played 29 games in all competitions. In his second, he suffered calf and knee injuries, before not playing again from January 4 2025.

At the start of his third, Gary Caldwell, who had replaced Ryan Lowe in February 2025, placed him on the transfer list.

"Things happen fast in football," Sessegnon says. "When I was put on the transfer list, I was told I wasn't going to play and I didn't go on the pre-season trip - but I ended up starting the first game of the season through injuries or lack of availability, and I thought I did well.

Image: Sessegnon signed a two-year deal at AFC Wimbledon in June

"It's fair game, it's part of it. The manager came in, the club wanted to go in a different direction. As long as everyone can come out of it happy and people can move onto clubs they know they can do well at, there's no problem with it."

A move away did not materialise so, on the few occasions Caldwell did select him, he was deployed at centre-back, where he had never played before.

"It was tough. Very, very tough. I felt like I could contribute to a team, but didn't really have the trust or belief behind me to do it.

"But as much as I could say I didn't have the proper backing to be in my own position, I was still given a chance to play football. It was down to me and it just never happened.

"There was no issue with anyone else apart from myself. I learned a lot there, a lot I can take with me for the rest of my career. It was a learning curve.

"The biggest thing was professionalism. Even in the worst stages of when I wasn't playing and I was told I wasn't going to be a part of it, I could still carry myself and be the best possible person.

Image: The 26-year-old made only 20 League One starts across the last two seasons at Wigan

"I felt I owed it to myself to show people I was still a very good trainer, a very good player and I think that helped me stick around longer than they probably wanted me to."

Sessegnon was released by the Latics in the summer and joined AFC Wimbledon on a two-year contract, with the option for a further 12 months, on June 25.

"I was preparing to go on holiday with my family and I got a call. As soon as they said Wimbledon, local, I said 'let's get it sorted'," he recalls.

"But it was also about the position I would play, how the gaffer [Johnnie Jackson] set it out. It wasn't complicated. I knew I could come in and, if I could get minutes, I would show my ability."

Sessegnon's first Dons appearance came on August 8 against Newport in the Carabao Cup, almost six months after his last competitive game for Wigan. He looks in genuine disbelief when he hears that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet League One match between Bromley and AFC Wimbledon

His full league debut came on September 7, in a 2-0 Sky Bet League One win over Bromley. He has had to bide his time, but he understands why.

"It's like injuries, you have a bit of anxiousness about getting going again, but I had the pre-season and here at Wimbledon, they looked after me very well. The gaffer has looked after me very well and communicated very well with me.

"In my head I wanted to start and play as many games as I could, but coming off the bench a few times has probably benefitted me to get to grips with football again.

"It's probably the simplest football I've played in my career, but the most effective. We're able to create chances, I'm able to get the ball high up the pitch.

"It's not overthought, and I think it brings the best out of the whole squad and definitely myself. I've enjoyed it so far and it takes the pressure off the whole squad; we know we can create chances, we just have to be solid."

The Dons have certainly been solid, with five clean sheets from seven games so far - the joint-most in the Sky Bet EFL.

They are four points behind leaders Bradford going into Saturday's trip to Cambridge - which is live on Sky Sports+ - despite having only scored five goals so far.

That said, they are still among the bookmakers' favourites to be relegated this season.

But now, back on home soil, Sessegnon has the chance to help AFC Wimbledon defy the odds again, just around the corner from where it all began.

Watch Cambridge vs AFC Wimbledon live on Sky Sports+ on Saturday; kick-off 3pm.

Sports.title: Hadjar to remain at Red Bull for 2027
Sports.content:
Red Bull have confirmed Isack Hadjar will remain as Max Verstappen's team-mate for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Hadjar stepped up to Red Bull at the start of this year after an impressive debut campaign with Racing Bulls in 2025 but has missed the last three rounds due to a wrist injury he suffered during last month's summer break.

But the 21-year-old is now fit enough to drive and is back at this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which takes place on Saturday - live on Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player No pun… extended! Red Bull announce Hadjar contract in hilarious video!

Red Bull had already announced last month that four-time world champion Verstappen signed a new contract to stay at the team until at least the end of 2030.

"We're very excited to continue our journey with Isack. Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision," said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve.

"You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierre Gasly and Isack Hadjar visit Cirque Du Soleil to try their hand at some hilarious stunts!

The second Red Bull seat alongside Verstappen is widely regarded as the toughest on the F1 grid after several drivers including Pierre Gasly, Alex Albon, Liam Lawson and Yuki Tsunoda all struggled against the Dutchman.

But, Hadjar has been closer to Verstappen than those drivers and has even got the better of his team-mate at times this season, so his seat has not come under scrutiny.

Despite missing the last three race weekends, Hadjar is still eighth in the Drivers' Championship and reclaimed his Monaco Grand Prix podium after Red Bull and McLaren successfully appealed Gasly's overturned speeding penalties.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Isack Hadjar has been reinstated to the Monaco podium after a Red Bull appeal with Alpine expressing frustration as Pierre Gasly's penalty for speeding in pit lane is restored

"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track," continued Mekies.

"We still have a lot we want to achieve this season, but it's a great feeling to know that the drivers, engineers and everyone back at the factory are all heading in the same direction, committed and together."

No surprise to see Hadjar retain seat Sky Sports F1's Craig Slater:



"Hadjar has been out for the last three rounds because he damaged his arm and wrist. I understand that was done by hitting a heavy bag in training because he does boxing in training.



"But he has recovered, he is taking part this weekend, and he will be Max Verstappen's partner in 2027.



"Hadjar will be continuing with Red Bull. Liam Lawson deputised very well in his absence but nobody was surprised that Hadjar gets the nod to carry on.



"He has probably been Verstappen's most competitive teammate since Daniel Ricciardo left a few years ago."

Hadjar added: "I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing. I came to this team eight months ago and immediately understood the scale and ambition of this organisation.

"There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me. I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day about what lies ahead.

Formula 1 2027 field Team Driver Driver Mercedes Kimi Antonelli George Russell Ferrari Lewis Hamilton Charles Leclerc McLaren Lando Norris Oscar Piastri Red Bull Max Verstappen Isack Hadjar Racing Bulls ??? ??? Alpine Pierre Gasly Franco Colapinto Haas ??? ??? Audi ??? ??? Williams Carlos Sainz Alex Albon Aston Martin ??? ??? Cadillac Sergio Perez Valtteri Bottas

What's left to play out in the F1 driver market?

F1's current top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have now all locked in their driver line-ups for 2027 with no changes.

Alpine, Williams and Cadillac's drivers are all under contract for 2027 while Audi are set to keep their pairing of Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg.

That leaves Racing Bulls, Haas and Aston Martin as the only teams yet to nail down their drivers for next year - but there could be changes.

Fernando Alonso is considering his future in the sport and is the biggest stumbling block in the driver market because if he retires, Aston Martin will have a seat available.

Alonso says news "will not come soon" as he's unhappy with the current regulations in F1 which led to FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem commenting he wants to accelerate the deficit of Aston Martin's engine supplier Honda.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Simon Lazenby, Martin Brundle, Bernie Collins and Nico Hulkenberg debate Fernando Alonso's future in F1 and what Aston Martin need to do to keep him in the sport

Britain's Oliver Bearman is set to stay at Haas but his team-mate Esteban Ocon is driving for his future after a difficult start to the season.

Although Ocon has improved since the summer break, Haas may give Ferrari junior Rafael Camara his F1 debut for 2027 after an impressive F2 campaign for the Brazilian.

The current F2 championship leader is Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov and history shows Red Bull are keen to give youngsters an F1 opportunity at the earliest opportunity.

However, Red Bull have a tricky decision to make as both current Racing Bulls drivers of Arvid Lindblad and Lawson are performing very well this year, so dropping one of them would be harsh.

Sports.title: Can Arteta turn champions into serial winners?
Sports.content:
When Mikel Arteta signed his last Arsenal contract in September 2024, his quest to bring major silverware back to the club was ongoing. Two years later, he agrees his new one after leading them to a long-awaited Premier League title.

His task now is to turn champions into serial winners.

Arteta has overseen a total transformation of the club since his appointment in 2019. Arsenal, 10th in the Premier League table when he took over, were in a state of drift. Now, they are re-established among Europe's elite, unrecognisable in all departments.

Arteta has joined a select group of 13 managers to have won the Premier League. He now has the chance to join an even smaller group, made up of only Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger, by winning it more than once.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol and Gary Cotterill provide the latest on Mikel Arteta's Arsenal future as he is expected to sign a new contract

Securing a first Champions League, after guiding Arsenal to only their second final last term, is another chance for immortality.

The agreement over his new contract, described as an "utmost priority" by co-chair Josh Kroenke in May, reflects the club's belief that they are in the best possible hands. It also gives Arteta the chance to get closer to Guardiola's longevity at Manchester City.

The club feel the departure of Arteta's old mentor from City, coupled with instability elsewhere, presents an opportunity to capitalise. Arsenal are in their "win window", to quote Kroenke. "We think we have a chance here to dominate," he said in May.

Arteta's task has been made harder by the failure to add a level-raising forward in the summer. But his squad is replete with players in or approaching their peak years, between 24 and 28, now with the added experience of having won major silverware.

Image: Mikel Arteta poses with the Premier League trophy in May

The group look well-set to build on their success. But Arteta, the rookie head coach-turned elite manager whose work other clubs now strive to emulate, might be Arsenal's biggest asset of all, which is why the news of his contract agreement is so significant.

Who better to nurture the culture which has underpinned their success than the man who painstakingly implemented it?

Arteta ensures stability, allowing Arsenal to operate from a position of strength. "Getting the foundations in place is usually the hardest part of the journey," added Kroenke.

His tenure has been a story of steady improvement, both domestically, where Arsenal have ended a 22-year wait for the title, and in Europe, where they have gone from Champions League quarter-finalists, to semi-finalists, to runners-up in three years.

But there is work to do to sustain the trajectory.

Their defeat to Brighton highlighted room for improvement. It felt like a slap in the face to Arsenal, largely because it was so uncharacteristic. Arteta's side, defined by their steeliness, hadn't lost a Premier League game by a margin of three goals since 2023.

Arteta will hope to use the result as a wake-up call, and a reminder to his players that there can be no room for complacency in their efforts to retain their crown. "This is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher explains why he believes Mikel Arteta has become the Sir Alex Ferguson of today's Premier League

He might even come to be grateful for it.

Arsenal went into the season as most people's favourites to win the title. But only a handful of sides have gone back-to-back in the Premier League era. Arsenal haven't managed it since the 1930s. History shows the enormity of the task ahead of them.

Part of the challenge for Arteta is to continue evolving the team.

Heavily impacted by injuries to their best attacking players for a second consecutive season last term, Arsenal leaned into their defensive and set-piece prowess to get over the line in the title race. They remain a formidable outfit on both fronts.

Clearly, there is still work to do in the transfer market to bring their attack up to the same level. For now, though, Arteta must get more from what he has, helped, at least, by a far clearer injury list.

Image: Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard struggled with injuries in the last two seasons

It is worth noting that the last time he had Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka fit for a full season, in 2023/24, Arsenal broke a club record for goals. The trio, together again at last, scored 10 goals in their first seven games of the campaign.

More broadly, there have been signs of a return to a more possession-orientated playing style, and a greater desire to control games with the ball rather than without it.

It is of course still early in the campaign to make definitive judgements. But Arsenal's numbers are up for possession, passes and passes in the final third compared to last season.

Sports.title: The Italian Job gets a sequel! Can Mancini inspire a new generation?
Sports.content:
This year, Italian football fell to its lowest ebb. In Europe, no Italian club made it past the quarter-finals - while Atalanta were the only Serie A side to reach the Champions League last 16. But that was nothing compared to the national team.

Italy did not qualify for the third World Cup in a row. An unthinkable prospect given they have won the competition four times.

The first two failures to qualify were masked over by the Euro 2020 triumph at Wembley. That at least gave the nation hope.

The third World Cup failure was one last straw. A 48-team World Cup did not include Italy. It brought about the resignations of not just head coach Gennaro Gattuso, but also Italian FA president Gabriele Gravina and Gianluigi Buffon as the team's head of delegation.

Image: Mancini is back as Italy head coach for a second spell

"It's a sensitive subject that affects me a lot, because not qualifying for three World Cups in a row is tough, and Italy certainly doesn't deserve that," Italy captain Gianluigi Donnarumma tells Sky Sports.

Now Italy have gone back to the future. Roberto Mancini, the manager who won the Euros five years ago, is back at the helm.

"We have to work. The only way forward is to work," adds Donnarumma. "There has now been a change of coach, the return of Mr Mancini - and the objective is to work and try to take Italy back to where it deserves to be.

"I know it's not easy for the fans, but especially for us, because only we know how much it means to us to play in a competition like the World Cup.

"So we'll give everything to bring Italy back to where it deserves to be. We have a great responsibility because history says that Italy should always be there. History has taught us that. So we have to bring Italy back to where it belongs."

Image: Gianluigi Donnarumma is the captain of the Italy national team

Yes, Italy belongs at the top table. But it has been far off the level for some time. The latest World Cup disaster was the latest in a long line of slippery slopes since they reached the top of the world in 2006.

Twenty years later, that penalty shoot-out win over France is still Italy's last appearance in a World Cup knockout game. They have just won just one World Cup match since then - the 2-1 victory over England in Brazil 2014.

Yes, there was the successful European Championships campaign of 2012 that saw Italy reach the final. But since those days, Italy have not been the same. And there are multiple reasons for it.

Italy have not been able to replicate the world-class talent they once possessed. The World Cup-winning side of 20 years ago had the likes of Fabio Cannavaro, Alessandro Nesta, Gattuso and Alessandro Del Piero.

Six years later in 2012, that generation still lived on through Buffon, Daniele De Rossi, and Andrea Pirlo. But since the retirement of stalwarts Giorgio Chiellini and Leandro Bonucci, the next generation of Italian football has been lost.

According to the CIES Football Observatory, between 2020 and 2025, Italy produced just 413 football exports. It ranked 24th in the world, behind the United States, Japan and Russia.
