Sports.title: Excessive focus on battle between Ferrari drivers is “not fair” – Leclerc | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc says too much attention has been paid to the on-track battle between him and his team mate, particularly since their clash at Monza.

The Ferrari driver has already admitted he went too far in his first-lap battle with Lewis Hamilton when he forced his team mate wide at turn two.

“Turn two in Monza is something that I’ve said repeatedly is not something that we want to see ever happen again,” said Leclerc. “And that [was] going too far on my side.

“But I’ve been through it already. I think it’s pretty clear that we don’t necessarily have to write [rules of engagement for] those things, I think it’s clear enough.

“But again, I feel like it’s being over-discussed and over-analysed when it’s about the red cars, and that’s not really fair.”

He alluded to incidents between the McLaren and Mercedes drivers during the final laps of the same race. “In Monza, if you look at the four top teams, three of them had fights like this with a car finishing in the grass, and at the end of the day, the only thing we are speaking about still now is the red car, which I don’t think is fair.”

Leclerc said both drivers have exceeded the limits of what is acceptable at times but he is happy with how they race wheel-to-wheel.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Of course there’s been moments where I went too far, where Lewis went too far, but I think the key in that is to discuss,” he said. “I’ve been with Ferrari since 2019 now and I know how everything we do is over-analysed, over-discussed and very often the conclusions that are taken after those kind of fights are the wrong ones.

“We only need to speak with Lewis to understand, we’ve been doing that all our life. We both want to win and there’s competition but we also want to win as a team and to make Ferrari come out on eventually. So that is the priority.

“I enjoy fighting with Lewis and that’s what is exciting in Formula 1 is to be fighting against the best and Lewis is definitely up there. So for me it’s a big challenge, but I’m enjoying it.”

Sports.title: “Money fears” delay F1’s decision on whether Middle East races will happen – report | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula One Management is delaying its decision over whether to cancel the final two rounds of the season due to concerns over money, according to a report in The Times.

F1 will not receive its huge fees from the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grand prix promoters if it calls off the races. If the promoters make the decision to cancel, they will bear the costs.

But the longer F1 leaves the decision, the harder it may be to organise a replacement for either race. Cancelling a race would reduce the number of points available and could affect the championship situation, potentially even deciding it. Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the championship by 81 points with 233 available.

Domenicali has indicated F1 has a plan to replace the Abu Dhabi finale if that cannot go ahead. This is believed to be a race at Imola in Italy.

F1 has already cancelled the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix as a result of the war. A replacement for the former, titled the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, will take place next week at the Sepang International Circuit.

Earlier this month FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the governing body will be guided by local promoters on whether the events could go ahead.

“Being from that part of the world, we can’t jump the gun and just say, that’s it, we are cancelling and then cancel,” he said.

“Are we going to allow our people, our staff, the drivers or the teams to go at risk? No, of course not. We will not. But we’ll have to also listen to the governments and to the local promoter there.”

Sports.title: Red Bull confirms Hadjar will remain as Verstappen’s team mate in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence to Isack Hadjar, extending his contract to drive for the team again next year.

Hadjar made his debut in Formula 1 last year with Red Bull’s second team, Racing Bulls, before being promoted to their leading squad this year.

“Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track,” said team principal Laurent Mekies, “especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.”

Although Hadjar did not compete in the last three rounds due to injury, Hadjar made an impressive start to life at Red Bull, taking a podium finish in his sixth appearance in Monaco. Before being forced out due to injury he had scored 71 points to Verstappen’s 109.

Red Bull has struggled to find an effective team mate to pair Verstappen with. The team handed Sergio Perez a two-year contract extension during 2024 but dropped him at the end of the year for Liam Lawson. Perez’s replacement lasted just two rounds at the start of last year before Red Bull dropped him. Yuki Tsunoda, who replaced Lawson, ended the season with the largest points deficit to a team mate ever seen in F1, leading Red Bull to make another change.

Mekies said Hadjar performed well from the outset after moving up to Red Bull. He will race for the team this weekend in Baku for the first time since the Hungarian Grand Prix in July.

“You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat,” said Mekies. “The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can’t wait to see him back out on track.”

Hadjar said he is “really excited” by his new deal. “From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I’ve been able to justify the faith they’ve had in me,” he said. “I’m constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead.”

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Conor Benn’s Comeback Pays 100% More Than Hearn Offered
Sports.content:
Conor Benn took a two-round thrashing from Ryan, yet his management still secured a lucrative deal for his next fight. Keith Connolly revealed Benn has a guaranteed purse for a return bout, a sum more than 100% higher than Eddie Hearn’s original offer for a Rolly Romero clash.

Connolly did not reveal either figure. His comparison still raises an awkward question for Zuffa: after paying Benn to face Garcia, what kind of fight justifies paying him substantially again?

“In the deal that we made for Conor, we have a substantial comeback number,” Connolly told talkSPORT. He said the payment was negotiated to give Benn a comeback fight in which he can get a win. Connolly also said Zuffa cannot drop Benn under the contract because of the Garcia defeat.

Connolly did his job for Benn. Give him an easy opponent, and he probably gets the win, but who’s going to be impressed after Ryan took him out in two rounds? Put him in with someone who can punch, and Zuffa risks paying a big guarantee to watch Benn lose again.

Benn can still sell a fight in Britain. He’s Nigel Benn’s son, he has a following, and there’s another Chris Eubank Jr. fight to make. But Ryan exposed the part of the sales pitch that said Benn belonged with the best welterweights. He’d looked poor in several fights since coming back; getting stopped in two rounds in his first world title shot made that much harder to sell his fights.

Connolly expects Benn to fight Chris Eubank Jr. a third time, and that’s Zuffa’s best chance of making money on his return. British fans know the family rivalry, even after Ryan stopped Benn in two rounds. Beating an easy opponent first might give Benn a win, but it won’t erase what happened against Garcia. Connolly made sure Benn gets paid either way.

Zuffa bought a circus act, and now they are stuck footing the bill for the cleanup. Dana White thought he was purchasing an elite British star with crossover appeal. Instead, Ryan took two rounds to turn Benn into an international laughingstock.

Now Zuffa holds a contract guaranteeing Benn millions for a return date, with nowhere left to hide him. They cannot put him in with an actual contender at 160 or 168 because any legitimate puncher will put him into retirement. They cannot put him on pay-per-view against an imported tomato can because fans will not pay fifty dollars to watch an unranked punching bag fall down in ninety seconds. That leaves Chris Eubank Jr. as the only escape route.

The promotional idea for a third fight between these privileged sons of famous British legends has completely changed. Nobody with working eyes believes this is a meeting of championship contenders. The athletic intrigue disappeared the moment Ryan landed his right hand, and Benn hit the deck.

The only angle left to sell is morbid curiosity. British boxing fans will tune in for one simple reason: to watch Benn get knocked out again. The novelty of the family rivalry is gone. It has turned into a pure demolition watch party. Eubank has every physical advantage, and he knows Benn cannot take a punch from someone with genuine power. If Zuffa pulls the trigger on the trilogy, they are selling tickets to an execution.

Benn-Eubank Jr. III can do strong business in the UK, but it will not generate the kind of money Zuffa needs to break even on the massive guarantees they handed out.

The British domestic market operates on nostalgia. UK ticket buyers will pack a stadium like Tottenham Hotspur again simply because of the family names. The problem is the pay-per-view numbers and international interest. Benn getting humiliated by Ryan inside two rounds destroyed any illusion that he is an elite global star. Overseas buyers in the United States will not pay sixty or seventy dollars for a domestic grudge match between an exposed welterweight and an aging middleweight.

Sports.title: WBC Orders Carlos Adames to Face Meiirim Nursultanov Next
Sports.content:
Meiirim Nursultanov was supposed to fight for an interim belt Saturday. Instead, he is going straight to Carlos Adames for the full WBC middleweight title.

The WBC ordered Adames to face his mandatory challenger next, Dan Rafael reported Tuesday. If the two sides cannot make a deal, a purse bid is scheduled for October 20. The winner must then fight interim champion Jesus Ramos Jr.

Nursultanov was set to face Ramos on Saturday’s PBC card before Ramos was hospitalized and withdrew with what PBC described as food poisoning. The WBC had previously said the winner of that fight would challenge Adames. Ramos had a sound reason to withdraw, but Nursultanov was ready to fight and should not have to wait for his title opportunity because the bout fell through.

The change gives Nursultanov more than a new opponent. He can fight for the full belt without first risking a loss to Ramos, and the WBC order gives him a deadline for negotiations. He still has to beat Adames, a difficult champion, but he no longer has another fight between him and the title shot he has sought.

Adames, meanwhile, has a mandatory to deal with rather than an open choice of opponents. Nursultanov offers a hard fight without the obvious payday of a marquee name. If the camps cannot agree on terms, the purse bid could also take control of the promotion out of their hands. That makes October 20 a meaningful date for both fighters, though an order is no guarantee the fight gets made.

Ramos keeps his claim to the winner, but his wait could stretch well beyond this fall. First, Adames and Nursultanov have to negotiate, fight, and recover. The WBC has given all three men a sequence; now it has to see that sequence through. Adames is completely trapped in boxing purgatory. He is the ultimate poster child for high risk, zero reward.

When Adames went to Riyadh and took Hamzah Sheeraz to school, he exposed the British fighter for everyone to see. He walked out of Saudi Arabia with a controversial draw while Sheeraz packed his bags and bolted straight out of the division to super middleweight rather than dare run that back. That fight cost Adames his golden ticket. If he had been given the decision he clearly earned, he would have commanded the massive purses and respect of an undisputed or marquee kingpin in Riyadh Season shows. Instead, he got left holding an empty bag.

Calling out Janibek Alimkhanuly and Osleys Iglesias was pure desperation to find someone with a pulse, but both routes were dead ends. Janibek has his own promotional mess and brings virtually no ticket sales or mainstream buzz to make the risk worthwhile for either side. Iglesias is a monster who punches like a mule and brings even less commercial appeal. Nobody with options wants to look in Adames’ direction because he is awkward, hits hard, possesses an iron chin, and cannot sell out an arena on his own name.

Now the WBC has boxed him into a corner. Instead of landing a lucrative unification or a recognizable name, Adames gets Meiirim Nursultanov. This is the classic who needs him scenario at its absolute worst. Nursultanov is a stone-cold Kazakh grinder with deep amateur seasoning who will make every second of every round physically miserable. If Adames wins a grueling decision, nobody outside the hardcore fanbase will care, and the casuals will not give him an ounce of credit. If he gets clipped or outpointed, his entire career plummets off a cliff.

Adames wanted the glory, the rematches, and the unifications. Instead, the boxing business did what it always does to guys without fanbases: shoved him into a basement fight against a dangerous mandatory where he has everything to lose and almost nothing to gain.

Sports.title: Gene Tunney Made Jack Dempsey Chase His Title
Sports.content:
Jack Dempsey’s left hook was most dangerous when he could weave inside and plant his feet. Gene Tunney spent their September 23, 1926, fight making both steps difficult. In the rain at Philadelphia’s Sesquicentennial Stadium, Tunney took the heavyweight championship by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Dempsey had not defended the title since his 1923 knockout of Luis Firpo. Tunney had remained active and had already fought Harry Greb five times. The layoff invited questions about Dempsey’s timing, but Tunney gave him an immediate, practical problem: getting close enough to throw with full force.

Tunney watched Dempsey come forward and met him with straight punches. A right hand on one of the champion’s early rushes showed the danger of lunging in without making Tunney give ground first. When Dempsey tried again, Tunney changed his position and made him start the attack over. The champion was still dangerous at close range, but he could rarely keep Tunney there.

The rain made the canvas slippery for both men. It is tempting to blame Dempsey’s trouble closing the distance on his footing, yet the wet ring did not stop Tunney from punching and repositioning. Tunney’s timing was the more visible obstacle: he caught Dempsey on the way in, then denied him the stationary target his hooks needed. Contemporary accounts described the fighters slipping on the canvas as the rain grew heavier.

Tunney also refused to spend ten rounds merely fleeing. He stood his ground when he had the opening, drove Dempsey back at times and worked his body as well as his head. Dempsey’s attacks came in bursts, followed by pauses while he searched for another way through. That gave Tunney repeated chances to regain the distance he wanted.

By the final round, Dempsey’s left eye was badly swollen and he was still trying to force his way inside. Tunney continued to meet him with punches. Referee Tommy Reilly and judges Mike Bernstein and Frank Brown awarded the challenger a clear decision.

Dempsey’s three year absence may have cost him sharpness. The fight cannot measure how much. What it showed was Tunney denying him a sustained attack for ten rounds. Dempsey never stopped trying to reach him; Tunney kept making him pay for the attempt.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Backs O’Shaquie Foster to Pressure Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley is picking O’Shaquie Foster to defeat Emanuel Navarrete, but the call comes attached to an urgent reality check. Foster cannot spend thirty-six minutes waiting around for an immaculate counterpunch. Navarrete throws volume in bundles, keeps men moving in reverse, and steals rounds from guys who are content to admire their own defense.

The two meet October 24 in San Antonio with three super featherweight titles on the line.

Navarrete brings an unorthodox, lunging assault that presents a massive trap. He leaps into wide hooks, throws uppercuts from his knees, and squares his stance right in the line of fire. Foster owns the hand speed to slice Navarrete down the middle while those feet are still airborne. The opening vanishes instantly if Foster retreats instead of planting his feet to fire.

“You ain’t getting no points for no damn defense,” Bradley said on his channel when detailing the habit Foster has of letting opponents throw punches without paying an immediate tax.

Foster cannot afford to tuck behind a high shell while Navarrete clubs away at his elbows and shoulders. Those heavy thuds count in the eyes of ringside officials, particularly in Texas, where aggressive punch output always gets rewarded. Foster already tasted that bitter lesson during his robbery loss against Robson Conceicao, where he landed the cleaner counters yet gave away the visual contest.

The real blueprint involves ripping straight to Navarrete’s midsection and forcing him to drag his feet in reverse. Navarrete lacks the balance or footwork to operate on his back foot, but Foster must put hands on him early to make that happen. If Foster surrenders ring real estate and searches for single counters, he hands Navarrete the exact grinder bout he wants.

Sitting back and relying on defense against Emanuel Navarrete as the B-side is professional suicide. Navarrete is an established ticket seller, a fan favorite, and an all-action Mexican slugger fighting in front of a heavily pro-Navarrete Texas crowd. Every time Navarrete unleashes an ugly four-punch flurry that bounces off Foster’s gloves and forearms, ten thousand people in the arena are going to scream as if someone just got dropped. Judges hear that roar, see the constant forward march, and instinctively score the round for the aggressor.

Foster’s biggest flaw is that he falls in love with making guys miss by an inch without making them pay for it. He treats the sweet science like an academic exercise where simply not getting hit clean is enough to bank three minutes. It is not. That exact minimalist habit burned him against Robson Conceicao in Newark, where Foster clearly outboxed the guy on pure contact quality, threw far too little, and watched the belts get handed to the man who simply looked busier.

The similarities between Foster and Shakur Stevenson expose the exact problem. Shakur gets away with his safety-first style because he commands ring generalship with an authoritative, southpaw lead hand that physically dictates the distance. Shakur controls the geography of the ring so thoroughly that his opponents stop throwing because they feel stupid missing. Foster does not control real estate that way. He retreats in straight lines, covers up, and lets his opponents dictate where the action takes place while he waits for a clean counter window.

Against an awkward buzzsaw who throws 80 punches a round from his knees, his hips, and odd ceiling angles, waiting for the perfect counter means giving away forty seconds of every minute. Navarrete’s punches are heavy and crude. Even when they land on the shoulders, they physically push a retreating fighter back.

Foster does not need to get reckless and swing for the fences, but he absolutely must stand his ground and fire first. If he allows Navarrete to initiate every single sequence and just tries to slip and counter in spurts, he will walk back to his corner after twelve rounds feeling like a master boxer, only to hear the ring announcer read out scores that send him home empty-handed.

Sports.title: Rocky Marciano’s Greatest Win Almost Got Away
Sports.content:
Jersey Joe Walcott was ahead on the scorecards when Rocky Marciano caught him with a right hand in the 13th round on September 23, 1952. That punch made Marciano heavyweight champion. Seventy-four years later, the rounds before it offer a better way to judge him than his perfect record alone.

Walcott knocked Marciano down in the first. He was the older man, but he was also the reigning champion, and his skill gave Marciano trouble deep into the fight. Marciano kept pressing until Walcott made one mistake he could punish. It took him nearly thirteen rounds to find it.

The familiar criticism is that Marciano beat aging champions. There is truth in the ages: Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his title, and Joe Louis was 37 when Marciano stopped him in 1951. Louis was past his best. Walcott’s age, though, does little to explain a fight he was winning before Marciano knocked him out. Marciano gets too much credit if every famous name on his record is treated as a prime opponent. He gets too little if the Walcott fight is dismissed by reading a birth date.

Their rematch lasted one round. Marciano’s next title defense, against Roland LaStarza, took eleven. LaStarza had pushed him to a split decision before Marciano won the championship; in their second meeting, Marciano stopped him. Ezzard Charles then took Marciano the full fifteen rounds before losing their first fight. Three months later, Charles badly cut Marciano’s nose in the rematch, but Marciano finished him in the eighth.

Marciano’s final opponent, light heavyweight champion Archie Moore, dropped him early. Marciano got up and knocked Moore out in the ninth round on September 21, 1955. He retired after that fight with six successful title defenses and a 49–0 record.

The record tells us Marciano never lost. The Walcott fight tells us something harder to capture in a number: he was hurt, behind, and still dangerous enough to change the result with one punch.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley’s Yoenli Hernandez Defense Heads to Purse Bid
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s first defense as WBO middleweight champion is headed toward the fight he hoped to delay. Talks with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez have failed, with a September 29 purse bid set to decide who stages the bout.

Bentley had a unification with IBF champion Aaron McKenna in reach. The WBO blocked it, ruling that its overdue mandatory obligation passed to Bentley when he was elevated to full champion. The sanctioning body also rejected a proposed title fight with Conor Benn. Bentley has the belt, but little freedom to choose what comes next.

Bentley has every reason to be frustrated. McKenna offered a UK fight with commercial appeal and, on paper, a more manageable opponent. Instead, he must face Hernandez, a highly regarded Cuban who brings far less name recognition and a serious risk of taking his belt. Bentley earned the interim title in the ring, but gained the full championship through elevation. If Hernandez beats him, there is no guarantee he finds another route to a world title. The McKenna unification and the bargaining power that comes with being champion would be gone.

Hernandez is a two-time amateur world champion, but Bentley has the deeper professional experience. He went twelve rounds with Janibek Alimkhanuly; Hernandez has yet to fight twelve as a professional. Bentley’s best chance is to close the distance with discipline, work to the body, and make Hernandez fight at a pace he cannot set himself entirely. Loading up on single punches would give the challenger time to move and score between Bentley’s attacks.

Hernandez’s August win over Francisco Daniel Veron offers a useful caution, though not a ready-made plan. Veron kept pressing and reached the final bell, but two judges gave Hernandez the fight by wide margins; the third scored it even. Pressure alone did not erase the Cuban’s cleaner work.

The purse bid adds another uncertainty. If a promoter outside Bentley’s camp wins, the champion may have to defend away from home. The WBO’s $200,000 minimum bid says where bidding starts, not what either fighter will earn.

Bentley wanted McKenna and a chance to add a second belt. Now he must beat Hernandez to keep the first one. For a champion who waited years for this position, that is a steep price for a fight with so little commercial upside.

Facing Yoenli carries massive tactical risk, but it remains the only move that preserves Bentley’s championship equity. Even if Hernandez outboxes him, Bentley at least collects a champion’s 75 percent purse bid share and goes down swinging with his career earnings maximized. If he vacates out of self-preservation, he surrenders the title for zero dollars, forfeits the McKenna unification anyway, and brands himself as a champion who ran from his mandatory.

In professional boxing, getting outpointed by a world-class Cuban amateur hurts, but surrendering the belt in a conference room without getting paid ruins a career far worse.

Without the WBO belt, Bentley reverts instantly to being a tough, high-risk, low-reward domestic gatekeeper. At thirty-one years old, clawing back up the sanctioning body rankings could take years, with no guarantee of ever receiving another title shot.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Questions WBA Future After Catterall Order
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez is sitting down with his management and legal team to figure out if he actually wants to keep the WBA in his plans moving forward. The sanctioning body just ordered him to defend his welterweight belt against mandatory challenger Jack Catterall, and the immediate reaction from Lopez’s camp tells you everything.

“NEWS: Teofimo Lopez’s team says 3 weeks ago Gilberto Mendoza personally assured them the Catterall fight wouldn’t be ordered & Lopez could pursue a bigger fight. He’ll meet with his managers, Keith Connolly & Mike Borao, & legal team to decide if he wants to allow the WBA to be part of his future plans. #boxing,” said Dan Rafael on X.

Teofimo has stopped short of saying he will drop the belt, yet the wording speaks volumes. If his side had any real desire to mix it up with Catterall, they would not be sitting around plotting an exit from the WBA system.

His camp claims WBA president Gilberto Mendoza promised them three weeks back that Catterall would get bypassed so Teofimo could chase a massive payday. Mendoza owes the public an answer on that. The official stance from the sanctioning body states that Teofimo inherited the mandatory commitment the moment he took the welterweight super title from Rolando Romero on August 22. Both camps have until October 22 to work out terms before purse bids enter the picture.

Stylistically, Catterall represents pure problems for Teofimo without offering a massive purse to justify the danger. The British contender works out of a disciplined southpaw stance, glides along the perimeter, controls distance with a sharp jab, and punishes aggressive mistakes. We watched Sandor Martin and Jamaine Ortiz give Teofimo fits simply by making him lead, refusing to trade inside the pocket, and circling away from his power. Catterall has the exact tools to drag Teofimo through another frustrating night.

The financial upside looks completely upside down. Dropping a decision to Catterall destroys any massive showdown with Ryan. Picking up a decision keeps the hardware but does not build extra hype for that blockbuster. If this saga goes to a purse bid, Matchroom holds the muscle to outbid Top Rank, take control of the promotion, and stick Teofimo on hostile territory.

The calendar is open for this defense anyway. Ryan is currently in talks to face Isaac Cruz, meaning Teofimo does not have to clear his schedule right this second to stay in position. That reality makes this summit with Connolly, Borao, and the attorneys look weak. Teofimo possesses a clear path to defend the belt, collect a win, and still secure Ryan down the road.

A champion cannot reasonably claim the title’s advantages while treating its mandatory challenger as an inconvenience to be removed.

Sports.title: Jacob Bank Gets Zhanibek Alimkhanuly Title Shot
Sports.content:
Jacob Bank protested when the WBO reinstated Zhanibek Alimkhanuly at the peak of its super middleweight rankings following a doping suspension. Now the sanctioning body has ordered Bank to trade punches with him for its vacant championship. The Danish contender possesses the exact opening he demanded, paired with the most dangerous opponent of his professional life.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri announced on X that both camps have fifteen days to finalize terms before purse bid proceedings take over. The formal written decree will surface shortly.

Bank previously insisted that gifting Alimkhanuly an immediate path to the belt cheated active contenders who climbed the rankings through merit. Accepting the match does not erase that criticism. It forces Bank to validate his complaints inside the ring.

A massive incentive exists for Danish boxing. Bank built a dedicated local following in Kolding, yet capturing a world belt would provide Denmark its first premier 168 pound titleholder since the Mikkel Kessler era. The jump in class remains extreme. Bank has never shared a ring with a world champion possessing Alimkhanuly’s southpaw timing, pedigree, and precision.

Alimkhanuly faces his own trial. He dominated at middleweight, but moving up eight pounds tests his punch resistance and speed against a naturally bigger man. If Bank absorbs the early fire, applies relentless pressure, and attacks the ribs along the ropes, he will expose how well the Kazakh fighter holds up across twelve rounds at 168 pounds. Marching forward behind an upright guard will get Bank wrecked by Alimkhanuly’s signature straight left and counter uppercuts.

Pacheco holds the number two ranking above Bank, yet Olivieri bypassed him entirely by labeling Bank the first available contender. Pacheco squares off against Darius Fulghum on November 14 on DAZN. That booking hints at calculated matchmaking from his handlers, choosing to protect his trajectory rather than jump straight into a bout against an avoided southpaw.

The WBO had no choice. Olivieri had to keep the belt moving once Sheeraz vacated, and Pacheco effectively took himself off the board. Bank might be a far less marketable name internationally, but he is doing what Pacheco chose not to do: taking the fight that actually tests him.

If the fifteen-day window expires without signatures, a purse bid determines who controls the ring, the location, and the network. A Top Rank bid takes Bank to America on ESPN, while local backing from promoter Kasper Holgersen could bring the event to Denmark. Bank complained about the sanctioning body cutting corners for Alimkhanuly. He now holds the contract to settle that dispute with his fists.

Ghana News.title: Tema-Kpone road had no valid contract or approved scope of work – Roads Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, says the absence of a valid contract and an approved scope of work has hampered the construction of the Tema-Kpone Junction road.

According to him, the project will be restructured and completed under the government’s Big Push initiative.

Speaking during a tour of Big Push projects in the Greater Accra Region, Mr Agbodza said the existing arrangement for the road had to be completely overhauled before work could proceed effectively.

“So the original scope, and perhaps the contract, will have to be completely overhauled. Whatever, I’m not sure if the contractor has got a valid contract. He said, let me hear. Do you have a valid contract? You don’t,” he said.

Mr Agbodza explained that although the contractor was already working on the road when President John Mahama assumed office, there was no approved contract or scope of work guiding the project.

He said this had created the impression among residents and businesses in the area that the contractor was simply not working or was not being paid.

The Minister said President Mahama has directed that the road from the TOR roundabout through the relevant section be completed as a concrete dual carriageway, while the stretch from Medina to the Kpone Barrier will also be completed.

“We are here today to first of all, through Urban Roads’ directive to you, resume full operations on the project, and we’ll cover the full cost of what we are going to do,” he said.

Mr Agbodza said the project has now been brought under the Big Push programme, with the government committed to ensuring its completion.

The Tema-Kpone road has been a major concern for commuters and heavy-duty vehicle operators, with its poor condition causing significant inconvenience.

Tanker drivers recently staged a sit-down strike to demand urgent government intervention over the state of the road.

Mr Agbodza also questioned the level of support from corporate institutions operating within the Tema industrial enclave towards improving road infrastructure in the area.

He noted that major companies such as VALCO and the Tema Oil Refinery operate around the area and benefit from the road network.

“Ghanaians and corporate citizens are happy to pay to extend electricity to their houses. They are happy to pay and extend water to their houses, but no one wants to pay extra money to extend road to wherever they are working,” he said.

Ghana News.title: You pay for electricity, water but not roads – Roads Minister chides Tema companies
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, has challenged corporate institutions operating in the Tema industrial enclave to contribute more towards the development of roads in the area.

He said that while companies and residents are willing to contribute financially to extend electricity and water services to their facilities and homes, there is little willingness to support road infrastructure.

Speaking during a tour of Big Push projects in the Greater Accra Region, Mr Agbodza said corporate institutions in Tema benefit significantly from infrastructure developed by the state and should also play a role in supporting road development.

“I have a few comments to make about the corporate citizens in Tema. Just yesterday we celebrated the birthday of President Nkrumah. Dr Nkrumah built Tema before every company here came to benefit,” he said.

The Minister added: “Ghanaians and corporate citizens are happy to pay to extend electricity to their houses. They are happy to pay and extend water to their houses, but no one wants to pay extra money to extend road to wherever they are working.”

His comments come amid concerns over the poor condition of the Tema-Kpone road, which has been a major source of difficulty for commuters and heavy-duty vehicle operators.

Tanker drivers recently staged a sit-down strike to demand urgent government intervention over the deteriorating road.

Mr Agbodza has said the road project will be restructured and completed under the government’s Big Push initiative.

Ghana News.title: Political independence earned under Nkrumah is being eroded – P.L.O Lumumba
Ghana News.content:
Renowned Pan-Africanist Professor P.L.O. Lumumba has warned that the political independence achieved by African countries during the era of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, is gradually being eroded by external economic and political influence.

Prof. Lumumba said that although African countries attained formal independence from colonial rule, many continue to face constraints that, in his view, limit their ability to make fully independent decisions.

Speaking on Joy Prime on September 23, on the legacy of Nkrumah, Prof. Lumumba argued that the former Ghanaian leader understood that political independence would remain vulnerable if it was not supported by economic independence and African unity.

He said Nkrumah had warned about the possibility of colonial influence returning in different forms after political independence.

“When Nkrumah said, first the political kingdom and the rest will be added unto you, he was clear that the neocoloniser would want to come back in subterranean ways,” Prof. Lumumba said.

He referenced Nkrumah’s book Neo-Colonialism: The Last Stage of Imperialism, arguing that the former president recognised the danger of African countries remaining divided and operating independently of one another.

“He is aware that if African countries remain disunited and continue to operate in silos, even the political independence would be undermined,” he said.

Prof. Lumumba questioned the depth of political independence in parts of Africa, arguing that the existence of national symbols and African-led governments does not necessarily amount to complete sovereignty.

“I am of the view that many African countries are only independent to the extent that they have flags, to the extent that they have national anthems, to the extent that they have black faces as presidents or ministers, but in truth, they are not,” he said.

He cited the influence of international financial institutions as part of his argument.

“Why? Because the IMF still tells us what to do. The World Bank still tells us what to do,” he said.

He also pointed to other areas in which he believes external influence remains significant, including currency systems and electoral processes.

“Our currencies are still printed outside of our countries. Our elections are still supervised by the neocolonisers,” Prof. Lumumba said.

Prof. Lumumba went further to describe some African countries as operating as “satellite states” of external powers.

“And we are fundamentally, in many ways, satellite states of the neocolonisers,” he said.

He argued that countries that attempt to pursue greater independence can face pressure to conform to existing international arrangements.

“In other words, it can be argued that even the political independence that we earned has been eroded and is being eroded by the day,” he said.

Linking independence to African unity

According to Prof. Lumumba, the issue cannot be separated from the question of African unity.

He said Nkrumah understood that Ghana’s independence was intended to serve as a platform for the liberation and integration of the wider continent.

“The Kwame Nkrumah wanted Ghana to be more than a nation-state. He wanted it to be a launching pad for African liberation and unity,” he said.

Prof. Lumumba argued that Africa’s continued political fragmentation makes it more difficult for individual countries to exercise collective influence on the global stage.

He also linked the continent’s political challenges to conflicts in countries including Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Cameroon.

“That is the reason why the question of governance is an issue that is alive and well in Africa,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Oro Oil CEO urges decentralised use of $500m World Bank oil palm fund
Ghana News.content:
Dr Maxwell Commey, Chief Executive Officer of Oro Oil Ghana Limited, has urged the government to prioritise smallholder farmers and community-level processing in deploying the US$500 million World Bank-supported Oil Palm Development Finance Window.

He said a decentralised approach would spread economic benefits, create jobs and promote inclusive growth, while strengthening Ghana’s palm oil value chain.

Dr Commey, a crude palm oil exporter with more than 27 years of industrial experience across Europe and Africa, said the financing presented an opportunity to expand production beyond large, centralised plantations.

He argued that a project involving more than 100,000 hectares of plantations and an estimated 300,000 jobs could not be concentrated in just two regions.

“Ghana’s palm oil sector is already largely smallholder-driven, accounting for the majority of fresh fruit bunches and a significant share of crude palm oil,” he said.

“The US$500 million World Bank facility, designed with long-term concessional financing and a focus on sustainable development, presents a historic opportunity to build on this foundation by decentralising production and processing.”

Dr Commey, a former two-term Board Member of the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA) and National Executive Member of the Oil Palm Development Association of Ghana (OPDAG), said the facility should support commercial viability, employment, smallholder inclusion and development across the value chain.

Proposes 70:30 funding allocation

Dr Commey proposed allocating 70% of the financing to existing mills, based on their capacity, and 30% to smallholder and outgrower schemes.

He said strengthening existing mills while supporting smaller producers would help expand processing capacity, improve smallholder incomes and create employment opportunities, particularly for women and rural youth.

The approach, he said, could stimulate economic activity across the Western, Central, Ashanti, Eastern, Volta and Oti regions, as well as parts of Bono East and Ahafo.

He added that decentralisation could accelerate implementation within the planned 10-year period by enabling stronger community partnerships and improving access to land for sustainable plantation development.

Other potential benefits, according to Dr Commey, include improved food security, reduced dependence on imported palm oil and lower foreign exchange pressures.

Processing fresh fruit bunches closer to farms could also reduce transportation costs and post-harvest losses while improving oil quality.

He said modern, energy-efficient local processing technologies, including biogas systems, could reduce smoke pollution and emissions, while improving yields on existing farmland.

A dispersed network of farmers and processors, he added, would also be more resilient to disruptions and support balanced regional development by keeping value addition within rural communities.

Financing can support mills and outgrower schemes

Dr Commey said the World Bank-backed facility, which he described as offering patient capital suited to oil palm’s long gestation period and support for up to 70% of project costs, could finance community mills, smallholder partnerships, rural infrastructure and cleaner processing technologies.

He also cited improved seedlings, mechanisation, credit and guaranteed offtake as forms of support that could strengthen the sector.

He said the approach aligned with the National Policy on Integrated Oil Palm Development, which seeks to expand sustainable production, create jobs and position Ghana as a regional palm oil hub.

“Large centralised plantations have their place, but history shows that well-supported smallholder and decentralised systems deliver broader livelihood gains and more inclusive growth,” he said.

“By channelling this World Bank financing towards decentralisation — paired with access to quality inputs, extension services, gender-inclusive associations, and transparent markets — we can unlock rural prosperity, strengthen supply chains, and move decisively towards self-sufficiency.”

Dr Commey called on the government, the TCDA, Development Bank Ghana and private-sector players to prioritise inclusive, decentralised models in deploying the facility.

He said Oro Oil Ghana Limited remained committed to sustainable palm oil production, stakeholder partnerships and national development.

About Oro Oil Ghana Limited

Oro Oil Ghana Limited is an integrated agro-industrial company specialising in oil palm cultivation and processing. The company, which describes itself as a multiple award-winning crude palm oil exporter, says it has created more than 300 direct and indirect jobs while advancing sustainable agro-industrial practices in the Eastern Region. It aims to become a leading sustainable palm oil producer in West Africa.

Ghana News.title: Busuama MA Basic School in crisis: 120 KG pupils stranded as teacher deficit bites
Ghana News.content:
The Busuama MA Basic School, located in the Kintampo North Municipality of the Bono East Region, is currently grappling with a critical shortage of teachers, a situation that is threatening the academic future of hundreds of children in the community and surrounding villages.

The school, which is the only educational facility serving Busuama and its neighbouring communities, now operates with just six teachers catering for pupils from Kindergarten through to the Junior High School level.

A school stretched to breaking point

The current staff distribution paints a grim picture of the challenges facing the school. Three teachers are responsible for Primary 1 to 6, while the remaining three handle Junior High School (JHS) 1 to 3 classes. Tragically, the Kindergarten, which accommodates more than 120 pupils, has no teacher at all.

Speaking to Joy News, the Headmaster of the school, Nawang Moses, disclosed that the situation was not always this dire. As of the last academic year, the school had a staff strength of nine teachers. However, three teachers were transferred without replacements, plunging the school into a severe teacher deficit.

“For the KG, we don't have a teacher at all. The teacher handling them was a volunteer teacher who had also left,” the headmaster lamented.

Primary and JHS levels also affected

The impact of the teacher shortage is not limited to the Kindergarten level. At the primary level, the three available teachers are forced to adopt a rotation system to cover all six classes, a situation that significantly compromises the quality of instruction.

At the JHS level, the three teachers are collectively responsible for teaching nine different subjects, a workload that is clearly unsustainable and is already reflected in the school's academic performance.

The headmaster noted that the situation is taking a toll on the school's overall academic output, as teachers are overstretched and unable to give each class the attention it deserves.

Furniture and learning materials also lacking

As if the teacher deficit were not enough, the school is also struggling with inadequate teaching and learning materials. The headmaster revealed that the lack of furniture for pupils is another major challenge, with the Kindergarten currently without chairs altogether.

“This is affecting the school's academic performance,” Mr Nawang added, appealing to the government, non-governmental organisations and benevolent individuals to come to the aid of the school.

A community's future at stake

The Busuama MA Basic School serves as the only hope for education for children in Busuama and its neighbouring villages. With the current state of affairs, parents and community members fear that the future of these children hangs in the balance.

The situation at Busuama is a stark reminder of the challenges facing rural education in Ghana, where inadequate teacher deployment and a lack of basic infrastructure continue to undermine efforts to provide quality education for all.

A call for urgent intervention

The headmaster and the community are appealing to the Ministry of Education, the Ghana Education Service, the Kintampo North Municipal Assembly and benevolent organisations to intervene urgently.

They are calling for the immediate posting of teachers, particularly for the Kindergarten, as well as the provision of furniture and teaching and learning materials to restore the school to a functional state.

For now, the more than 120 Kindergarten pupils of Busuama MA Basic School continue to wait, their futures uncertain, as the community prays for help to arrive before it is too late.

Ghana News.title: Churches are not exempt from paying music royalties – GHAMRO CEO
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Music Rights Organisation (GHAMRO), Jackson Brefo, says churches are required to pay royalties for songs they use during church services.

Speaking to Kwame Dadzie on Joy FM’s Showbiz A-Z, he said the law considers churches as users of music and does not exempt them from royalty obligations.

“The law is not biased towards any entity. There is no mention of church in the law but it says that a person who intends to use the work of an author or causes the work of an author to be performed in public.

“There is a portion for fair use and that mentions educational purposes. The law never mentions churches,” he said.

Asked whether churches were complying with the payment of royalties, Mr Brefo said the orthodox denominations were the most compliant.

“Some of the orthodox churches are compliant. The bit of difficulty we face is the ‘up and coming’ charismatic and Pentecostal churches. With the orthodox churches, we are trying our best. Church of Pentecost being compliant, Assemblies of God, Methodist,” he said.

Jackson further noted that if churches are encouraged to pay their royalties promptly, it will help increase the revenue share of gospel music royalties.

Against this background, he urged gospel musicians to impress upon churches to fulfil the obligation.

This is not the first time GHAMRO has admonished the Christian community over the payment of royalties.

In July 2017, then Chairman of the organisation, Rex Owusu Marfo, popularly known as Rex Omar, said they were preparing measures to make churches pay royalties for music they used.

“Yes, we are considering that. We are putting in place the necessary measures to let churches pay royalties because they also use musicians’ intellectual property,” he made the comment at a workshop.

The issue resurfaced in March 2020, when Rex, again argued that churches should be licensed and billed for copyrighted music used during services.

Section 37(2) of the Copyright Act, 2005 (Act 690), provides that “an owner of copyright is entitled to collect royalties for the live performance of the copyright work or for the public performance of the recorded copyright work.”

GHAMRO is a collective management organisation responsible for administering the rights of music rightsholders in Ghana. Its mandate includes licensing music users, collecting royalties on behalf of rightsholders and distributing those royalties.

Ghana News.title: Gender Ministry expresses condolences over death of child in Cantonments fire
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP) has expressed its condolences to the family of a young girl who died in a fire incident at Cantonments in Accra on Sunday, September 20.

In a statement issued by the Public Affairs Unit of the MoGCSP on Wednesday, September 23, the Ministry said it shared in the grief of the bereaved family and others affected by the incident.

It also used the incident to urge parents, guardians and caregivers to take practical steps to protect children from potential hazards at home and in other environments.

The Ministry advised households to keep matches, lighters and other sources of fire out of children's reach, while ensuring that electrical appliances and installations are safe.

It further cautioned against situations where young children may be left unattended.

“Households are also encouraged to observe basic fire safety measures, have emergency evacuation arrangements in place and, where age-appropriate, teach children what to do in the event of an emergency,” the Ministry said.

The Ministry said the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

It urged that the investigation be completed and the cause of the fire established.

“This, the Ministry believes, will help provide clarity on the circumstances of the tragedy and inform measures to prevent similar incidents in the future,” it said.

The statement did not disclose further details about the circumstances leading to the fire or the identity of the deceased child.

The Ministry stressed that protecting children from harm requires the involvement of families, caregivers, communities and relevant institutions.

“Child protection remains a shared responsibility. Families, caregivers, communities and relevant institutions all have a role to play in identifying risks, promoting safe environments and taking timely action to protect children from harm,” the Ministry stated.

The MoGCSP also extended its sympathies to the bereaved family, wishing them strength and comfort as they come to terms with the loss.

Ghana News.title: Nkrumah foresaw Africa’s vulnerability without unity – P.L.O. Lumumba
Ghana News.content:
Renowned Pan-Africanist and anti-corruption crusader Professor P.L.O. Lumumba has said Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah foresaw that Africa’s failure to unite would leave the continent vulnerable to domination, humiliation and external influence.

According to Prof. Lumumba, Nkrumah possessed exceptional foresight and understood as far back as the 1960s that a fragmented Africa would struggle to protect its interests and address challenges affecting its people.

Speaking in an interview with JoyPrime’s Israel Laryea, Prof. Lumumba said Nkrumah’s vision remained relevant as the continent continued to grapple with conflicts, humanitarian crises and other challenges.

“Nkrumah would have been celebrating his 117th year and what one must remember about the Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah is that he had the foresight of a prophet,” he said.

He said Nkrumah recognised that an Africa without meaningful unity would be vulnerable to domination and undermining by external forces.

“He was able to see an Africa that was not united would be dominated, would be undermined, would be humiliated, and I dare say if you look at all the critical sectors of human relations, Africa is being dominated, Africa is being humiliated, and Africa is being disregarded,” Prof. Lumumba said.

Prof. Lumumba argued that Africa could have been in a different position today had the continent and the wider international community paid greater attention to Nkrumah’s call for African unity.

He said the former Ghanaian leader envisaged a strong Africa capable of contributing meaningfully to global affairs while protecting the interests and dignity of its people.

“If Africa would have listened to Kwame Nkrumah, if only the world would have listened to Kwame Nkrumah that you needed a strong African… it would be different,” he said.

The Pan-Africanist said Nkrumah’s concerns about the consequences of division had become particularly evident in the area of peace and security.

He pointed to the numerous conflicts on the continent, arguing that they continue to undermine peace and create humanitarian situations that African countries often struggle to resolve.

“As we talk now, there are almost 40 conflicts in the continent of Africa which undermine peace, which creates humanitarian situations which cannot be handled by Africans,” he said.

Prof. Lumumba stressed that Nkrumah had anticipated such difficulties decades ago.

“The Osagyefo had foreseen that as early as the 1960s,” he added.

His comments form part of renewed reflections on Nkrumah’s Pan-African legacy as Ghana commemorates what would have been the former President’s 117th birthday.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: UEFA’s Ceferin says FIFA trust still broken after Infantino investment row
World.content:
UEFA president speaks for the first time since FIFA said it would review its decision-making, says trust still broken.

Share UEFA’s Ceferin says FIFA trust still broken after Infantino investment row on social media

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin says trust in world football has not ⁠been restored following the collapse of FIFA’s controversial private investment plan.

The remarks, made in a video address to the ⁠Portugal Football Summit on Wednesday, were Ceferin’s first public comments since FIFA president Gianni Infantino offered a review of the governing body’s decision-making.

Ceferin said unity, transparency and governance that served the wider game were essential to maintaining trust in football. “Yet not everyone places the game above their own ambitions.”

“Trust in our sport rests on three pillars: unity, transparency, and governance that serves the many, not the few. ‌In recent times, all three were disregarded by people who had sworn to protect them.

“The project that shattered the unity of world football may be abolished, but the trust it broke has not returned, and repairing it is our work now.”

Ceferin did not name Infantino or FIFA, but his comments were an apparent reference to the abandoned proposal to sell a 20 percent stake in FIFA’s commercial rights, including the World Cup, to private investors. The plan ⁠was dropped in July after fierce opposition from UEFA, the Asian Football ⁠Confederation and the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF).

“Football is not for sale,” Ceferin said. “That is the message UEFA has carried for years, and I’m certain this summit will carry it further.”

His intervention came two days after Infantino sought to address the fallout in a letter ⁠to the FIFA Council and the presidents of all 211 member associations.



He said he would ask the council whether it wanted to commission an ⁠independent external review of FIFA’s governance framework for major strategic initiatives ⁠and proposed consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders on strengthening its decision-making processes.

He said any review could examine the roles of the president, bureau, council and congress and ways to improve transparency and accountability.

The letter has so far failed ‌to win over several federations that had criticised Infantino over the investment proposal.

Infantino has said he remains fully committed to leading FIFA and is expected to seek another term at the presidential ‌election ‌in March 2027.

Ceferin said those running the sport needed to remember whom they served.

“The game will remain safe if those who govern it remember whom they govern it for,” he said.

World.title: Qatar on mediation efforts: ‘We can’t let diplomacy fail’
World.content:
NewsFeed Qatar on mediation efforts: ‘We can’t let diplomacy fail’

Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari has told Al Jazeera his country is determined to make diplomacy work to end the US-Iran conflict. On Tuesday Qatar oversaw the first meeting between the US and Iran in months, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

World.title: China’s swimming prodigy Yu Zidi bags third gold in Asian Games record
World.content:
The 13-year-old beat the previous 400m Asian Games record, set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014, by about 4.5 seconds.

China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi has completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years before the Los Angeles Olympics.

The schoolgirl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4 minutes 28.56 seconds (04:28.56) on Wednesday to make it a clean sweep of her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in games-record times.

She beat the previous 400m games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by approximately 4.5 seconds.

It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.

With the next Olympics two years away, Yu is shaping up to be a major medal contender at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

Last year, she became the youngest medallist at the World Aquatics Championships, where she won bronze for China’s relay team at the age of 12, and has since been earmarked for success in the swimming world.

At the same championship, Yu finished fourth by a small margin in three individual events.

In March, the teen sensation built on her growing reputation with a 200m butterfly victory over seven-time American Olympic medallist Regan Smith at the China Swimming Open.

At the Asian Games, Yu has dominated the pool and showed another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m individual medley, where she took the lead from the start and finished 3.95 seconds clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.



In addition to grabbing international headlines, Yu has become a sensation at home following her Asian Games exploits.

The story of her introduction to competitive swimming after being spotted by a coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, has gone viral on local social media platforms.

At the games, Yu was asked by the media whether answering questions was the hardest part of competing. She replied, with a giggle: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

World.title: Powerful El Nino could cause more than 450,000 deaths, scientists say
World.content:
Heaviest toll expected in poorer countries, already struggling with food insecurity and high energy costs, report says.

Share Powerful El Nino could cause more than 450,000 deaths, scientists say on social media

More than 450,000 people are projected to die from additional heat due to the unusually strong El Nino event over the next six months, according to a research report.
