The session followed participants’ immersion at the Dangote Refinery and used the Dangote industrial experience as a practical case through which to examine the cost and tenor of capital, infrastructure and logistics constraints, development finance, backward integration, technology and talent, institutional capacity, capital markets and the discipline required to translate ambition into enduring enterprise.

Contributors included Zouera Youssoufou, MD/CEO, Aliko Dangote Foundation; Innocent C. Ike, Group CEO, Access Holdings; Obeahon Ohiwerei, Managing Director/CEO, Coronation Merchant Bank; Adebayo Adewolu, CEO, Trium; Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/CEO, NGX Group; Chuka Eseka, Group Managing Director/CEO, Vetiva Capital Management; David Bird, Managing Director, Dangote Refinery; Kola Karim, Chairman, Shoreline Natural Resources; and Adesuwa Okunbo Rhodes, Founder & Managing Partner, Aruwa Capital Management, alongside other leaders from business, investment and development finance.

A central theme of the discussions was how Africa can move from episodic examples of extraordinary scale to a more repeatable model of capital formation and institution-building, including deeper domestic capital markets, greater mobilisation of pension, insurance, sovereign and private capital, and stronger pathways from concentrated private ownership to broader institutional and public participation.

Speaking during the engagement, Aig-Imoukhuede said:

“Vision attracts capital, governance maintains capital, and execution by great talent compounds capital. All three must be present for an institution to endure.”

Reflecting on the cohort’s visit to the Dangote Refinery, Aig-Imoukhuede described the project as an example of the scale of ambition and execution possible on the continent:

“My dilemma as an African is that for the continent to realise its potential, vision, governance, and execution must happen repeatedly across several nations at the same time. It cannot remain episodic. We cannot wait 20 years between mega-projects. Furthermore, we must fix our greatest handicap, learning how to successfully transfer great visions and institutions from one generation to the next without restarting from the bottom.”

He also called for Africa’s financial architecture to extend across the full yield curve, connecting shorter-term commercial financing with the long-tenor institutional capital required to fund businesses and infrastructure across generations.

Reflecting on the purpose of the programme, Zouera Youssoufou noted that developing visionary leadership and expanding Africa’s capital ecosystems are fundamental to the continent’s long-term prosperity.

The discussions reinforced that Africa’s challenge is not a shortage of ambition or entrepreneurial capacity, but the need to strengthen the capital, institutional and operating systems that enable ambitious enterprises to reach scale and endure.

Closing his remarks with a challenge to the Young Global Leaders, Aig-Imoukhuede said:

“We know that figures like Aliko Dangote are rare, but all of you must be game changers. With the intellect, network and courage you possess, there are no excuses. You share the mantle of responsibility to carry these principles forward and build the enduring institutions Africa requires.”

The Finance and Investment engagement formed part of the wider ADF/WEF YGL Africa-Diaspora Leadership Programme, bringing together current and former Young Global Leaders and senior African decision-makers to examine practical models for building and sustaining African enterprises at scale.

World.title: ‘She’s healing’: Rachel Kolisi’s ‘Miss Independent’ video goes viral
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi, the ex-wife of Springboks captain Siya Kolisi, sang along to Ne-Yo’s hit song Miss Independent in a viral video that racked up close to six million views on social media.

RACHEL KOLISI SINGS ALONG TO ‘MISS INDEPENDENT’ GOES VIRAL

Director, author and motivational speaker Rachel Kolisi, shared a video of herself at an event, where she sang along to Ne-Yo’s hit song Miss Independent. In the video, Rachel’s name is seen at the back of the screen as the keynote speaker. She confidently sang and danced in front of the audience, capturing the attention of many social media users as the video currently has 2.9 million views on TikTok and 3.1 million on Instagram. Take a look…

Rachel is often travelling around the country for her Falling Forward Foundation, which she started after she stepped down from The Kolisi Foundation. Siya and Rachel co-founded The Kolisi Foundation together in 2020. Falling Forward is branded as a movement for women choosing courage, resilience and growth. Rachel has released both a documentary and a book through Falling Forward.



SOCIAL MEDIA USERS REACT TO VIDEO

Many social media users noticed Rachel’s confidence and thought she was healing from the divorce.

“She’s healing bafazi angith we all love it for her right 🥺🥺🥺,” wrote Kwandoh.

“That glow..is not from a skin routine..it’s straight from your soul 😻,” wrote Chaz.



“Yasss queen 🥰🤎 Love this energy 🔥🤌🏾,” wrote @precioustheplanner.

“Oh she’s glowing!!!😍,” wrote @noxx_zondi.

While others picked on her singing Miss Independent while keeping the Kolisi surname.



“Miss Independent… Last name ‘Kolisi’ okay,” wrote Nkaisana_m.

“Why she kept his surname?” wrote Keegan.

Rachel previously addressed this in an interview with 947FM, stating that she kept her surname because of her kids. The author and director has two kids – Nicholas (12) and Keziah (9) with Siya.



“My children share the same surname as me, and travelling with my children, because they are brown, is already a big challenge. Sometimes I get stopped at gates and people want to double-check certain things, so it would be a really big challenge for me, so I’m keeping my surname,” she said.

World.title: RIP | WATCH: Traffic officer dies after state vehicle catches fire
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal traffic officer Timothy Simpson died after the state vehicle he was travelling in caught fire on the N2 near Park Rynie. Image: Rising Sun Chatsworth

Traffic officer Timothy Simpson died inside the state-owned vehicle after it caught fire on the N2 near Park Rynie on Tuesday night, 22 September.

Simpson served as a provincial inspector with the KwaZulu-Natal Road Traffic Inspectorate (RTI) and was based at Park Rynie.

The vehicle became engulfed in flames at about 20:00 while Simpson was on duty.



Investigation launched into deadly vehicle fire

KwaZulu-Natal Transport and Human Settlements MEC Siboniso Duma confirmed Simpson’s death on Wednesday.

Duma said the department had assigned an RTI team to work with a specialised South African Police Service (SAPS) team to establish what happened.

Investigators are examining forensic and mechanical evidence from the vehicle to determine what sparked the fire.

Authorities have not yet confirmed the cause.

Duma has expressed his deepest condolences to the family and colleagues of the most disciplined, hardworking, decorated, and award… pic.twitter.com/iEuyh61Iny — NANCY PALIEN (@Traffic247KZN) September 23, 2026

RTI spokesperson Sindi Msimang said Simpson was alone in the vehicle when the fire broke out.



She said he could not get out before the flames engulfed the vehicle.

“We hope to get answers soon on how this happened,” Msimang said, adding that the RTI would await the outcome of the SAPS investigation.

Traffic officer remembered for his service

Duma described Simpson as a disciplined and hardworking officer who served KwaZulu-Natal and the country with distinction.

He said Simpson was also an award-winning traffic officer.

The department sent officials to Simpson’s family after the incident and senior management was expected to meet his colleagues at the Park Rynie RTI station on Wednesday.

Duma also extended condolences to Simpson’s wife, family, friends and colleagues.

Police and transport officials are continuing their investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal fire.

World.title: Mass shootings in SA: Over 100 killed in a year of deadly attacks
World.content:
Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township on Tuesday, opening fire on 14 people. Image: SAPS/ Facebook

At least 11 people were killed during a mass shooting on Tuesday night, after gunmen opened fire at a house party in KwaMakhutha, south of Durban.

The latest attack brings renewed attention to a string of high-casualty mass shootings across South Africa over the past year.

Police said three men entered a house in the Ziko area shortly before 23:00 and opened fire on 14 people. Ten victims, including a woman believed to be pregnant, died at the scene.



Four people were taken to hospital. One later died, while three others survived with injuries. No arrests had been made by Wednesday morning.

The motive for the attack has not yet been confirmed. However, SAPS said some of the victims were known to Crime Intelligence in connection with suspected illegal activities.

“Although the motive of the shooting cannot be confirmed yet, a feud between rival groupings cannot be ruled out,” police said.

Mass shooting attacks across South Africa

The KwaMakhutha shooting follows several other devastating attacks at taverns and residential properties that resulted in mass casualties.

In December, 12 people were killed and 13 injured when gunmen stormed an illegal tavern inside the Saulsville hostel in Pretoria.

Two weeks later, nine people were killed and 10 injured at a tavern in Bekkersdal. At the time, acting Gauteng Premier Jacob Mamabolo condemned the “escalation in mass shootings that have occurred in the province.”



In January, nine people were killed at a tavern in Marikana, Philippi East in Cape Town. Police and prosecutors later linked the case to alleged extortion.

Other high-casualty attacks occurred at a Bronkhorstspruit tavern, a house in Philippi East, a Mayville tavern in Durban and a residence in Kwadwesi, Gqeberha.

The incidents have also extended beyond taverns and homes.

In June, 13 people were eventually confirmed dead after gunmen opened fire across the Jumpers informal settlement in Cleveland, Johannesburg. Fourteen others were injured.

Western Cape police have separately raised concern over repeated mass shootings in Cape Town, while authorities in other provinces have also warned about illegal firearms, organised crime and gang violence.

Schools and gang-related shootings

The past year has also seen deadly shootings that aren’t linked to taverns and residential properties.

In January, three teachers were killed and another wounded when a former deputy principal opened fire at Ntabankulu Primary School in the Eastern Cape.

Cape Town has also experienced numerous mass shootings that police have described as suspected gang-related attacks. These include repeated incidents and drive-by shootings in Philippi East, Delft, Khayelitsha, Langa and other Cape Flats communities.

The incidents do not share a single confirmed motive. Police investigations have variously examined extortion, gang conflict, illegal mining, taxi violence and other forms of organised crime.

Mass shootings with four or more fatalities: 23 September 2025 – 23 September 2026

World.title: Stormers celebrate the homecoming of superstars
World.content:
The Stormers have bolstered their ranks with the signing of flanker Siya Kolisi, winger Cheslin Kolbe and tighthead prop Wilco Louw following spells with the Sharks, Tokyo Sungoliath and the Bulls respectively.

In addition, Haashim Pead – the Player of the Tournament at the 2025 World Rugby Junior World Championship – has signed a four-year deal with the Stormers.

The 21-year-old was called up to a Springbok senior alignment camp and featured for South Africa A against Zimbabwe earlier this season.



Director of Rugby John Dobson said Pead’s profile was the perfect fit for the squad as part of Project 2029, which seeks to position Stormers Rugby as one of the top global rugby clubs on and off the field.

“Haashim is a rising star and as a local lad who fits our game model perfectly, it made sense on every level for us to bring him back to Cape Town.

“He is a gifted athlete who has an incredibly high ceiling, and we look forward to seeing how he develops here with us.



“This is a four-year deal, so there is a big commitment from both ourselves and Haashim to Project 2029 and our goals as a club,” he added.

Stormers making moves

Meanwhile, captain Ruhan Nel said there was good reason for the Cape Town-based outfit to go into the new season full of confidence.

“It’s pretty well documented about their abilities as rugby players, but I think if you look at the humans we are getting back into our system, that’s actually the thing that stands out the most for me,” said the veteran centre.



“I had the pleasure of playing Sevens with Cheslin in a couple of tournaments and he is exactly the same guy now as what he was back then and I think that speaks volumes of his character.

“We know Siya for the character he is and the impact he has on the people of South Africa and I know Wilco as well.

“For me, the more better people you can get in the environment, I just believe you will have better rugby players as well.



“We have got three very big guys coming back, also three Stormers men. It’s very exciting.

“Apart from what they are bringing on the field physically, just the type of humans we are going to have in the environment is also a massive contribution to us.”

Adding his thoughts, Director of Rugby John Dobson said: “They are all multiple season Stormers. So there’s a sense of a homecoming.



“We offered all our Springboks a week off next month and not one of those three guys took up that right which is fantastic.

“It shows their commitment to the Stormers that they wanted to play every game.”

High calibre players

Dobson went on to speak about all three players individually.



On double World Cup-winning Springboks skipper Kolisi, he said: “He’s already thoroughly invested.

“He’s a guy we’d look at in all positions in the back row.

“We’ve got three guys that have played six for South Africa this year in Siya, Deon Fourie and Paul de Villiers.



“With the way Siya has grown physically, he could play seven and eight for us as well.”

As for Louw, who started all four Tests in the recent Greatest Rivalry series against New Zealand, he said: “Just seeing the damage he is doing on the world stage now, he’s a massive acquisition for us.”

Kolbe, who passed 50 caps this summer, will have a delayed start to the campaign after suffering a broken jaw against the All Blacks in Johannesburg three weeks ago.



Dobson said: “It’s a bit of a blow that Cheslin won’t play the October matches because we have been a bit light on the wings over the last season or two.

“It’s a blow he’s out for four weeks, but he’s got a long season after that.

“He’s massive for us in terms of what he brings as a player and to the community.”

World.title: SASSA confirms grant payment dates for October to December
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries now have confirmed payment dates for the final three months of 2026, giving millions of South Africans the opportunity to plan ahead for the festive season. Image: Facebook @SASSANewsZA

SASSA beneficiaries now have confirmed payment dates for the final three months of 2026, giving millions of South Africans the opportunity to plan ahead for the festive season.

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) pays Older Persons Grants first, followed by Disability Grants and then Children’s Grants.

The final three months of the 2026 payment calendar are as follows:



Month Older Persons Disability Children’s October Friday, 2 October Monday, 5 October Tuesday, 6 October November Tuesday, 3 November Wednesday, 4 November Thursday, 5 November December Wednesday, 2 December Thursday, 3 December Friday, 4 December

October SASSA payments

The next major payment cycle begins with the Older Persons Grant on Friday, 2 October.

Disability Grant beneficiaries will receive their payments on Monday, 5 October, followed by Children’s Grant beneficiaries on Tuesday, 6 October.

SASSA has also allocated a fourth payment day in October for certain beneficiaries whose grants are subject to review or eLife certification. This falls on Wednesday, 7 October.

November grants

The November payment cycle begins on Tuesday, 3 November, when Older Persons Grant beneficiaries are scheduled to receive their money.

Disability Grant payments follow on Wednesday, 4 November, with Children’s Grants paid on Thursday, 5 November.

The final major grant payment cycle of the year starts on Wednesday, 2 December, when Older Persons Grant beneficiaries are scheduled to be paid.



Disability Grant beneficiaries will receive their payments on Thursday, 3 December, while Children’s Grants are scheduled for Friday, 4 December.

Why SASSA payments are staggered

SASSA uses a staggered payment system to help manage demand and reduce congestion at payment points.

Beneficiaries should also remember that they do not have to withdraw their money on the day it is paid.

Once the grant has been deposited, the money remains available in the beneficiary’s account.

This means beneficiaries can choose when to access their funds rather than rushing to a payment point on the scheduled payment date.

How much will SASSA beneficiaries receive?

Following the grant increases introduced in April 2026, the main grant amounts are:

Older Persons Grant: R2 400

R2 400 Disability Grant: R2 400

R2 400 Care Dependency Grant: R2 400

R2 400 War Veterans Grant: R2 420

R2 420 Foster Child Grant: R1 290

R1 290 Child Support Grant: R580

The SRD grant remains separate from the permanent social grant payment schedule.

The R370 Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant has individual payment dates rather than following the three-day payment cycle.

Beneficiaries receiving the SRD grant should check their personal SASSA status for their specific payment date.

With the final three payment cycles of the year now confirmed, beneficiaries can plan their household budgets around their respective payment dates – particularly with the December festive season approaching.

World.title: How many public holidays are left in South Africa in 2026?
World.content:
Heritage Day (24 September) is among us and unfortunately, this is one of the last public holidays before December. How many public holidays are left in 2026?

HOW MANY PUBLIC HOLIDAYS LEFT IN 2026?

South Africa has 12 official public holidays that were expected in 2026 according to the Public Holidays Act. As it stands today (23 September), nine public holidays have officially past. New Year’s Day kicked off the public holidays for the year on 1 January, followed by Human Rights Day on 21 March (which landed on a Saturday, so no bonus Monday off).

The Easter long weekend had Good Friday and Family Day on 3 and 6 April then in the same month, Freedom Day on 27 April. Many made this an extra long weekend as Workers’ Day was on 1 May. Youth Day on 16 June, and National Women’s Day on 9 August, which fell on a Sunday. So, Monday 10 August was observed as a public holiday too.



So how many public holidays left for 2026?

Heritage Day : Thursday, 24 September.

: Thursday, 24 September. Day of Reconciliation : Wednesday, 16 December.

: Wednesday, 16 December. Christmas Day : Friday, 25 December.

: Friday, 25 December. Day of Goodwill falls on Saturday 26 December. Unfortunately workers won’t get an extra day off as this falls on a Saturday this year.

falls on Saturday 26 December. Unfortunately workers won’t get an extra day off as this falls on a Saturday this year. There is also an “extra” public holiday for this year. President Cyril Ramaphosa has officially declared Wednesday, 4 November an additional public holiday for South Africa, giving voters the day off to take part in the country’s local government elections.

This means that there area a total of five public holidays left for this year.

THE ‘EXTRA’ PUBLIC HOLIDAY FOR 2026

The declaration follows the formal gazetting and proclamation of 4 November 2026 as the election date by Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Velenkosini Hlabisa in August 2026. Ramaphosa first announced the election date on 30 April 2026, at the Birchwood Hotel in Boksburg, during discussions at the Extended Presidential Coordinating Council meeting.



At the time, he stated that as the local government elections were due in 2026, the date “should be held on a Wednesday, which is the middle of the week,” settling on 4 November 2026.

World.title: 48-hour water shutdown planned across parts of Durban
World.content:
A major Southern Aqueduct shutdown is planned for Durban next week. Image: canva / file

Residents and businesses across parts of Durban are being warned of a planned 48-hour interruption to the water supply next week.

The water shutdown will run from 06:00 on Tuesday, 29 September, until 06:00 on Thursday, 1 October 2026.

The interruption is required for construction and tie-in work on the Southern Aqueduct pipeline in Westville.



The work forms part of the City’s Southern Aqueduct Pipeline Upgrade Project and will affect parts of the Inner West, Central and South regions.

Why is the water being shut off?

The shutdown will allow contractors to construct and connect two major connection chambers in Westville as part of Work Package 6 of the project.

The Southern Aqueduct upgrade is being completed in several work packages.

Work Packages 1, 2 and 3 have already been completed and commissioned, while Work Packages 4, 5 and 6 remain under construction.

Once completed, the project is expected to strengthen the City’s bulk water network and reduce the risk of unplanned failures, water losses and lengthy interruptions caused by emergency repairs to ageing infrastructure.

The upgraded network will reportedly serve approximately 1.2 million people.



Which Durban areas will be affected?

The affected areas span the Pinetown South, Central and South regions.

World.title: Tsakane Matlala, two others granted bail in lease-fraud case
World.content:
PRETORIA - The wife of alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala, Tsakane, and two other co-accused have been granted bail in a lease-fraud case.

Tsakane appeared in the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court on Thursday alongside her husband, Matlala, Given Makofane and Claudette Masethe.

Tsakane, Makofane and Masethe were granted R20,000 bail, the State opposed bail only for Matlala.

The three were arrested on Tuesday by the Gauteng Political Killings Task Team in connection with an allegedly fraudulent lease agreement.

They are accused of falsifying bank statements to help Matlala secure a R95,000 lease agreement for a property in Waterkloof. Matlala allegedly applied for the lease using an eSwatini identity document.

The matter was postponed to 29 October for further investigation. Matlala is expected to bring an application for bail on 14 and 15 October.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Madlanga Commission continues
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Madlanga Commission continues to probe the murky links between the taxi industry, the alleged Big Five cartel, and political figures.

On Tuesday, attention turns to taxi boss Bafana Oupa Sindane, who is expected to take the stand and face questions about the industry’s alleged networks and connections.

ALSO READ | New deadline for Madlanga Commission

Sindane’s testimony follows that of his associate and fellow taxi boss, Joe “Ferrari” Sibanyoni.

Sibanyoni has denied having links to corrupt police officers or hiring hitmen. However, during his testimony, he acknowledged having what he described as brotherly relationships with some police officers.

Sindane and Sibanyoni are also co-accused in an extortion and money-laundering case.

World.title: Oil prices fall after Trump hails 'good' talks with Iran
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Oil prices fell on Wednesday after President Donald Trump said US and Iranian representatives had met for "very good" talks at the United Nations.

International benchmark Brent crude and main US contract West Texas Intermediate were below the symbolic $100 mark that has been repeatedly breached since the Middle East war began in February.

Brent hit $99.30 and WTI lowered to $89.93 per barrel in afternoon Asian trading.

Trump told reporters the three-hour US-Iran meeting was "very good", "very productive" and "they have another one scheduled in the very near future".

The US leader's statements came just hours after he delivered a bellicose address to the UN, saying he faced a "big decision" on whether to make a deal with Iran or "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly".

Nearly seven months after US-Israeli strikes triggered war, the foes are at an impasse, with Iran keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed and the United States enforcing a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Conflict between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen has enveloped the kingdom, squeezing energy exports from the Red Sea.

"The three-hour US-Iran meeting matters because it shifts the market from pure escalation pricing toward a genuine diplomatic process, even if a final deal still looks distant," said Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

Trump has pledged that oil would come down "as soon as" the United States wins the war.

The dip in oil prices came as the world's biggest crude exporter Saudi Arabia reportedly rebooted operations along its East-West Pipeline -- a crucial oil export route shut down by drone attacks.

The kingdom is aiming to resume exports later this week, Bloomberg quoted a source as saying.

But while Saudi oil giant Aramco reportedly told Asian refiners they could soon pick up crude from the Red Sea port of Yanbu, the firm told their European counterparts they will not be allocated oil in October, Bloomberg said.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Mapisa-Nqakula’s corruption trial continues
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula is expected to face tougher questions in court on Wednesday as her corruption trial continues.

The state has this week focused on her relationship with contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu and a series of payments allegedly linked to Mapisa-Nqakula’s former secretary.

Mapisa-Nqakula has admitted making several payments but told the court she cannot remember exactly what they were for.

The proceedings have also heard allegations that the former Speaker requested R150,000 from Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu.

According to the evidence before the court, the money was allegedly intended to find someone to care for Mapisa-Nqakula’s father.

World.title: KZN traffic inspector killed in vehicle fire on N2
World.content:
DURBAN - A KwaZulu-Natal Road Traffic Inspector has died after a state-owned vehicle he was travelling in caught fire while he was on duty along the N2 freeway in Park Rynie on the South Coast.

The incident happened at around 8pm on Tuesday, when the vehicle was engulfed in flames.

The officer was unable to escape and was declared dead at the scene.

The circumstances surrounding the fire remain unclear.

ALSO READ | 11 dead, three wounded in KZN shooting

The KwaZulu-Natal Department of Transport has launched an investigation, with a specialised team dispatched to establish what caused the vehicle to catch fire.

Transport MEC Siboniso Duma expressed his condolences to the officer’s family, friends and colleagues.

“We extend our deepest condolences to the family and colleagues of the officer during this difficult time,” the department said.

World.title: 30 years of vaccine research, Wits University celebrates progress and greenshoots
World.content:
JOHANESBURG - The Vaccines and Infectious Diseases Analytics (VIDA) Research Unit at Wits University has been at the forefront of vaccine development for 30 years.

The importance of vaccines has never been clearer than when COVID-19 broke out in 2020.

The recent Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has made the continent realise how important it is for Africa to create its own vaccine-creating capabilities.

"The amount of expertise that was developed over the past 30 years in South Africa is phenomenal," said Wits Health Sciences Dean, Dr Shabir Madhi.

That came through during the COVID-19 pandemic.

"Even now, we see South African scientists being involved in the development of vaccines across a number of pathogens," said Madhi.

World.title: Bafana Sindane files urgent bid to block Madlanga subpoena
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Mpumalanga taxi boss Bafana Oupa Sindane has filed an urgent application in the Gauteng High Court seeking to interdict his testimony before the Madlanga Commission.

Sindane was expected to testify before the Commission on Wednesday. His lawyer has confirmed that the urgent application has been filed.

Sindane is also challenging the manner in which his electronic devices were handed over to the Commission’s Recommendations Task Team. His legal team also said he is medically unfit to take the stand.

His testimony was expected to focus on alleged networks and connections within the taxi industry and would have followed that of his associate and fellow taxi boss, Joe “Ferrari” Sibanyoni.

Sibanyoni has denied having links to corrupt police officers or hiring hitmen. However, during his testimony, he acknowledged having what he described as brotherly relationships with some police officers.

Sindane and Sibanyoni are also co-accused in an extortion and money-laundering case.

World.title: Confirmed Mpox cases in SA rise to 22
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – The number of confirmed Mpox cases in South Africa has risen to 22, up from 18.

As of Tuesday, the Department of Health said 22 cases had been confirmed, including a 47-year-old man from Cape Town who travelled to Spain earlier this month.

The man had previously been classified as a probable case while awaiting laboratory results from Spanish health authorities. Following confirmation of a positive test, the Department of Health said the case had been reclassified as laboratory-confirmed and included in the updated national tally.

The three additional cases include infections involving German and Norwegian citizens.

READ | Health department receive 10 500 Mpox vaccines

Of the 22 confirmed cases, 18 are in the Western Cape, three in Gauteng and one in KwaZulu-Natal. All but one of the patients are male, with those affected ranging in age from 23 to 50.

Mpox can cause a range of symptoms, including fever, headache, muscle aches, back pain and fatigue. One of the more recognisable signs is a rash or skin lesions, which can appear on the face, hands, feet and other parts of the body.

The virus is transmitted mainly through close physical contact with an infected person. It can also spread through contact with contaminated materials, including bedding, clothing and towels.

Health authorities are urging anyone who develops symptoms associated with Mpox to seek medical attention.

World.title: Bomas of Kenya : Theatre of political controversy every election cycle
World.content:
When former IEBC chairperson Wafula Chebukati was whisked to safety after chaos erupted at Bomas of Kenya before presidential results were announced. [Standard]

For decades, the Bomas of Kenya has stood as the theatre of Kenyan democracy, characterised by high-stakes political drama.

While originally founded to be a cultural centre meant to showcase the country’s heritage, the venue finds itself at the chaotic epicentre of Kenya’s Presidential election tallies every five years, ever since it was selected as the most preferable national tallying centre for the Presidential elections by the Independent Electoral Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Ruto offers Kenya as test case on African risk
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto with Dangote Industries President and CEO Aliko Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) CEO Samaila Zubairu on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

President William Ruto has offered Kenya as a test case for how African risk is assessed, saying the country will open its default and recovery data to rating agencies and accept changes to the methodology if the evidence supports them.

Ruto said financial rules are steering African pension savings towards government securities rather than infrastructure, even where regulations allow greater investment in projects.

He made the proposal Monday, September 21, at the Africa We Build High-Level Roundtable on regulation, risk and reward in New York. The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) convened the event on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Kenyan pension funds hold 46 per cent of their Sh3.2 trillion ($24.7 billion) in government securities but only 0.02 per cent in infrastructure debt, Ruto said. The rules allow pension funds to invest up to 10 per cent in infrastructure.

“Africa's problem is no longer the amount of capital available to it. Africa's problem is the set of rules that decide where that capital is allowed to go,” Ruto noted.

Ruto returned to an argument he made at the inaugural Africa We Build Summit in Nairobi in April, where he said African countries should use domestic capital to finance their own infrastructure.

At the New York roundtable, he revisited his earlier phrase, “he who pays the piper calls the tune”, using a teacher in Eldoret who has contributed to a pension fund for 20 years to illustrate his point.

“In Nairobi I said that he who pays the piper calls the tune. I meant it as a warning about depending on other people's money. This morning I mean it as an opportunity. The teacher in Eldoret is paying the piper. She has earned the right to call the tune,” Ruto explained.

He said the teacher's savings are more likely to sit in a US Treasury bill than in a nearby geothermal plant.

“Her fund manager is not being unpatriotic. He is being rational. The rules he works under tell him the Treasury bill is prudent and the power plant is adventurous. Capital follows incentives, and we wrote the incentives,” Ruto observed.

The Africa Finance Corporation's President and Chief Executive Samaila Zubairu framed the wider problem in similar terms at the Nairobi summit, saying Africa is “not capital-poor; it is capital-trapped.”

Ruto now wants African risk assessed using evidence from African markets rather than assumptions that he argues can make projects and countries appear more expensive to finance.

He said Kenya will make its pension and insurance regulators available to work with rating agencies, insurers and standard setters.

“If the evidence vindicates the current methodology, we will accept the finding and say so publicly. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto added.

He proposed that the roundtable establish a working group based in Nairobi to continue the work and report to the next Africa We Build Summit in 12 months with findings backed by numbers.

President William Ruto on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

Ruto made four requests to rating agencies, insurers, regulators and other institutions involved in financing: price African risk against African experience, make insurance on productive assets affordable, end penalties on long-term assets in prudential and liquidity rules and build bankable project pipelines.

He said African non-bank domestic capital pools have passed $2 trillion, while external concessional and commercial flows to Africa totalled $1.7 trillion between 2014 and 2024.

Official development assistance has also fallen every year since 2020, Ruto said, arguing that Africa can no longer rely on external financing to meet its infrastructure needs.

Kenya has begun putting some of the proposed financing mechanisms in place.

Ruto said the National Infrastructure Fund, signed into law in March, aims to mobilise up to $40 billion for roads, ports, power and water without new public debt.

In May, Kenya listed its first infrastructure fund on the Nairobi Securities Exchange and raised Sh3.4 billion with United Kingdom support. Kenya also increased its equity in the Africa Finance Corporation by Sh3.25 billion ($25 million), Ruto said.

The president said Kenya was willing to expose its own financing system to scrutiny as part of the test.

“If the evidence supports the current methodology, we will accept it. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto told the roundtable.

The broader goal, he said, is to make it as easy for African institutional investors to finance productive assets as it is to buy government debt.

“The day a Kenyan pension trustee can buy a Kenyan power station as easily as she buys a Treasury bill, this argument will be over,” Ruto said.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro, Kinangop MP clash over alleged threatening message
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro arrives at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town for the service on September 20, 2026. [James Munyeki, Standard]

There was drama at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town during service on Sunday after Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro clashed with Kinangop MP Zachary Kwenya Thuku over an alleged threatening message.

Thuku, who is allied to the Kenya Kwanza government led by President William Ruto, is said to have warned Nyoro against attending the service.

"Yesterday, I received a message from the MP for Kinangop, Kwenya Thuku, warning me not to attend the church service. If I am lying, let him come here and read the message he sent me," Nyoro said.

He challenged the Kinangop MP to read the message aloud to the congregation.

"If anything happens to me today, Kenyans will judge whoever will be responsible," said Nyoro.

The Kiharu MP challenged Thuku to face him at a public rally at Engineer Trading Centre.

When he rose to speak, the Kinangop MP said he would not address the matter in church.

Instead, he said this was a political issue that the leaders would resolve.

"Let us solve this matter amicably. We are all brothers in this political journey," he said amid cheers from the congregation.

Recently, Nyoro added his voice to the growing political realignment in Mt Kenya, openly acknowledging the political tightrope he now walks as he distances himself from his former allies in the ruling party.

In a candid interview, he admitted that his previous close ties with President William Ruto and the Kenya Kwanza administration have left him vulnerable to suspicion from both sides of the political divide but insisted his decision to abandon the ruling party, United Democratic Alliance (UDA) was deliberate, difficult, and necessary.

World.title: Ruto leaves for New York ahead of UN General Assembly
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto leaves for New York ahead of 81st UN General Assembly. [PCS]

President William Ruto has departed for New York, United States, to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Ruto is expected to push Kenya’s investment agenda and advocate for increased financing for Africa.

According to a statement from State House, Ruto will use the global gathering to seek partnerships in energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, health, agriculture and technology.

He will also advance Kenya’s agenda on artificial intelligence and Africa’s participation in the global digital economy.

Ruto is expected to co-chair roundtables hosted by the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Global Africa Business Initiative (GABI), alongside industrialist Aliko Dangote.

A key focus will be the planned Sh2.2 trillion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, which the government says will have a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and create more than 60,000 jobs. The project is scheduled to break ground on September 30, 2026.

On artificial intelligence, Ruto and Finland President Alexander Stubb will co-lead the AI Middle Powers Initiative, which seeks to enable countries to pool computing resources, data and talent to build AI capabilities.

Kenya will also advance the Africa Development Bank-backed AI 10 billion initiative, which aims to mobilise up to 10 billion dollars by 2035 for investment in Africa’s artificial intelligence sector.

The President is further expected to sign a global declaration and roadmap on child online AI safety alongside leaders from Spain, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

He will also launch an Africa Resilience Compact that will use artificial intelligence, satellite earth observation and predictive technologies to strengthen preparedness for El Niño and other climate shocks.

During his address to the UN General Assembly, Ruto is expected to champion an Africa-financing-Africa approach, calling for reforms and international guarantees to unlock more African capital for infrastructure and enterprise.

Ruto will also highlight Kenya’s National Infrastructure Fund, which the government says is designed to mobilise up to 40 billion dollars without adding to public debt.

On the sidelines of the General Assembly, the President is expected to hold meetings with heads of state and government, multilateral institutions and global corporations to discuss trade, investment and diplomatic cooperation.

He will also engage Kenyans living in the United States as the government advances a Diaspora Investment Platform intended to channel diaspora capital into productive investment in Kenya.

World.title: Inside Parliament's probe into secondary school fees and capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Pangani Girls School Chief Principal Dr Millicent Odhiambo before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Parliament’s scrutiny of the Auditor-General’s report on public secondary schools has exposed inconsistencies in capitation funding, student enrolment figures and the National Education Management Information System (NEMIS).

The National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education has raised concerns over the impact of funding shortfalls on school operations and called for discussions with Ministry of Education officials to address the challenges.

The committee is also exploring whether the secondary school fee structure should be reviewed amid concerns that current capitation is insufficient to meet rising operational costs.

Chaired by Luanda MP Dick Maungu, the committee raised the concerns after the Auditor-General’s report showed that several national schools (C1) had sought additional fees from parents above the approved Sh53,000 annual amount, citing rising costs and inflation.

MPs also questioned disparities between capitation disbursements and the actual number of students in schools, which principals said had contributed to underfunding.

For the first time, administrators of national schools appeared before a parliamentary committee to respond to audit queries, with several saying discrepancies between NEMIS figures and actual school records had affected the amount of capitation they received.

Chief principals from Alliance High School, Alliance Girls, Bishop Gatimu Ngandu Girls, Limuru Girls, Mang’u High, Kenya High School, Pangani Girls and Kabare Girls, among others, said they had experienced difficulties validating learner data on NEMIS.

They said capitation received by their schools did not cover all students, with principals reporting that they receive less than the Sh22,244 expected per learner annually. The amount, they said, averages about Sh15,000.

Schools defend additional fees

During the committee’s examination of Alliance High School’s audit report, the Auditor-General flagged the irregular increase in school fees, including Sh17.6 million collected from parents.

“The school charged fees of Sh68,554 whereas the fees as per the Ministry’s guideline is Sh53,554 and the school thus raised fees by Sh15,000 per student annually contrary to Regulation 44 of Basic Education Regulation 2015, which states that no public school or institution shall issue alternative fee structure other than that approved by the Cabinet Secretary,” the auditor read. ‎Alliance High School's Principal David Kamau before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Alliance High School Chief Principal David Kamau admitted that the school had sought alternative funding but said the initiative came from parents.

He said the approved Sh53,000 fee was insufficient to sustain the school’s budget amid rising costs and expectations of maintaining the institution’s standards.

“We have a certain lifestyle we have to maintain and that is why parents came in – in fact it was their idea – and asked us to maintain that. They came in and suggested they can do a budget support so that we maintain the same standards. For us, to acquire the results, we have to do a lot of activities to make sure we give a holistic education associated with the school over the years,” he explained.

“Parents approve that at an Annual General Meeting and we write to the Ministry but that letter of authority has never been granted. We have followed the process to the letter in terms of seeking approval for extra levies from parents,” he added.

The audit also flagged fee arrears in almost all the schools, with Alliance High School reporting arrears amounting to Sh36 million.

Kenya High School Chief Principal Rev Edith Koech was also required to respond to an audit query over unapproved fees under the parents’ association support programme, through which parents were charged Sh25,000 above the set amount per student without approval from the county education board.

Koech said the school had written to the Ministry seeking approval and, although it did not expressly receive authorisation at the time, it had since obtained it.

She said additional funds were approved during annual general meetings, where two budgets were presented — one based on Ministry guidelines and another reflecting what parents felt should be covered.

“Kenya High has its standards, for instance we have tea three times a day and they eat githeri once, they will burn the school if we change,” Koech explained.

Kiminini MP Kakai Bisau said the issue of additional levies had emerged in many schools, with principals arguing that the funds were necessary for students’ wellbeing.

“Looks like this issue is conflicting the law yet public participation is conducted among parents of respective schools. This is something we need guidance on and embedded in policy,” he said.

Other MPs questioned what happens to students from poor backgrounds who cannot afford the additional charges.

Lungalunga MP Chiforomondo Munga said principals had been entrusted with following the law, which states that public schools should not issue alternative fee structures without approval.

“I was a parent of Alliance but all said and done, you have done contrary to the law because approvals must come from the CS and I can assure you there is nobody who will approve that because they know they will be breaking the law and will be held accountable,” he said.

He said the situation presented a dilemma because schools were expected to maintain certain standards while operating within existing regulations.

Embakasi West MP Mark Mwenje said the issue of additional fees had existed for years, noting that he had paid about Sh40,000 while he was an Alliance High School student about two decades ago.

“We just need to sit down with the Ministry because it is becoming obvious that this money is no longer sufficient but we need to inform the principal that whenever such things are happening, there should be concurrence of the Principal Secretary but when we meet with the CS that issue should come out because we can no longer bury our heads in the sand,” Mwenje said.

Igembe Central MP Daniel Karitho described the issue as a “tricky” one, given rising inflation and the need to comply with the law.

“We cannot allow parents from any institution to just sit down and agree because there are those who are voiceless. This is an issue that needs to be discussed even in the House on the fees structure and if there is something that needs to be done, even on the basic regulation so that we can have a level,” Karitho said.

Alliance principal, however, maintained that the school’s process was transparent, with parents being provided with budget documents during annual general meetings and informed why additional funds were required.

“We tell the parents that is their decision to make and if they want to stick to the Sh53,000 but what we can offer as a school will reduce. I can assure we are conscious of the needy and we do not send anyone away because of the fees, either for statutory or additional,” he explained.

Kenya High echoed similar sentiments, saying additional contributions were based on public participation among parents and that no child was sent home over fees. The school also has endowment funds, it said.

NEMIS discrepancies

In another case, MPs questioned how Limuru Girls High School received an additional Sh785,946 in capitation after discrepancies emerged between its student enrolment records and figures captured in NEMIS.

The committee noted variances in Limuru Girls’ records and those of other national schools for the financial years 2020/2021 to 2024/2025.

The Auditor-General’s report for the year ended June 2024 showed that NEMIS recorded 2,099 students at the school in September 2023, 2,300 in January 2024 and 2,354 in May 2024.

However, records presented by the school showed enrolment of 2,062 students in September 2023 and 2,253 students in both January and May 2024.

The difference resulted in Sh785,946 in excess funding, raising concerns over whether the variance affected service delivery in other schools that did not receive capitation and made it difficult to confirm value for money.

Limuru Girls Chief Principal Susan Kariuki acknowledged the discrepancies but attributed them to differences between physical enrolment records and learner information captured in NEMIS.

“The difference arose from variations between the school’s physical enrolment records and the learner information captured in NEMIS at the respective reporting periods. The school did not intentionally provide inflated enrolment figures,” Kariuki said.

“So, because you are given more money, where do you take it?” Maungu posed.

Kariuki, however, said the school had not received the full amount of capitation due per learner and therefore did not consider itself overfunded in the ordinary sense. She said the Government was expected to provide Sh22,244 per learner but the school had been receiving about Sh15,000.

Narok Woman Representative Rebecca Tonkei questioned how Limuru Girls received higher funding for learners who were not captured in NEMIS, noting that other schools appearing before the committee had complained of underfunding caused by incomplete NEMIS records.

Maungu questioned the reliability of NEMIS, saying a system used to determine public funding should be predictable, consistent and dependable.

“This is not a good system. A good system should be predictable, consistent and dependable. But this system gives some people less and others more, sometimes the data is missing,” Maungu noted.

Starehe Girls raises fresh questions

Starehe Girls presented a different case that the committee said contained several grey areas after it emerged that 70 per cent of the school’s 776 learners are fully sponsored while the remaining 30 per cent are self-sponsored.

The school explained that all learners receive about Sh16,000 in Government capitation. For the 70 per cent, their upkeep is sourced through the board of trustees, while self-sponsored learners cover their own costs.

“Being a C1 school, by law it should pay Sh53,000. Instead, some are paying Sh150,000 meaning Sh96,000 extra to take care of the vulnerable. On this other side, you are saying they have a sponsor who take care...are you seeing the kind of confusion because they are already sponsored?” posed Maungu.

Despite the school’s unique funding arrangement, the committee said Starehe Girls remained a public institution and should therefore be audited.

The committee noted that not all financial years had been covered in the audit, unlike other C1 schools, and directed the institution to present all relevant documents for review.

Meanwhile, Mang’u High School surprised the committee when its administration said the school also faced challenges posed by snakes and hyenas that sometimes invade the institution.

World.title: Ruto faults Uhuru for undermining his government
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto join traditional dancers in Homa Bay on September 17, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has renewed his public criticism of former President Uhuru Kenyatta, accusing his predecessor of undermining the government and urging him to withdraw from active political mobilisation.

Ruto said he had supported Uhuru throughout their political partnership and expected reciprocal support when he sought the presidency.

“I stood by you through four elections; I stood by you, helped you, took care of you, and worked for you.”

Ruto claimed the two had discussed an arrangement in which each would serve as president for ten years. He accused Uhuru of failing to honour that understanding, saying:

“When the time came for you to help me, after you said ‘ten years for you, ten years for me,’ not even for a single day did you support me.”

Ruto also appealed to Uhuru to respect the position of former President and withdraw from political activities that he said were aimed at destabilising his administration.

“A former president! Surely, my brother, you are lowering the dignity of the office of the former president. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” Ruto said.

Ruto made the remarks on Thursday, September 17, 2026, in Sindo, Homa Bay County, as he concluded a four-day development tour of Nyanza.

The tour covered Kisumu, Siaya, Migori and Homa Bay and focused largely on roads, markets, housing, water and other development projects. The Star+1

The latest confrontation adds another chapter to the complicated political relationship between the two leaders.

Ruto served as Uhuru's deputy from 2013 to 2022, after the two politicians formed a political alliance that won the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections.

Contemporary accounts describe their original arrangement as involving support for Kenyatta for two terms, followed by support for Ruto's presidential ambitions. The Washington Post

The President nevertheless acknowledged Uhuru's democratic right to oppose his government but urged the former president to respect the office he once held.

“You are running schemes to sabotage the government. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” he said.

His criticism centred instead on what he described as continued political mobilisation against his administration.

He said his administration had stabilised the economy and pointed to investments in education, housing, markets and infrastructure. During the Homa Bay leg alone, the government highlighted a Sh3.5 billion plan for 21 modern markets.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Temperatures across Egypt to drop following humidity as Autumn begins
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) revealed its weather forecast and temperature projections for the coming hours, announcing the onset of weather fluctuations alongside chances of rainfall across several governorates.

Unstable conditions will begin over several northern regions, according to weather maps, stretching from the Mediterranean coast to parts of the Nile Delta.

Despite the persistence of relatively hot and humid conditions, cold air currents in the upper atmosphere will collide with warm, humid air, generating a brief and localized state of instability.

The atmosphere will remain humid due to rain-bearing clouds forming over the region, heightening the feeling of heat.

Once this brief weather system passes, temperatures are expected to drop noticeably starting Friday and Saturday.

Rainfall map: Scattered thunderstorms expected Thursday

Regarding the rainfall map, random thunderclouds are expected to form starting early Thursday morning over the northwestern coast (from Matrouh to Alexandria).

By afternoon and late afternoon, convective thunderclouds will build, penetrating and expanding over the Delta governorates—namely Beheira, Monufiya, Sharqiya, Gharbiya, and Daqahliya—in addition to Kafr El-Sheikh, Damietta, and Port Said.

Rainfall across these areas is expected to be scattered.

The EMA outlines autumn 2026 forecast

The EMA outlined the expected weather features for the 2026 autumn season, which begins on Wednesday and will last for three months.

The Director-General of the Forecasting and Early Warning Center at the EMA, Mahmoud Shaheen, told Al-Masry Al-Youm that potential weather fluctuations are expected, as autumn weather maps shift rapidly according to changes in atmospheric pressure patterns and distributions.

Light to moderate rainfall is anticipated, with thunderclouds potentially developing over scattered areas of the northwestern coast and the Nile Delta, with some rain potentially reaching Greater Cairo.

The EMA confirmed that seasonal forecasts suggest rainfall amounts and temperatures during this autumn may be slightly above average climatic norms.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egyptian, US FMs discuss strategic ties, regional issues in New York
World.content:
Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Expatriates Badr Abdelatty met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, on the sidelines of the high-level segment of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The meeting underscored the importance of the strategic relations between Egypt and the United States and the need to broaden and deepen them, as well as intensify coordination and consultations on issues of common interest in a manner that serves the two countries’ shared interests.

The talks also covered a number of regional issues, including the situation in Sudan.

World.title: Red Crescent delivers over 131,000 food baskets to Gaza
World.content:
The Egyptian Red Crescent (ERC) on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, dispatched the 281st “Zad Al-Ezza… From Egypt to Gaza” convoy carrying humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip as part of its role as the national mechanism for coordinating and delivering humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian people.

The convoy carried tons of various humanitarian supplies, including more than 131,000 food baskets, flour, relief materials and medical supplies, as well as petroleum products needed to operate hospitals and vital facilities in the Strip.

The ERC has maintained a presence at the border since the start of the crisis, keeping its logistics centers ready and intensifying efforts to prepare and deliver humanitarian and relief aid to the Gaza Strip.

The total volume of aid delivered has exceeded one million tons, with the participation of more than 75,000 volunteers from the organization.

World.title: IDSC: Egypt tourism revenues, arrivals rise in 2026 amid regional tensions
World.content:
The Cabinet’s Information and Decision Support Center (IDSC) has published infographics highlighting developments in Egypt’s tourism and travel sector, including growth in hotels and rooms under construction, tourist arrivals and tourism revenues, as well as international forecasts for the sector’s performance in the coming years.

The figures point to continued growth in Egypt’s tourism and travel sector despite regional tensions, alongside an expansion in hotel capacity and expectations for further improvement in the sector in the coming years.

According to W Hospitality Group, the number of hotels under construction in Egypt rose to 185 with a total of 46,000 rooms in 2026, from 143 hotels with 33,900 rooms in 2025.

The number stood at 109 hotels with 26,200 rooms in 2024, 103 hotels with 24,900 rooms in 2023 and 85 hotels with 21,300 rooms in 2022.

Tourist arrivals reached 12.7 million in the January-August 2026 period, up from 12.2 million in the same period of 2025.

Tourism revenues rose to $12 billion from $11.8 billion over the same period.

The World Travel & Tourism Council expects Egypt’s tourism and travel sector to grow 3% in 2026 despite geopolitical tensions. It forecasts the sector’s contribution to gross domestic product to rise to $35.4 billion in 2026 from $34.4 billion in 2025, while employment is expected to increase to 3.03 million from 2.97 million.

The International Monetary Fund expects Egypt’s tourism revenues to rise from $19.9 billion in fiscal year 2025/26 to $20.8 billion in 2026/27, $22.9 billion in 2027/28, $25.4 billion in 2028/29, $27.9 billion in 2029/30 and $29.8 billion in 2030/31.

World.title: Egyptian, Moroccan FMs discuss bilateral ties, regional issues
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty met with Moroccan Minister of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Abroad Nasser Bourita on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, on the sidelines of the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Foreign Ministry Spokesman Nader Zaki said Abdelatty underscored the special nature of the bilateral relations and historic ties between Egypt and Morocco, stressing the two countries’ keenness to further strengthen cooperation across various fields.

He also praised the outcomes of the first session of the Egyptian-Moroccan Coordination and Follow-up Committee and stressed the importance of building on them to advance economic, trade and investment relations between the two countries.

At the regional level, the two ministers exchanged views on a number of issues of common interest, notably the latest developments concerning the Palestinian cause and developments in Sudan and Libya.

They stressed the importance of continued coordination and consultations to support regional security and stability and strengthen joint Arab and African action.

World.title: Mamdani is a “dangerous leader,” Israeli ambassador says
World.content:
Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations, called New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani a “dangerous leader,” claiming Mamdani condemned Israel’s elimination of Hamas operatives.

“If you condemn the elimination of terrorists who took part in the atrocities of October 7th, you endorse Hamas,” Danon told CNN’s Jim Sciutto.

He was echoing remarks today by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who released a video accusing Mamdani of supporting Hamas and “inciting riots against New York Jews.” Netanyahu said that he would come to the UN “to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I’m going to tell the truth about you.”

Mamdani denied the accusations made by Netanyahu.

“What we do know to actually be the truth when it comes to the prime minister is that he is the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity. And as the prime minister, is the architect of a horrific genocide against Palestinians,” the mayor said during a news conference.

CNN’s Gloria Pazmino contributed to this report.

World.title: Iran’s leadership warns US against any new attacks after Trump’s threat at UN
World.content:
Tehran’s leadership has warned the United States against any fresh attacks on the country after US President Donald Trump threatened to “annihilate” Iran in his speech to the UN General Assembly.

The US president said that he has a “big decision” to make on Iran — casting it as a choice between striking a deal after the midterm elections and annihilating Iran.

The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) warned against new attacks, saying Washington would gain “nothing but failure” from any such action, Iran state media Press TV reported.

“Trump forgets that he has already made threats before but was unable to carry them out, and now he is once again making new threats,” said IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi, according to Press TV.

The General Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces warned Tehran would deliver “even harsher, crushing, and unpredictable blows,” and said the US’s repetition of “baseless allegations and threats” should not be interpreted as a sign of strength, Press TV reported.

And parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that Iran would not surrender or stop its activities in the face of US pressure, Iranian state media Tasnim reported.

World.title: Fact check: Trump’s false claims to the United Nations
World.content:
President Donald Trump made multiple false claims in his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, though he largely stuck to a prepared text.

Here is a fact check of some of his assertions.

Trump and wars

Trump, repeating a frequent false claim, said, “Since I took office, it has been my great honor to settle eight wars.”

He specified that he was talking about conflicts between Cambodia and Thailand; Kosovo and Serbia; Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo; India and Pakistan; Armenia and Azerbaijan; and the war in Gaza. And he has previously claimed that the other two wars he ended were last year’s brief conflict between Israel and Iran and a supposed war between Egypt and Ethiopia.

Trump’s “eight” figure is a clear exaggeration.

His list includes two situations that were never actually wars during his tenure. The situation between Egypt and Ethiopia was a diplomatic dispute over an Ethiopian dam project, not a war, and the mysterious supposed issue he says he resolved between Serbia and Kosovo was also not a war.

In addition, the war involving Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo has not ended despite a peace agreement brokered by the Trump administration. And though Trump cited the war in Gaza, Israel continues to conduct frequent attacks in the enclave despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement.

Trump did help to end the brief 2025 conflict between Israel and Iran, though Israel proceeded to join the US in starting another war against Iran in 2026.

Global warming

Trump scoffed at dire warnings that artificial intelligence might eventually attack or kill people, claiming they are coming from “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming, a name since reborn to climate change because the planet was cooling, not warming, and nobody was dead.”

There are at least four things wrong with his sentence about global warming.

First, the phrase “global warming” remains in widespread use even though the phrase “climate change” is also common; they mean different things. Climate scientists use both, often saying “global warming” when referring to the long-term trend of increasing global temperature and “climate change” when referring to the numerous effects the world is experiencing because of that trend. (NASA, part of the Trump-led federal government, explains the difference between the terms on its website.) For example, a 2023 report from the UN’s climate change panel is titled “Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report,” but it says this: “Human activities, principally through emissions of greenhouse gases, have unequivocally caused global warming, with global surface temperature reaching 1.1°C above 1850-1900 in 2011-2020.”

Second, while Trump didn’t say what time period he was talking about, he didn’t acknowledge that the world has continued to get warmer, not cooler. The UN’s World Meteorological Organization reported in January that “the past 11 years have been the 11 warmest on record,” with 2023, 2024 and 2025 the three very warmest — as NASA also found — though 2025 wasn’t as hot as 2024.

Third, experts widely disagree that “nobody” has died from the various impacts of a warming world. It’s impossible to pinpoint a precise death number, but some estimates total in the millions. The deaths are likely to continue; the World Health Organization says, “Between 2030 and 2050, climate change is expected to cause approximately 250,000 additional deaths per year, from undernutrition, malaria, diarrhea and heat stress alone.”

Fourth, while somebody somewhere might have said that “we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming,” that isn’t how an expert report framed the issue.

A widely discussed 2018 report from climate scientists said the world needed to sharply cut carbon emissions within the next 12 years to be on track to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels; scientists said above that threshold, the potential deadly impacts from climate change would be larger. Though the 2018 report was often oversimplified by politicians, the expert claim was never that “we’ll all be dead in 12 years” — it was that significant action was needed within 12 years to improve the future. (The UN program reported earlier this month that the world is set to exceed the 1.5-degree increase, “likely within the next few years.”)

Investment in the US

Trump delivered a more cautious version of his inaccurate previous boast that $21 trillion in investment is pouring into the US, this time saying, “We’ve secured commitments for $21 trillion in new investments from all over the planet.” His figure has no apparent basis even with the “secured commitments for” caveat; the White House has never been able to substantiate it.

When the president spoke at the UN, the White House’s own website claimed there had been “$11.2 trillion” in “major investment announcements” during Trump’s second term, far less than the “$21 trillion” in commitments the president cited. And a detailed CNN review in 2025 found the White House list was counting trillions in vague investment pledges, pledges that were about “bilateral trade” or “economic exchange” rather than investment in the US, and vague statements that didn’t even rise to the level of pledges.

The White House figure includes pledges from US-based companies as well as foreign entities. Federal data shows that new foreign direct investment in the US was about $232 billion in 2025.

The US and munitions

Trump defended the Iran war at length. And he claimed, “The cowards and traitors would love to say the United States is low on munitions, but that’s not true. We have more munitions than we could ever possibly even think of using, and we’re building them at levels that we have never done before.”

We don’t have access to classified information on the precise current state of US munitions stockpiles, and it’s not clear who Trump is calling “cowards and traitors.” But it’s not just CNN and other media outlets that have reported that the war with Iran has depleted at least some US munitions levels; the federal inspector general overseeing the Defense Department and the nonpartisan federal Congressional Budget Office essentially said the same in separate reports released last week.

The inspector general report, which discussed the period from the beginning of April through the end of June, said a Defense Department acquisitions office “said that the munitions expenditure in (the war) has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply.”

The report said the acquisitions office also noted that while the Pentagon “has begun to implement mitigation strategies, the defense industrial base requires ‘significant lead time’ to expand production capacities.” The report specified: “The most persistent bottlenecks remain in the production of solid rocket motors, the availability of high-grade explosives and propellants, and the recruitment of skilled manufacturing labor.”

The Congressional Budget Office report said there is a “shortfall” of missile defense interceptors and that the war will leave “the United States with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years.” The report said the Defense Department had a “limited” inventory of interceptors even before Israel and the US attacked Iran during a brief conflict in June 2025, and that the budget office’s research indicates the US “has probably used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of those munitions since June 2025.”
