World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: Colombia pulls out of international LGBT coalition
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella pulled Colombia out of the international Equal Rights Coalition, which promotes the rights of sexual and gender minorities around the world.

The Foreign Ministry announced its departure from the coalition in a letter addressed to the organization of which Colombia was co-president until February next year.

According to Caribe Afirmativa, a gay rights NGO that was part of the international initiative, warned that the decision was “a serious setback in foreign policy and commitments to LGBTIQ+ rights.”

We also view this action as a snub to the international community, a break from the leadership role Colombia had established, and an unequivocal political signal regarding the place the current government is willing to grant to the rights of LGBTIQ+ people. Caribe Afirmativa

De la Espriella has appointed multiple prominent far-right figures in his government and has vowed to wage a “Culture War” against what it considers “gender ideology.”

On top of this, De la Espriella and multiple of his cabinet members oppose the right of gay couples to adopt children and reportedly sacked the newly appointed planning chief because he and his gay partner had adopted a child.

World.title: Court imposes strict conditions on Colombia’s military air strikes if minors are present
World.content:
A Bogota court imposed strict conditions on Colombia’s military authorities if they want to carry out air strikes on illegal armed groups in places where victims of forced recruitment are present.

The ruling of Bogota’s 34th Family Court lifted a suspension on the strikes that had been imposed earlier this month in response to a lawsuit.

The court imposed the following conditions on air strikes to evade violating International Humanitarian Law, which prioritizes the rights of child victims of forced recruitment over the success of military operations.

Don’t assume minors are legitimate targets because they form part of an illegal armed group

Intensify the verification and cross-checking of available information on the possible presence of minors at potential targets

Explicitly include this assessment to the legal and operational assessment of the attack

Assess the foreseeable risk of an attack on the lives and integrity of the minors

Examine the existence of less harmful means, methods, timing or operational alternatives that would allow the achievement of a comparable military advantage

Rigorously apply the principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality before authorizing and executing the operation

The court additionally ordered family welfare institute ICBF to be integrated into military operations and strengthen the pathways for disengagement, restoration of rights, comprehensive care, and reintegration of children and adolescents who are victims of recruitment, with a differentiated and territorial approach.

The court asked the Ombudsman and the Inspector General’s Office to monitor compliance of the orders issued to maximize the protection of children’s rights.

The lawsuit had been filed in a successful attempt to protect children against the violence President Abelardo de la Espriella sought to unleash on illegal armed groups that refused to demobilize.

World.title: US maintains Colombia “failed demonstrably” in fighting drug trafficking
World.content:
The United States President Donald Trump maintained that Colombia “failed demonstrably during the previous 12 months to make substantial efforts to adhere to their obligations under international counternarcotics agreements.”

In an annual reviews, Trump stressed that the South American country maintains its an unwilling drug trafficking country “solely due to the incompetence and chaos produced by the previous far-left government.”

“If, as expected, Colombia makes progress on aggressive coca eradication and dismantling its narcoterrorist networks over the coming year, I will consider lifting the country’s ‘failed demonstrably’ status,” said the US president.

President Abelardo de la Espriella “has pledged to lead an aggressive campaign against coca cultivation and cocaine production, which reached record levels under the failed socialist policies of his predecessor,” Gustavo Petro, according to Trump.

Colombia is poised to resume its place as our foremost security partner in the hemisphere, and the country’s military, police, prosecutors, and courts now finally have a worthy champion in President de la Espriella. US President Donald Trump

De la Espriella, who took office in August, informally joined the US Government’s Shield of the Americas program in an attempt to increase cooperation between Trump’s conservative and far-right allies in the region.

As part of his counternarcotics efforts, the Colombian president tried to increase air strikes on so-called “narcoterrorist” groups, but was forced to stop this by a court to protect minor forced recruitment victims.

The National Police announced a pilot aerial fumigation program, but this was also suspended by a court because of health and environmental concerns.

The State Department vowed to seek $1 billion dollar in aid, but has yet to ask Congress for these funds while allegedly dealing with the world’s highest number of deaths caused by the consumption of illicit drugs.

World.title: Colombia’s statistics chief sacked for claiming Petro did not manipulate statistics
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella sacked his statistics chief because he claimed he found no anomalies in labor statistics presented by the administration of former President Gustavo Petro.

In a press statement, De la Espriella’s press secretary said that DANE director Ricardo Valencia was sacked for claiming “that he had not found any anomalies in the DANE indicators for the month of July, figures compiled during the final month of the previous administration.”

Valencia made that claim “without any in-depth audits having been conducted beforehand,” according to the press secretary.

It is essential for the National Government to conduct a rigorous review of the information received and to ensure that the data on which strategic decisions for the country are based fully reflect the economic and social reality of Colombians. President’s Office

The former DANE director was sacked days after the President’s Office canceled another statistics press conference that are common because of the agency’s regular updates on the state of the Colombian economy

July’s labor statistics confirmed claims by the previous government that unemployment dropped to record lows after Petro raised the minimum wage.

De la Espriella has insisted that the country’s economy is in crisis contrary to evidence, which indicated Petro increased economic growth in his last half year in office.

World.title: Colombia’s social organizations and labor unions announce national strike in November
World.content:
Some 1,500 representatives of social organizations and labor unions agreed to begin organizing an anti-government national strike that should take place throughout Colombia either on November 11 or on November 20.

The organizations agreed to the mass mobilization during the National Gathering for the Defense of Life, Dignity, Democracy, Peace, Sovereignty, and Social Reforms that had been organized by labor unions in the capital Bogota.

The first and fundamental decision of the Meeting is to declare the most radical opposition to the illegitimate government of Abelardo de la Espriella because of the course it has imposed on the country—one of subordination to the interests of U.S. imperialism and alignment with the agenda of the international far right—which constitutes a direct threat to national sovereignty, democracy, and the rights won by the Colombian people, and an undeniable shift toward fascism. Social organizations and labor unions

In a statement, the organizations said that the national strike will be preceded by regional protests on October 10 and 14 that will seek to generate momentum for the national strike.

Indigenous organizations will additionally organize a Day of Indigenous, Afro and Popular Resistance on October 12.

A final date for the national strike has yet to be defined.

The organizations decided to call a strike to protest the government’s security and defense policy, the ending of peace processes with illegal armed groups and in defense of social reforms that had been implemented by former President Gustavo Petro.

The protests additionally seek to express solidarity with the people of Palestine, western Sahara, Iran, Bolivia and Venezuela, and reject US imperialism in the Americas.

We must categorically reject the interference of U.S. government officials in the formulation of domestic policies under the guise of so-called friendly aid, which in reality masks the ambition to intensify overexploitation, extractivism, territorial control, and the presence of foreign troops on our soil. Social organizations and labor unions

The organizations agreed to “prepare, through the most intense and massive agitation and propaganda campaign, a national strike.”

World.title: Burnham at the UN: “the rights of British territories to remain British”
World.content:
Burnham at the UN: “the rights of British territories to remain British”

23rd Wednesday, September 2026 - 09:49 UTC Full article

“We will stand firm in the face of any threats and challenges to the rule of law,” he said

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham placed the Falklands among the challenges to the rule of law in his first address to the United Nations General Assembly, delivered on Tuesday evening in New York, setting them in the same sentence as Russia.

“We will stand firm in the face of any threats and challenges to the rule of law,” he said. “Not just from Russia, but also from others, including where they threaten the rights of British territories to remain British, such as the Falkland Islands.” He did not mention Argentina at any point in the speech.

The wording goes further than his September 9 statement to the House of Commons, when he said his government would be “relentless” in defending the islanders' right to choose to be British. Hours before the speech, after his first meeting with US President Donald Trump, the prime minister said he had raised the issue: “I felt I owed it to the people, obviously in the Falklands and back at home, to make the position very clear and that's what I've done today.”

The same day left the Chagos Islands agreement in doubt. The deal transfers sovereignty over that British territory to Mauritius, with a subsequent lease of the Diego Garcia base. Trump called it “terrible” and “ridiculous” and said Burnham was “going to be looking at it”; the prime minister replied “yep”. Asked later by the BBC whether the deal was dead, he did not deny it, saying he had inherited it and that “we need a resolution” safeguarding the base's future. The cost is measured three ways: the government cites £3.4 billion in net present value, around £101 million a year over 99 years; the Conservative opposition uses the £34.7 billion nominal cash total; a third measure puts it at about £10 billion.

Most of the speech was devoted to what Burnham called an “industrial-scale assault” by hostile actors on Britain's information environment. According to the prime minister, Russian agencies used bots, fake websites and falsified newspaper articles, forged the branding of 28 British organisations including universities and the BBC, amplified far-right narratives, and there is evidence they tried to interfere in the 2019 general election. He put Kremlin spending on information manipulation at around £1.3 billion a year. These are British government assertions, presented without accompanying public documentation. He announced he had tasked security chiefs with beginning work on a National Centre for Information Defence and offered to share British experience with other countries, following support given to Moldova.

On artificial intelligence, Burnham called for “a single set of global principles and standards” and said he would put the issue at the heart of Britain's G20 presidency next year, alongside a new AI defence partnership with the United States to protect critical national infrastructure. Trump, in his own address, rejected any “globalist scheme” of regulation.

The prime minister also backed Ukraine, criticised Russian strikes on civilian energy infrastructure and, on the Middle East, said the Israeli government's actions in Gaza and the West Bank are not justified, after condemning the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. He listed measures taken with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband: banning trade with illegal settlements, recognising the occupation as unlawful and sanctioning those involved in settlement construction.

Argentina claims sovereignty over the archipelago, has 60 administrative proceedings open with no penalty applied and three criminal complaints covering ten companies, and last week sent Congress a sovereignty bill. None of the allegations has been proven. In the 2013 referendum, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Delcy Rodríguez calls her meeting with Trump "historic" and thanks him for his support
World.content:
Delcy Rodríguez calls her meeting with Trump “historic” and thanks him for his support

23rd Wednesday, September 2026 - 08:55 UTC Full article

Hours earlier, in his address to the General Assembly, Trump had called Maduro an “outlaw dictator” and said hundreds of political prisoners had been freed since his capture in January

Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, described her first meeting with US President Donald Trump as “historic”. The encounter took place on Tuesday evening in New York behind closed doors and with no press access. Her post on the social network X is the only available account of what was discussed: the White House confirmed the meeting and those present but released no agenda or outcomes.

“We held a historic meeting with the President of the United States, Donald Trump, with whom we discussed strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, and security and other matters of common interest,” Rodríguez wrote, posting a photograph alongside the president and thanking his administration for its support.

It was an informal encounter on the margins of the official agenda, scheduled for 7:40 p.m. at the Lotte New York Palace hotel in Manhattan, during a reception Trump hosted for foreign leaders for the General Assembly's high-level week. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller took part. Unlike other meetings Trump held in New York this week, such as his bilateral with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, this one was closed to reporters.

It is the first meeting between a US president and a Venezuelan leader in more than eleven years, since the brief encounter between Barack Obama and Nicolás Maduro at the 2015 Summit of the Americas in Panama. Maduro remains in US custody a few kilometres from the hotel where the meeting took place, awaiting trial and with the presumption of innocence.

Hours earlier, in his address to the General Assembly, Trump had called Maduro an “outlaw dictator” and said hundreds of political prisoners had been freed since his capture in January. On the oil agreement signed with Caracas last month, which gives the United States access to more than 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, he said: “To the victor belong the spoils,” describing it as “perhaps the biggest deal ever made.” He said he expected some US$100 billion in investment to flow into Venezuela's oil industry. He also presented January's military operation as evidence that the United States would use its “unmatched military might” to protect its interests in the Western Hemisphere.

Rodríguez arrived in New York on Monday and had earlier met UN Secretary-General António Guterres and the heads of the International Monetary Fund, Kristalina Georgieva; the World Bank, Ajay Banga; and the Inter-American Development Bank, Ilan Goldfajn. According to the UN, her talks with Guterres covered ongoing economic reforms, debt restructuring, dialogue initiatives and cooperation on human rights, as well as “the path towards full democracy”. State channel VTV described the meetings with the financial institutions as reflecting a “progressive normalisation of relations”.

Venezuela's diplomatic reintegration is not limited to Washington: on September 19, Caracas signed the restoration of relations with Paraguay at the Miraflores palace. Rodríguez addresses the General Assembly on Thursday.

World.title: Lula warns against foreign interference in Brazil's election at the UN Assembly
World.content:
Lula warns against foreign interference in Brazil's election at the UN Assembly

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 19:53 UTC Full article

“Brazilian democracy belongs to Brazilians,” he said towards the end of his address

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva warned the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that his country will not allow domestic or foreign actors to undermine the October 4 election, in a speech combining a defence of national sovereignty with a broader critique of the multilateral system.

“Brazilian democracy belongs to Brazilians,” he said towards the end of his address. “Brazil will remain a sovereign country.” Earlier he argued that Latin America faces a resurgence of “hegemonic ambitions” and foreign interference in elections, that “Brazil does not belong in anyone's backyard”, and that attempts to divide the world into spheres of influence are “anachronistic”. He did not mention Donald Trump by name. On regional security he said: “We do not need aircraft carriers watching our waters. We need cooperation to stop the flow of weapons and money that fuels crime.”

Trump spoke immediately afterwards, under the protocol assigning Brazil the opening of the general debate since 1955 and the host country the second slot. In his address he said “our actions in Venezuela prove that the United States will not allow any threat against America anywhere in the Western Hemisphere, and if necessary, we will use our unmatched military might to secure the vital national interests of the United States”. He also announced negotiations with Cuba led by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, during which passage the Cuban delegation walked out of the hall, praised cooperation with Delcy Rodríguez's interim government in Venezuela, and framed the Iran question as a choice between a deal and “annihilating the Islamic Republic”.

No bilateral meeting between the two leaders was scheduled. Brazilian diplomat Carlos Márcio Cozendey confirmed on September 16 that neither side had requested one, though an informal encounter of the kind held in September 2025 remains possible. Lula had said last week he intended to tell Trump directly not to interfere in the vote.

Trade tensions remain unresolved. Since July 22, certain Brazilian goods have paid an additional 25% under Section 301 of the US trade act, with exemptions including aircraft, coffee, beef and orange juice; a separate 12.5% forced-labour duty has applied since July 24, covering dozens of other economies as well. Brazil's trade ministry calculates that 23.1% of exports to the United States face the new duties, mostly cumulatively, for 37.5%. Brazil has held off on retaliation while negotiations continue, though Lula told CNN on Monday it could still invoke its reciprocity law if talks fail.

On the multilateral front, Lula said the UN is going through one of its most critical moments and that it “is failing” in its mission to prevent wars. “The feeling that moves me today is indignation,” he said, attributing the paralysis to the Security Council and the use of the veto by its permanent members, a practice Brazil has objected to since the first General Assembly in 1946. On the Middle East he said generations of Palestinians will carry the pain of the “genocide of women and children”, a characterisation contested in international legal debate, and criticised the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank. On Ukraine he said there would be “no winners on the battlefield”. He also called for regulation of large technology companies and artificial intelligence, and defended scientific evidence against climate disinformation.

World.title: Burnham says he raised the Falklands with Trump at their first meeting
World.content:
Burnham says he raised the Falklands with Trump at their first meeting

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 19:45 UTC Full article

“I think he's going to be a great prime minister. I think he's got a lot of assets on his side,” Trump said, adding that the United Kingdom “is a really special country”

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Tuesday that he raised the question of the Falklands with US President Donald Trump during their first meeting, held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. “The Falklands we mentioned. And you were good enough to listen to us on those issues,” he told reporters. Trump made no public response on the archipelago.

The approach comes eleven days after the US president sidestepped, in Dublin, a question on whether the United States would come to Britain's aid in any future conflict over the islands, and after he told the BBC that he reviews every position. Several outlets have noted that those remarks, along with his comments favouring Irish unification, unsettled the British government.

The tone of the meeting was warm. “I think he's going to be a great prime minister. I think he's got a lot of assets on his side,” Trump said, adding that the United Kingdom “is a really special country” and that Washington is “with you all the way”. Burnham replied that the relationship “matters so much” to his country and that the two had established “a good connection” in earlier discussions. He also reminded Trump that Manchester, where he was mayor before entering Downing Street in July, is not a “town” as the president had described it, but “a great city”. “I don't hold it against you as the former mayor,” he joked.

It is their first face-to-face meeting; the two had spoken twice by telephone since Burnham took office. Trump had described him as “a nice guy”. As mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham had said Trump was not welcome in the city and that he would refuse to meet him.

The agenda covered Ukraine, the Middle East, trade, energy, immigration and Rolls-Royce, as Trump himself set out. Burnham was seeking interceptor missiles to bolster Ukraine's air defences ahead of winter, and ways to restore the movement of ships through the Strait of Hormuz, largely blocked since the start of the war with Iran in February, a closure that has driven up crude prices. “We're still ready to play our part in the Middle East in terms of helping you stop the conflict, open the strait,” the prime minister said, mentioning a request from Saudi Arabia and adding: “obviously, we're with you that Iran must never be a nuclear power”.

The United States has never taken a formal position on sovereignty over the archipelago, though it recognises British de facto administration and supported the 1982 military campaign. Argentina claims sovereignty over the islands; in the 2013 referendum, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Over 40 items and £60,000: the Friends of the Falklands Museum launch their website
World.content:
Over 40 items and £60,000: the Friends of the Falklands Museum launch their website

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 11:26 UTC Full article

FIMA Friends has been a registered charity in the UK since July 2016 and directs its funds to research into the archipelago's maritime history and the preservation of artefacts and archives

De Martino painting of Stanley

The UK charity that acquires and sends Falklands heritage items to the archipelago has launched a new website after securing more than 40 objects, documents and books for Stanley's historical institutions over the past decade.

The Friends of the Falkland Islands Museum and the Jane Cameron National Archives, known as FIMA Friends, has been a registered charity in the United Kingdom since July 2016 and directs its funds to research into the archipelago's maritime history and the preservation of artefacts and archives. Its acquisitions, obtained through auctions, direct purchases and donations, go to the Historic Dockyard Museum, the Jane Cameron National Archives and the library in Stanley. The most recent is an original oil painting depicting the action in San Carlos Water during the 1982 war. The website is fimafriends.co.uk

“We have spent over £60,000 in the last 14 years, contributing to historically important collections and helping the institutions share them with the public,” said the charity's chair, Graham Bound, who founded Penguin News in 1979, the only newspaper produced in the archipelago. “We have ensured that many valuable items are now where they belong: in the Falkland Islands.”

Among the items returned is the first known image of Stanley, a painting of the town shortly after its founding by the Italian artist Edoardo De Martino, whose works are also held in the Royal Collection in London. The charity also located and purchased the memorabilia of Louis Baillon, the only islander to win an Olympic gold medal, as a member of England's hockey team at the 1908 London Games.

Secretary and trustee Karen Clapp, who led the website's development, said it will be the charity's principal means of recruiting supporters. “It is important to have a digital footprint that allows people to see what we do and, just as importantly, join us with just a few clicks of a button,” she said, adding that trustees will be more easily contactable, particularly by anyone who learns of an item of historical value to the archipelago.

The site also carries details of forthcoming online talks and access to recordings of past lectures on the region's history. The charity has additionally funded exhibitions, publications, training and specialist equipment for the museum and archives.

World.title: Replica of the flag shown by Argentina's football team unfurled at Darwin cemetery
World.content:
Replica of the flag shown by Argentina's football team unfurled at Darwin cemetery

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 10:55 UTC Full article

The delegation spent a week in the islands and visited Stanley, the Darwin cemetery and various sites of the 1982 fighting

A group of Argentine veterans of the 1982 war and relatives of fallen soldiers unfurled at the Darwin cemetery in the Falklands a flag bearing the inscription “The Malvinas are Argentine”, a design the Argentine press describes as a reproduction of the one displayed by Argentina's national football team after defeating England at the 2026 World Cup. It is the first time the emblem has been displayed in the archipelago.

The delegation spent a week in the islands and visited Stanley, the Darwin cemetery and various sites of the 1982 fighting. The two Argentine outlets that covered the trip differ on its composition: one describes a group of eleven veterans and relatives from the Agrupación 2 de Abril, based in Avellaneda, while the other mentions participants from La Matanza, La Plata and Córdoba. For several of them it was the first time they had set foot in the archipelago since the conflict. During the tribute they sang the national anthem before the graves and left letters, flowers, football shirts and rosaries.

The Darwin cemetery holds 230 graves. Of these, 121 plots contained 122 unidentified bodies, marked with the inscription “Argentine soldier known only to God”. In December 2016, Argentina and the United Kingdom tasked the International Committee of the Red Cross, together with the Argentine Forensic Anthropology Team, with identifying them. Exhumations took place between June and August 2017, and the first report, in December that year, identified 88 bodies; the plaques were installed in March 2018. As of April 2025, 117 had been identified and five remained outstanding.

Among the relatives travelling was Gramisci, sister of Donato, killed in combat days before Argentina's surrender and whose remains were identified in 2018. “I think this is his place. Even though he is far from his family, far from what was his home, it is the place where he, without choosing it, chose to be,” she said. Argentina rejected repatriations at the time, arguing the soldiers were already buried on its own territory, which has made the cemetery a recurring destination for family visits over the past two decades.

Ramón Robles, who leads the group and fought near the cemetery's present location, described the trip as “humanitarian, to close chapters”. He said he applies for a new passport after each visit so as not to retain the stamp of the archipelago's authorities, which he regards as recognition of British administration. According to EFE's coverage, members of the group agreed in dismissing President Javier Milei's recent sovereignty measures as inconsequential; that assessment appears as the reporter's summary rather than a quote attributed to any individual.

The 1982 war left 649 Argentine dead, 255 British and three residents of the archipelago.

World.title: UK public debt nears £3 trillion, equivalent to 93.8% of GDP
World.content:
UK public debt nears £3 trillion, equivalent to 93.8% of GDP

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 10:40 UTC Full article

The figure is £78.5 billion higher than a year earlier, though its weight on the economy was 1.3 percentage points lower than in August 2025, reflecting a growing nominal GDP

The United Kingdom's public sector net debt reached £2,985.5 billion — close to £3 trillion, some US$4 trillion — at the end of August, equivalent to 93.8% of gross domestic product, according to figures published on Tuesday by the Office for National Statistics. The agency noted these are levels last seen in the early 1960s.

The figure is £78.5 billion higher than a year earlier, though its weight on the economy was 1.3 percentage points lower than in August 2025, reflecting a growing nominal GDP.

From the start of the financial year in April through August, the public sector borrowed £77.3 billion, 2.7% less than in the same period last year, but £8.1 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility's forecast. That gap widened sharply: a month earlier it stood at £2.3 billion. The comparison comes five weeks before the UK budget, due on October 28.

In August alone, borrowing reached £18.3 billion, 19% more than a year earlier and £3.5 billion above the OBR's estimate. According to the ONS, the increase occurred because spending grew faster than revenue from taxes and other sources, partly because of inflation.

The government also paid £8.8 billion in debt interest in August, the highest figure on record for that month. Of that total, some £2.1 billion reflects the capital uplift on index-linked gilts, whose return moves with the Retail Prices Index, a mechanism that adds volatility to interest costs.

Not all indicators point the same way. Borrowing in the financial year to August equates to 2.5% of GDP, 0.2 percentage points lower than a year earlier, and is the tenth-lowest April to August period since comparable monthly records began in 1993.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds reaffirmed the Labour government's commitment to “maintaining fiscal discipline” while pursuing economic growth.

The figures frame the public spending debate running through Westminster. On September 9, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the House of Commons his government would meet NATO's target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035, with an interim 3% goal, while Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch questioned the cost of the Chagos Islands agreement and argued a decade was too long to wait.

World.title: De la Espriella skips the UN and delegates Colombia's address to his vice president
World.content:
De la Espriella skips the UN and delegates Colombia's address to his vice president

22nd Tuesday, September 2026 - 10:30 UTC Full article

“You know I promised not to leave Colombia and I am going to keep that,” the president said in a video

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella will not attend the United Nations General Assembly and has delegated the country's address to his vice president, José Manuel Restrepo, scheduled for Thursday afternoon, September 24. It is the first time in recent history that a Colombian vice president has taken on that role.

The decision stems from a campaign pledge. “You know I promised not to leave Colombia and I am going to keep that,” the president said in a video released on Friday, adding that Restrepo “will read before the UN plenary words that will surely make a great impact”. Opposition congressman Alejandro Ocampo said on X that this is the first vice president to deliver Colombia's address to the body since 1946, a claim that has not been independently confirmed.

Security will be the central theme, as agreed by the president and vice president at a meeting in Barranquilla, with the presentation of the new government's national security strategy. The foreign ministry also flagged investment and “strategic alliances” as priorities. Restrepo will speak immediately before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The vice president arrived in New York on Sunday leading a delegation markedly smaller than those of previous governments, comprising Foreign Minister Ómar Bula, UN Ambassador Mauricio Gaona and Ambassador to Washington María Consuelo Araújo. He travelled on a commercial flight, in economy class and in a middle seat, according to a photograph he circulated himself. On Monday he held meetings with the World Economic Forum, the Inter-American Development Bank, energy sector executives and Dominican President Luis Abinader. “We have a clear agenda: attract investment, train the talent artificial intelligence demands and modernise the state,” he said.

Lists of planned meetings differ by source. Ambassador Gaona mentioned the United States, United Kingdom, France, Peru, United Arab Emirates, Chile and Ecuador; other coverage adds Saudi Arabia, Estonia and Switzerland, and explicitly includes strengthening ties with Israel. US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau welcomed him on X.

De la Espriella, in office since August 7, has softened his position on the organisation. During the campaign he called it “a political directorate of the left” and threatened to withdraw Colombia's delegation. Once in government, Bula confirmed before Congress that Colombia will remain on the Security Council, to which it was elected in 2025 and where its term runs to December 2027.

The new government's foreign policy has aligned with the United States and Israel. Last week, Colombia was one of four countries to abstain in the vote allowing Palestine to address the assembly remotely, after Washington denied visas to its representatives: 152 countries voted in favour, with the United States, Israel and Paraguay against. Washington last week kept Colombia on its list of countries it deems to have failed demonstrably to combat drug trafficking, though with explicit praise for the new president.

Last year's address, the final one by then president Gustavo Petro, led to the revocation of his US visa and his subsequent inclusion on the OFAC sanctions list. Petro referred to the episode on X on Monday: “Now that I will no longer give a speech at the United Nations Assembly, the last one put me on OFAC.”

World.title: JD Sports, the British sportswear giant, is bringing its brand to Mexico next year
World.content:
British sportswear retailer JD Sports is poised to expand into Mexico next year after negotiating a long-term franchise with Mexican fashion retailer Grupo Axo, betting on high demand from the country’s growing young population.

Under the agreement, Axo will operate JD stores and e-commerce in Mexico, managing the JD brand and intellectual property, while both companies will leverage JD’s own brand and unique product portfolio in footwear, clothing and accessories.

Axo, described by Fashion Network as “Mexico’s leading omnichannel multi-brand retailer,” will operate more than 140 of JD’s locations through existing Axo sneaker stores.

Betting on strong demand from Mexico’s growing young population, JD also plans to expand stores in key locations over time.

“This initiative represents another significant step in the ongoing execution of the group’s ‘JD Brand First’ strategy to enter one of the world’s most dynamic and youthful consumer markets,” JD said in a statement.

Axo will also leverage JD’s portfolio of private-label and exclusive products “to offer a differentiated proposition to Mexican consumers in the footwear, apparel and accessories categories.”

In the statement, JD noted that Mexico’s population of over 130 million — roughly 40% of whom are under 25 — has a sportswear market valued at around US $6.5 billion, a market that is projected to grow to over US $10 billion by 2034.

“Mexico is a market with a large and highly engaged consumer base, and a demographic profile that closely aligns with JD’s unique position as a trendsetter in footwear and apparel across the sports, music and fashion sectors,” JD said.

JD CEO Régis Schultz described the agreement as “an exciting milestone,” adding that “our position at the intersection of sports, music and fashion will deepen our connection with consumers.”

Schultz described Axo as “an ideal partner,” touting its “30-year track record of working with brands [in Mexico],” its deep market knowledge and robust operating platform.

Axo President and CEO Andrés Gómez highlighted JD’s brand relationships, differentiated product catalog and immersive retail experience as elements that will be incorporated into Axo’s commercial capabilities.

“This collaboration represents a significant moment for sportswear in Mexico,” he said.

For the Mexican consumer, the arrival introduces another major competitor in a category already dominated by flagship stores of large brands (such as Nike and Adidas), specialty chains (such as Grupo Martí and Innvictus), department stores and marketplaces.

With reports from Reuters, Forbes México, Informa BTL and Fashion Network

World.title: At UN, Trump singles out Mexico, likening cartels to ISIS
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that Mexico is the “epicenter” of cartel violence and “must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity.”

During a lengthy address at the U.N. General Assembly Building in New York City, Trump described drug cartels as “the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere” before labeling Mexico as “the epicenter of the cartel violence, unfortunately.”

🇺🇳🇺🇸 Donald #Trump aseguró que 🇲🇽 #México es el epicentro de la violencia de los cárteles de la droga a quienes debe quitarle el control de su territorio, esto en su discurso ante la Asamblea General de la #ONU en Nueva York. “Lamentablemente, México es el epicentro de la… pic.twitter.com/eKhqP9yPpL — La Jornada (@lajornadaonline) September 22, 2026

“It’s unacceptable for the United States to share a 2,000-mile border with a territory controlled by enemy cartels. So Mexico must reclaim control of its soil from the enemies of humanity,” he told his fellow world leaders and other officials, including Mexican Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco.

Trump subsequently declared that “freedom will be coming to Cuba and safety and security will be coming to Mexico.”

He didn’t specify how “safety and security” would be achieved in Mexico, but he has previously demonstrated his eagerness to combat Mexican cartels with U.S. force on Mexican soil. President Claudia Sheinbaum is vehemently opposed to any kind of U.S. intervention in Mexico, and has firmly denounced what she sees as U.S. interference in Mexican affairs.

Despite bilateral tensions related to security and trade, Trump spoke glowingly about the Mexico-U.S. relationship in his U.N. address.

“I’m very proud to tell you we have a very good relationship with the Mexican government. We’ve made great strides — very great strides — with Mexico,” he said, apparently referring to security cooperation.

“They don’t want the cartels either. And when that day comes, this entire region will be a better, safer and more beautiful place in which to live and thrive.”

Trump delivered his speech in New York a week after he submitted a “presidential declaration” to the U.S. Congress in which he said that “Mexico must take additional action” against drug cartels “that dominate vast areas of its territory,” and arrest “the many corrupt public officials” who have colluded with them.

In response, Sheinbaum said that Mexico doesn’t need to be judged “from the outside” and questioned the United States efforts to combat drug use and the illicit southward flow of weapons.

Trump: Cartels are ‘enemies at war with civilization’

Before turning his focus specifically to Mexico, Trump spoke about cartel activity in the Western Hemisphere.

“For decades, other administrations allowed much of this region to be dominated by vicious gangs and bloodthirsty drug cartels, destabilized by uncontrolled migration and infiltrated by hostile foreign adversaries — foreign, sick, demented adversaries,” he said.

“But not anymore. We are reasserting American power, including American military power, where necessary, in our region and around the world to create a safer future for all of us. It’s happening and it’s happening quickly,” Trump said.

The U.S. president noted that his administration has designated various drug cartels — including eight Mexican ones — as foreign terrorist organizations, and “unleashed the United States Armed Forces to eliminate them.”

“The cartels are the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere — not good people. They’re enemies at war with civilization, using murder, rape, torture and extortion as instruments of terror. Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release, which is what we’re doing,” Trump said.

“To that end, the United States has carried out dozens of strikes on cartel drug boats, destroying 97% of the drugs coming into the [U.S. via the] ocean and sea. You’ve seen it. They disappear very quickly, and we’re down 90%. They’re down 97%. Nobody thought that was possible. It was a big source of delivery,” he said.

According to the International Drug Policy Consortium, on Sept. 2, a group of U.N. experts demanded an end to unlawful killings by U.S. forces, after at least 223 deaths at sea were recorded from U.S. air strikes in the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean over the past year.

“These systematic killings gravely violate the fundamental obligation to respect the right to life,” the experts said.

“International law does not permit governments to simply murder alleged criminals at sea, just as the police cannot summarily execute people on the street in United States territory.”

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Ensenada fishermen make an unusual catch: A US military torpedo
World.content:
A U.S. Navy torpedo lost during a training exercise off Southern California drifted into Mexican waters and was recovered near Ensenada before being returned to U.S. authorities, Mexico’s Navy said.

The device was a nonexplosive MK 54 REXTORP practice torpedo designed for training launches from aircraft or ships, the Mexican Navy said in a Monday press release detailing the recovery and return.

🚨 #BajaCalifornia | Un torpedo apareció a la deriva frente a las costas de #Ensenada y fueron pescadores quienes alertaron a la Marina. El artefacto fue localizado a 42.7 kilómetros al suroeste del puerto. La @SEMAR_mx confirmó que se trata de un torpedo de prácticas, utilizado… pic.twitter.com/PxTZ1ToGgo — Michelle Rivera (@michelleriveraa) September 17, 2026

The device was lost by U.S. Navy personnel on Sept. 2 and spotted adrift two weeks later by fishermen roughly 20 nautical miles southwest of Ensenada, Baja California, the Mexican Navy said.

The fishermen’s report of an object with ballistic characteristics prompted the Mexican Navy’s Ensenada Search, Rescue and Maritime Surveillance Station to send a small boat to investigate.

Naval personnel recovered the device last week and secured it at the Second Naval Zone’s facilities, noting that it posed no danger to navigation or the maritime community.

According to information provided by the U.S. Defense Attaché, the device belonged to the U.S. Navy and was lost about 18 nautical miles west of San Clemente Island during the Sept. 2 training exercise.

Mexico’s Navy said poor weather hampered the search and the battery for the torpedo’s location system later expired.

After U.S. authorities confirmed the device was theirs, the commander of Mexico’s Second Naval Zone handed it over to personnel from the U.S. Naval Attaché in Mexico for transfer to U.S. authorities.

The fishermen initially believed the object might be floating seaweed, according to ABC Noticias.

“We thought it was sargassum. We said: Let’s go fish for dorado,” one fisherman said.

In Mexico, mahi-mahi is commonly called dorado.

With reports from El Financiero, ABC Noticias and Tiempo

World.title: CDMX, Querétaro and Nuevo León lead as Mexico’s most competitive states for business, IMCO finds
World.content:
Listen to this article

Mexico City remains Mexico’s most competitive state for business, while Querétaro — the country’s data center hub — ranks second, according to an analysis by a Mexican think tank.

The Mexican Institute for Competitiveness (IMCO) published its 2026 State Competitiveness Index (ICE) on Monday.

According to IMCO, the ICE “measures the ability of the country’s states to generate, attract, and retain talent and investment.”

“A competitive state is one that makes efficient use of its capabilities to foster a favorable environment that contributes to improving its development and, consequently, the well-being of its inhabitants,” the think tank said in its index report.

The 2026 ICE — the 20th edition of the annual index — ranks all 32 federal entities based on their performance across 53 different indicators in six categories called “sub-indexes.”

The sub-indexes are innovation and economy; infrastructure; labor market; society and environment; law (which includes crime rates and citizens’ security perceptions); and political system and governments.

Mexico City ranks first in three of those sub-indexes — innovation and economy; infrastructure; and society and environment — and comes out on top overall for a 20th consecutive year.

Querétaro, which ranks first in the “political system and governments” sub-index, moved up four positions compared to 2025 to become Mexico’s second most competitive state.

Mexico City and Querétaro are the only two entities deemed to have a “very high” level of competitiveness.

The next three most-competitive states, each of which was found to have a “high” level of competitiveness, are Nuevo León, Coahuila and Baja California Sur. Nuevo León’s position didn’t change compared to last year, while Coahuila moved up three spots to become Mexico’s fourth most competitive state. Baja California Sur fell three spots in the ranking to fifth from second a year earlier.

On the other end of the scale, Guerrero is Mexico’s least competitive state, according to IMCO. The southern state fell one spot in the rankings to 32nd in 2026. IMCO said that “economic, labor, institutional and security shortcomings” limit the state’s capacity to attract investment and retain talent.

Oaxaca ranks as the second least competitive state while Michoacán is the third least competitive.

Guerrero and Oaxaca have “very low” levels of competitiveness, according to IMCO, while Michoacán’s level is “low.”

Chiapas, deemed Mexico’s least competitive state in 2025, rose five places in the rankings to 27th this year. Along with 10 other states, it has a “medium low” level of competitiveness, according to IMCO.

What makes CDMX Mexico’s most competitive state?

As mentioned above, Mexico City ranks first in three of the six ICE sub-indexes.

The capital ranks second in the “labor market” sub-index; fifth in the “political systems and governments” sub-index; and 28th in the “law” one.

In its index report, IMCO wrote that Mexico City “remains the top-ranked entity in the 2026 ICE 2026 by combining economic scale, talent, innovation, financial infrastructure, and fiscal capacity.”

The think tank said that 925 economic sectors operate in Mexico City and that 47.1% of the population has a higher education qualification. It also said that per capita GDP in Mexico — at 545,000 pesos (about US $31,500) per year — is 4.7 times higher than that of Guerrero.

Many large Mexican and foreign corporations have offices in Mexico City, while the main campus of Mexico’s most prestigious university, UNAM, is located in the capital. In addition, the federal government and most of its agencies and departments are based in Mexico City, as are some of the nation’s leading healthcare facilities.

This helps Mexico City attract highly educated workers from around the country and abroad.

Still, Mexico City’s competitiveness faces “concrete challenges,” according to IMCO.

“Only 23.7% of the adult population feel safe and 88.9% perceive frequent corruption in the state government,” IMCO said, referring to the administration led by Mayor Clara Brugada.

“To maintain its leadership in an environment of geo-economic competition, the capital must translate its economic and fiscal sophistication into greater certainty, security, and productive linkages with national and international value chains,” the think tank said.

Querétaro, which has received billions of dollars in data center investment in recent years, ranks in the top 10 in all six ICE sub-indexes. As noted above, the state ranks first in the “political system and governments” sub-index, scoring particularly well on the “state debt” and “corruption perception” indicators. Querétaro ranks second among Mexico’s 32 federal entities in the infrastructure sub-index.

Así se ve el ranking del Índice de Competitividad Estatal #ICE2026🏆. En esta edición, la Ciudad de México se mantiene en el primer lugar, Querétaro asciende cuatro posiciones🚀 hasta quedar en el segundo y Nuevo León permanece en tercero. El ranking también muestra cambios… pic.twitter.com/lm0wF1wokj — IMCO (@imcomx) September 21, 2026

10 states recognized for their ‘competitive performance’ over 2 decades

At the presentation of the 2026 ICE in Mexico City on Monday, IMCO director Valeria Moy and other representatives of the think tank recognized 10 states for the “competitive performance” and “strengths” they have maintained over the past 20 years.

Those states are Aguascalientes, Baja California, Baja California Sur, Chihuahua, Mexico City, Coahuila, Jalisco, Nuevo León, Querétaro and Sonora.

IMCO highlighted the strengths of each of those states in a statement.

Aguascalientes (8th in this year’s ICE) was lauded for its “strong integration” with North American supply chains and for the “significant progress” it has made in exports and the attraction of investment.

Baja California (17th in this year’s ICE) was praised for its “strong integration” with the global economy and its “sustained” strong performance in exports and attracting foreign investment.

Baja California Sur (5th in this year’s ICE) was described as having a tourism-driven economy with a strong ability to attract investment, “relatively high wages” and “low levels” of employment informality.

Chihuahua (15th in this year’s ICE) was singled out as Mexico’s “exports leader” during a period of 20 years.

Mexico City (1st in this year’s ICE) was described as the country’s leader in talent and higher education over the past 20 years. The capital was also said to be Mexico’s “most efficient economy in electricity use.”

Coahuila (4th in this year’s ICE) was lauded for being an “export powerhouse” in the automotive sector.

Jalisco (6th in this year’s ICE) was described as having a “diversified economy” with a “capacity for innovation.” The state was also praised for fostering the growth of medium and large companies.

Nuevo León (3rd in this year’s ICE) was lauded for its “highly trained talent” and “low” levels of employment informality. The northern state was also described as a leader in “innovation sectors.”

Querétaro (2nd in this year’s ICE) was praised for its “dynamism” in the automotive, aerospace and data center industries. It was also recognized for its “high level of economic complexity” in the past five years.

Sonora (12th in this year’s ICE) was described as a state with an “industrial economy with a highly educated workforce.” The northern state, which is also known for its high-quality beef, was praised for its “sustained” strong performance in GDP per capita and exports.

Moy: Water and energy are crucial to competitiveness

At Monday’s Mexico City event, Moy said that adequate access to water and energy is decisive to competitiveness in Mexico.

She said that each of the country’s states requires federal government support to ensure they have adequate quantities of the vital resources.

“We’re going to need electricity and water, and we know that these depend largely on the federal government —we’re very clear on that. The states won’t be able to manage on their own,” the IMCO director said.

“We urgently need a much more productive dialogue in order to have more electricity, [greater] supply and competitive prices. Otherwise, there will be no way to compete with the southern border of the United States,” Moy said.

With reports from El Economista and Reforma

World.title: Southwest residents on alert as ‘dangerous’ Hurricane Polo moves up Mexico’s Pacific coast
World.content:
Residents of the states of Guerrero and Michoacán remain on alert Tuesday as Hurricane Polo, a Category 5 hurricane, moves slowly along the Pacific coast and is forecast to bring heavy rain to southwestern Mexico.

At 9 a.m. Tuesday, the U.S. National Hurricane Center described Polo as ‘extremely dangerous’ with maximum sustained winds of 165 mph (270 km/h). It was moving slowly north at 2 mph, located about 200 miles (330 kilometers) south of Zihuatanejo, Guerrero.

Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km).

The storm had been moving east slowly toward the coast, but had begun to turn northwest and is forecast to continue west-northwest, moving away from land by Wednesday night.

Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 165 mph (270 km/h) with gusts reaching 195 mph (315 km/h). Additional strengthening is likely through Tuesday, with fluctuations possible throughout Wednesday.

Authorities have suspended classes in Guerrero and Michoacán and schools will remain closed through Wednesday. The Navy has restricted navigation in several ports as authorities continue to monitor the storm’s development.

Polo is expected to dump up to 6 inches of rain across coastal portions of Guerrero and Michoacán through Thursday. The National Water Commission has warned of potential landslides, overflowing rivers and streams, flooding and waves of up to 4 meters (13 feet) in Michoacán and Guerrero.

Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima and Jalisco through Thursday.

A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for the Pacific coast from Tecpan de Galeana, Guerrero, north to Punta San Telmo, Michoacán. At the same time, the Tropical Storm Watch that has been in effect north of Michoacán was extended westward to Playa Perula, Jalisco.

A Tropical Storm Warning signifies that tropical storm conditions are expected within 36 hours, whereas a Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are possible within 48 hours.

The governments of Michoacán and Guerrero have issued warnings encouraging residents — especially those living near the coast — to adhere to recommendations by Civil Protection authorities and take precautions to secure their homes against heavy winds.

Guerrero has established a Civil Protection center in Zihuatanejo to coordinate emergency response and mitigate risks.

With reports from El País, The Associated Press and NBC News

World.title: SENER: Wind power expected to grow 80% by 2030
World.content:
Mexico is doubling down on its renewable energy ambitions, with wind energy generation expected to increase 80% by 2030 to reach 15 gigawatts, the Energy Ministry (SENER) reported in September.

Mexico is expected to increase its renewable energy generation from 24.6% of its total portfolio in 2025 to over 38% in 2030, said Jorge Islas Samperio, SENER’s Deputy Minister of Planning and Energy Transition, at a forum of the Mexican Wind Energy Association (AMDEE) and the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC) earlier this month. He said renewable sources will account for more than 74% of new capacity additions, including solar, wind and hydroelectric power.

The SENER plan includes 6.86 gigawatts of capacity additions, of which 4.7 gigawatts have already been allocated to 17 wind farms.

At the same Sept. 10 forum, CFE announced the awarding of eight wind energy projects under mixed-ownership schemes, with a total capacity of 2.9 gigawatts.

The projects, which include 890 megawatts of battery storage, are expected to be operational in Nuevo León and Tamaulipas by 2030, supplying clean power to the industrial hubs of northeastern Mexico.

Energy Minister Luz Elena González previously presented the government’s plan to add almost 32.5 gigawatts of generation capacity to the national grid by 2030, with around 22 gigawatts — roughly 70% — coming from renewable sources, predominantly solar (55%) and wind (30%). González said that total investment across CFE, joint ventures, and private projects was expected to reach 739 billion pesos (US$ 41.9 billion).

In the September forum, Samperio highlighted opportunities for Mexico to develop across the wind energy value chain, including parts manufacturing and construction, and operation of wind farms.

The deputy minister said that expanding Mexico’s renewable energy capacity would be key to meeting growing electricity demand, supporting industrial development and achieving the country’s energy transition goals.

Meanwhile, AMDEE President Gerardo Pérez Guerra acknowledged that legal certainty, public-private collaboration and the expansion of transmission networks are needed to encourage new investments in infrastructure and storage.

With reports from La Jornada

World.title: MND Local San Miguel de Allende: Art passport, charity events and celebrity sightings
World.content:
A new passport guide focuses on the city’s lesser-known artists and art studios; a cow-sorting benefit event is coming up; an athletic challenge will help feed local schoolchildren, and a celebrity sighting is reported at a local bar and restaurant. Read on about some of the community activities going on in and around San Miguel de Allende.

Art passport draws attention to SMA’s ‘hidden studios’

San Miguel jewelry maker Mariana Díaz started thinking about her Hidden Studios Art Passport project in January after a period of feeling invisible as an artist and realizing others were in a similar situation.

“I just thought about everybody having so much talent, but no one knows about it,” she said. “People keep on the same route in Centro, and they really don’t walk around and see all the good stuff that’s out there.”

Her idea led to a Sept. 12 launch of the initial project, which included 14 local artists plus members of the public who can use her printed passport guide to find artists, studios and creative spaces around the city and collect stamps for each one they visit.

“The event was great,” Díaz said. “There were 70 people there. It was wonderful to see everybody. My family was there, all the artists were there and they brought a little piece of themselves — a sample of their art, a painting or a sculpture or something.”

How it works

Artists pay her a fee to participate and send in pictures of their work to be put in the passport guide. She then gives them stamps that she designed to hand out to people who visit their studios. It works like a treasure hunt and can be done year-round, she said.

Since the art passport project just started, Díaz is currently highlighting the opportunity for participation for artists and local businesses such as hotels, cafes and restaurants.

“There are two options that help,” she said. “People can carry the passport in their restaurant or cafe or appear in the guide or put their business in the guide.”

Seven artists have already signed up for the second edition of the passport, she noted, and more hotels and other businesses may join in.

“There are some big names interested, and I feel it could become really big at some point,” Díaz said. “I’m waiting to have the guide with me and go deliver it everywhere. The majority are really interested in it. It’s something for their guests to do.”

For more information, she can be reached on Instagram, Facebook or WhatsApp.

Upcoming cow-sorting event will benefit local NGO

The Billy Boots Cup cow-sorting event will be held Saturday, Oct. 10, at Rancho Sol Dorado, a 120-acre private ranch community and club about 6 miles north of San Miguel at Km 5.5, Marroquín de Abajo. Doors open at 10 a.m., and the action starts at 11 a.m. Admission is free.

Cow sorting (also known as ranch sorting) involves teams of riders separating numbered cows from a herd and putting them in pens in numerical order within specific time limits. The event will benefit Feed the Hungry San Miguel, a nonprofit organization that distributes meals to local schoolchildren.

Besides the equestrian action, there will be food and drinks, a raffle and 20 local vendors on hand.

Walk, Run, Bike challenge to help feed local schoolchildren

Feed the Hungry San Miguel will hold its seventh Walk, Run, Bike for Food Challenge on Sunday, Oct. 25, from 8:30 a.m. to noon to benefit its food and nutrition programs. The goal is to provide more than 5,000 nutritious school lunches every day to local and rural communities.

The nonprofit organization, formed in 1984, invites participants to sign up now to walk, run or bike through the Viñedo Dos Búhos countryside east of San Miguel and stay afterward for live music, food and community spirit.

Another benefit for Feed the Hungry San Miguel is coming Sunday, Nov. 15. The annual Fashion Feeds runway brunch is scheduled from noon to 3 p.m. at Live Aqua, located at Calzada de la Presa 85 in Centro.

Another celebrity sighting reported

Spotting famous people in and around San Miguel isn’t uncommon to anyone who spends time out and about. Diego Luna, Karol G, Lorde and Bill Murray have recently been seen in the city, along with others who likely slipped in and out without being recognized.

The most recent celebrity sighting was Sept. 18, when Canadian actor and musician Ryan Gosling was spotted enjoying the ambiance at Sala de Despecho at Umarán 14 in El Centro. The venue offers a bar, restaurant and karaoke featuring Spanish-language “pop and heartbreak ballads.” No word yet on whether he joined in.

Gosling is known for his breakout role in “The Notebook” (2004), followed by starring roles in “La La Land” (2016) and “Barbie” (2023), among others. His latest project, “Star Wars: Starfighter,” has reportedly finished filming and is in post-production, with release scheduled for May 2027.

Cathy Siegner is an independent journalist based in San Miguel and Montana. She has journalism degrees from the University of Oregon and Northwestern University.

World.title: Guanajuato has drawn US $630 million in data center investment as it evolves toward being a tech powerhouse
World.content:
Guanajuato is expanding its footprint in the digital economy with a portfolio of data centers that has drawn a combined investment of US $630 million and the creation of 200 jobs, as reported in a state government statement.

The Bajío state has currently two operational facilities and another in development, two of which belong to ODATA, a member of the Aligned Data Centers group located in San Miguel de Allende and Apaseo el Grande.

Centros de datos impulsan inversión y empleo tecnológico estatal

Guanajuato reporta 2 centros de datos en operación y uno en desarrollo, con inversión conjunta de 630 mdd y 200 empleos directos. Proyectos exigen energía, conectividad, seguridad y talento especializado.… pic.twitter.com/mCxUopjYFZ — Red Popular (@RedPopularMx) September 21, 2026

The third project is still under construction, also in San Miguel de Allende.

The development of these projects required a new substation at the San Miguel de Allende Business Park (PESMA)—featuring a 60 MVA capacity and an investment exceeding US $45 million— to ensure sufficient and reliable energy for new technological and industrial operations.

This electrical infrastructure is complemented by the Bajío region’s central location and by new investments in fiber-optic connectivity.

According to authorities, the data centers established in Guanajuato incorporate energy and water-efficiency technologies, including state-of-the-art cooling systems and reuse of treated water.

State Economy Minister Cristina Villaseñor explained that the inclusion of information technologies — including data centers, artificial intelligence, and semiconductors — is one of the strategic sectors within the Guanajuato Suma strategy, whose central objective is to evolve the economy from a traditional industrial base into a technological powerhouse.

According to the state government, Guanajuato has drawn over US $6.5 billion in investment — equivalent to 81.9% of the six-year target of $8 billion — across various sectors, including digital infrastructure and data centers.

Villaseñor explained that this strategy responds to changes in the global economy driven by the reconfiguration of supply chains and the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). In this context, the state’s vision is to boost digital infrastructure growth while protecting the region’s natural resources.

This vision dovetails with President Claudia Sheinbaum’s policy y regarding the technology industry.

Although she has said that Mexico needs data centers to develop AI and modernize its technological capabilities, she has warned that the country must not become a global hub for data storage and processing to meet external demand, given the high energy and water consumption involved.

World.title: Bringing Your Pet to Costa Rica: SENASA Rules, Vets and Costs
World.content:
Guides · Costa Rica

Key Facts The country — Costa Rica is a Central American republic of about five million people, and its animal health service, SENASA, decides which pets may enter. SENASA publishes its requirements free of charge, in Spanish and English, on its own website.

— Costa Rica is a Central American republic of about five million people, and its animal health service, SENASA, decides which pets may enter. SENASA publishes its requirements free of charge, in Spanish and English, on its own website. The rules — two requirement sheets govern dogs and cats. IN-006, version 11, covers every country of origin. IN-007, version 09, covers the United States and adds a federal endorsement step. Both have been in force since 19 July 2024, and SENASA warns that they may change without notice.

What matters now — search results on this subject are dominated by pet-shipper marketing pages that contradict the SENASA text on the titre test, the rabies waiting period, the certificate window and the microchip.

What happened — this guide sets out what the two sheets actually say, as read in full on 23 September 2026, and marks every point that could not be confirmed.

The numbers — the clinical examination must fall within 14 days of departure and the parasite treatment within 15 days. The import permit costs ¢10,653 (about US$23.67) under SENASA’s 2026 tariff. Copa Airlines charges US$125 for a pet in the cabin.

Copa Airlines charges US$125 for a pet in the cabin. What it means for you — if the animal flies with you in the cabin or as checked baggage, you present only the health certificate at the border inspection post. No import permit, no customs broker, no routine quarantine.

— if the animal flies with you in the cabin or as checked baggage, you present only the health certificate at the border inspection post. No import permit, no customs broker, no routine quarantine. Still open — what triggers the ¢100,750 (about US$223.89) supervised home quarantine charge in the tariff, the current federal endorsement fee, and any credible door-to-door cost range from Europe.

Most of what you will read online about this is out of date, and the parts people pay for are the parts Costa Rica does not ask for.

Bringing your pet to Costa Rica is governed by two short documents, and almost everything else you will find online contradicts them. SENASA is the national animal health service, and its sheets are free and bilingual. This guide follows them line by line and says plainly where a figure could not be confirmed. Colón amounts convert at ¢450 (about US$1), the Banco Central reference rate on 22 September 2026.

There is no routine quarantine, so a pet can be on the beach the day it lands.
